techniques.name: Plank and timber geometry: wear built into the shape
techniques.what_it_is: Replace plain boxes by individually different planks, posts and beams with rounded worn edges, bow, cup, twist, chips, end splits, replaced boards, pegs and nail heads, plus a veranda deck with staggered butt joints, a nosing and a lowered plinth so the boards stand clear.
techniques.why_it_matters: The person said the geometry of the planks was very basic. The old planks were boxes: 224 vertices a run, one 3 mm bevel, no warp, no thickness change. Wear that lives only in the texture cannot catch the low sun and does not change the silhouette.
techniques.how_to_do_it: One plank = one rounded-box loft (rings along the length, a profile across: flat top points, 30 and 60 degree arc points, side, underside chamfer), at most 400 vertices, built in numpy in world metres. Per plank random: width 9 to 17 cm (deck 12 to 17), thickness 4.5 to 7 cm, gap 5 to 14 mm, bow up to 6 mm, cup up to 4 mm, twist up to 1.5 degrees, top-edge rounding 6 to 12 mm, 3 mm underside bevel, walking-line dish 1 to 2 mm, a chipped corner on 10 to 15 percent (3 to 6 cm notch), an end check on 15 to 20 percent (a real 2 to 3 mm wedge, 5 to 12 cm long), 6 to 9 percent replaced boards (warmer, small dark nail heads instead of pegs). Write per-vertex attributes for the shader: wear, damp, plank_id, plank_tone, endd (distance to plank end), sided (distance to long edge), and per-plank knot choice. Material slots top, side, end grain. Round pegs 14 mm, 6 to 8 mm proud, domed, lighter end-grain tone (made 1.5 times bigger after the checker could not see them); iron cramps flat 3 x 12 cm; posts 14 cm square with 1.5 cm chamfer and 2 to 3 real V-grooves 2 to 4 mm deep; beams, rafter tails and edges chamfered. Deck: 14 rows, boards 1.2 to 2.4 m with neighbouring joints at least 40 cm apart, 3.5 cm nosing, joists about every 0.9 m with a peg or nail per board per joist, a lighter worn band, a few leaves; lower the plinth strip so board thickness shows (4.5 cm).
techniques.measured_results: Bridge: 49 arm planks plus 2 breakers (fix round 59 including 8 offcuts): width 9.4 to 16.7 cm (std 1.58), thickness 47 to 62.6 mm (std 3.9), gaps 5.7 to 13.8 mm (std 2.2), 97 percent with bow, cup or twist over the limit, max bow 6.0 mm, cup 4.0 mm, twist 1.48 degrees, chipped 16.2, end checks 21.8, replaced 7.8 percent, all planks different, at most 391 vertices a plank, 82 pegs plus 8 nails plus 8 iron cramps (fix: 94 pegs, 5 nail heads). Deck 14 rows, 91 boards 1.196 to 2.396 m, nearest neighbouring joints 60 cm, deck top 0.557 to 0.563 (limit 0.56 +- 0.005 was passed within rounding), nosing 3.5 cm. Triangles for the whole wood stage about 5 thousand net of the fix. Bridge detail energy 5.32 to 5.29 (floor 4.79): the new planks are shape and colour, not busy texture. Stage ran in about 3 to 5 s on the card.
techniques.traps_and_failures: Walking-line hole of 10 cm at the turns and one plank with a single support (fixed); bearer lines placed on dry land; shore footings too thick; 3 mirrored UV faces; first moss covered 17 to 37 percent of planks like green trim on every end; plank detail energy only just above the floor (0.94 times) because the new planks are cleaner on purpose; the outer corner of each mitred turn was left open and showed a dark triangle (fixed with 8 short offcut planks and 4 corner rails, outline overlap 0.869 to 0.919); half-lap joints and bearer notches never modelled (bearer ends overlap posts 2 cm and are pegged); a dark ring round each peg rendered pale like a hat brim (removed); the same two spiral knots were stamped on 10 of 13 planks because one 1 m normal-map tile served every plank (fixed with mirror tile and per-plank knots on about half). The deck stays the most orange, cleanest area at the end.

techniques.name: Roof tile variety, plaster walls, caps, stone chips and cracks (damage as geometry plus a few marks)
techniques.what_it_is: Give roofs, walls, stones and lanterns individual damage that reads as designed: tiles that differ in tone and shape (chipped, slipped, cracked, missing), ridge and eave details, plaster-loss dents, single clean cracks as thin ribbons, chipped cap corners, moss and lichen in a few places, drip stains under the eave.
techniques.why_it_matters: Rows of identical tiles and clean plaster were the 'bland, no character' the person named. Damage as shape catches the low sun; a texture-only crack does not.
techniques.how_to_do_it: Roof (instanced tiles): put a UV on the prototype; keep a table object with one row per tile (variant, tone, slip, moss, lichen, drip) read inside COPIES of the node groups; six tile shapes (whole, corner chip, crack groove plus notch, broken half, cracked in two, missing = dark underlay); keep tile shapes as OBJECT instances (see trap). Pick flawed tiles only among tiles the hero camera really sees (ray cast from the camera to a point just above each tile): 3 to 6 slipped (2 to 5 cm down-slope, 2 to 4 degrees; made 1.5 times bigger), 6 to 12 chipped, 1 to 2 cracked, 1 to 2 missing, a few near the ridge, one the second camera sees from below. Per-tile tone std about 0.02 to 0.06 in luminance. Marks (few, big): moss as soft olive blobs in valleys, on the last eave course and on the ridge, 4 to 10 percent of roof; pale lichen flecks 1 to 3 percent; 6 to 11 dark drip stains under eave ends, longer and wider so they read; ridge course of half-round cap tiles plus two rounded end caps with disc relief; round eave-end discs (14 cm, 3 cm thick, 86 of them). Walls (8-vertex boxes): subdivide the garden face to about 3 cm, cut 2 to 4 plaster-loss patches 1.5 to 2.5 cm deep with irregular outline, 4 to 8 hairline cracks as single tapering dark ribbons lying 2 to 3 mm off the surface (walked over the surface with ray casts every 3 to 4 cm; fix round: fewer, twice as wide 1.2 to 2.4 cm, jagged, not crossing, two starting where the hero looks), a splash band at the base, a low stone footing strip, caps with 3 to 6 chipped corners, blotch colour mixed 40 percent from a plaster swatch. Stones: scoop 1 or 2 chips by pulling a ball of vertices inward with soft falloff and mark the chip with a vertex attribute so the shader paints it paler; one clean crack per few rocks; a darker, smoother wet band up to just above the waterline (z -0.08 when water is -0.12); big soft value blocks (smooth Voronoi cells about 50 cm) so the stone reads as 4 to 6 planes. Lantern: 2 cracks on the post, 1 on the gallery, a chipped cap corner (about 6 cm), small moss pads; do not touch the glow.
techniques.measured_results: Roof: 9 chipped, 5 slipped, 2 cracked, 1 missing (all in the 226 tiles the hero sees), 11 drip stains, 37 ridge cap tiles plus 2 end caps, 86 eave discs, 8 leaves, 15 moss cushions (6 eave, 4 ridge foot, 5 on the cap); coverage on a top-down mask of the south slope: moss 4.9 percent, lichen 1.3, drip 0.6; tone std about 0.043 (computed, not measured on a picture). Walls: cracks 5/5/8 then 4/4/5, loss patches 3/3/4, chipped caps 4/4/5. Detail energy roof box 8.01 to 8.77 (limit 7.2 to 10; final 7.79), wall 3.37 to 3.53 (limit 4.7), rock 3.62 to 3.83 (final 4.59, limit 5.0). Hero final 40 s on a 4090. About 0.15 million triangles added. Lantern glow colour 1.0/0.46/0.14, strength 7.0 unchanged before and after.
techniques.traps_and_failures: The weathering kit read its wk_ numbers from the instanced OBJECT; geometry instances read the Hall roof's numbers, so the first roof version made the eave and ridge mint green (fix: keep Object Info As Instance on). Plaster-loss patches first star-shaped and bright orange, then too round, then flat brown stickers (integration softened them: lighter clay, factor 0.62). Lichen first looked like small white flowers (too many tiny dots). First wall cracks looked like wire or twigs. At 1200 px slipped tiles, drip stains and the glaze craze did not read (the dark eave discs read best); glaze at strength 0.9 looked crumpled and faceted (fix: 3 craze lines not 14, 4 dents not 8, strength 0.55, smooth shading with edges over 40 degrees kept). Mint slivers between eave discs were the roof's timber turned mint by the kit's growth layer. The veranda camera sees only 23 roof tiles, so no flawed tile is visible there. Rock 0 got chips but no crack (ray walk left the top faces). Only 4 of 6 planned lantern moss blobs found a surface. Step 7 (basin stains, soot) was only partly done.

techniques.name: Chunky grass, flowers, leaves, worn paths and a lawn with a story (ground cover)
techniques.what_it_is: Ground cover built from a small set of designed tuft shapes placed in clumps by rules from the scene (rock feet, water edge, kerb, path edge, plinth), small flowers in short lines, big readable fallen leaves, a soft bare-earth worn path from a painted mask, and a mottled lawn colour.
techniques.why_it_matters: Grass was named by the person as bland. The first tufts followed the brief (6 to 9 thin blades 6 to 14 mm wide) and read 'thin and spiky, realistic sedge'; the concept's tufts are chunky. Also: hair-level grass is exactly the photographic noise the style forbids.
techniques.how_to_do_it: Tuft recipe (fix round): 4 to 6 broad folded leaves 3.5 to 9 cm wide (a V channel so the low sun lights one half, two clean planes per leaf), soft tips, lighter vein, darker edges; plump seed heads (six-sided spindle 8 to 12 cm long, 1.5 to 2.2 cm across) on three-sided stalks (flat stalks vanish edge-on and leave heads floating), a nodding pod kind, a broad-leaf kind for rock feet, a dry straw clump, a clover of flat leaf discs, a reddish bent kind. 12 shapes, 16 meshes with tints. Colour is a vertex colour from dark olive base to lighter tip, pulled 45 percent toward its own grey so the warm sun does not turn it fresh green. Placement by the stage with ray casts against the live scene: density per m2 = 0.72 in open lawn plus exponential bumps near rock feet, water edge, kerb, path edge and plinth; clumps of 2 to 5, radius 15 to 35 cm, first tuft biggest (clump hierarchy), scale range at least 3 to 1, tall kinds suppressed near the camera, worn path kept bare, only where a camera sees plus a margin, no tuft where an obstacle sits (World.free). Instance with a small generic geometry-nodes group reading point attributes g6_pick, g6_scale, g6_rot. Flowers: 5-petal, 6.4 to 8 cm heads in four short curved lines (24); twigs 20, dry blades 33, dry leaves 16; red maple stars 36 (five-pointed, 14 to 20 cm, each within 5 mm of the surface by ray cast). Worn path: top-down mask 2048 px (R bare earth, G footfall dish), made as distance to polylines with a slow 15 to 70 cm edge wave and a 0.3 to 1.7 m width wobble so it reads as ONE soft shape (no grass islands, no camouflage), a lighter dusty middle, a damper darker rim, 19 real pebbles 3 to 6 cm. Lawn: two-scale olive and warm-brown mottling that is neutral on average.
techniques.measured_results: Tufts: 16 meshes of 12 shapes, scale 0.44 to 1.58 (3.6:1), seed heads 21.7 to 27.8 percent, 4 tints, 499 to 616 tufts, tuft triangles 1.97 times the old count (limit 2.0), vertices 1.18 times; flowers cover 0.11 percent of the hero and 0.28 of the veranda (limit 0.3); blades base width 6.8 mm (builder) to leaf widths 26 to 91 mm median 45 (fix). Grass-box detail energy 3.58 to 4.39 (limit 3.2 to 5.0); lawn luminance 0.227 to 0.205; lawn hue 50.1 to 46.9 degrees (limit 6); worn path 8.6 percent of the hero lower right and 10.7 of the veranda foreground. Strongly saturated pixels outside the maple 2.6 percent with the first chunky tufts, 1.49 after pulling toward grey (limit 1.0, already 1.45 before). Whole scene triangles +60 thousand (builder), +142 thousand (fix) against a 1.5 million limit.
techniques.traps_and_failures: The multi-input socket of Geometry to Instance evaluates its links in REVERSE order of creation: tuft shape numbers were swapped and seed heads sat on about 4 percent instead of 28 until realised triangles were counted against the stage's own picks (link sources last-first). One round of finals was drawn with the lineup test light still in the scene (everything brighter, sand energy -22 percent): thrown away. Two cameras landed inside a rock or hedge (one black picture): cameras now test line of sight and hedge distance. First ground normal map too strong. Fix-round chunky tufts cost 0.011 (hero) and 0.020 (veranda) of the squint score; turning width, density and mottle down bought back at most 0.009. The checker still found the lawn colour between tufts a smeared, streaky scan that clashes with the chunky tufts; worn path in the hero dark and hard to read; the 44 first-round flowers cover 0.02 percent and cannot be seen; moss domes can read as green gumdrops; far tufts are 1 to 3 pixels wide and read as texture; a lawn wedge still pokes into the path.

techniques.name: Designed moss, mould and wear: where it goes, how it is drawn, and the bean-bag and sticker traps
techniques.what_it_is: Moss, mould, algae, lichen, stains and wear drawn as a few soft rounded designed shapes (a moss patch is one soft rounded shape with a lighter top edge and darker rim, a mould stain a soft dark grey-green blotch) placed where water and shade put them, as caps, cushions, collars and patches.
techniques.why_it_matters: 'No wear, no mold or moss' was the person's complaint. The first pass answered it with numbers that did not hold up in the picture (claimed 9.8 percent moss and mould on planks, measured 0.6 percent olive pixels) and then with stickers and bean bags. Where moss goes is knowledge a small model lacks; how it is drawn decides whether it reads as design or as paint.
techniques.how_to_do_it: Where: at plank ends, at post feet, near rocks and water, in shade, in gaps (thin strips on the side faces), at roof valleys, last eave course and ridge, on the TOP faces of rocks (normal z above 0.7), at rock feet as collars on the land side, at kerb joints and stepping-stone edges; clear the walking line (share on the walking line at most half the average); never on raked gravel or raked area; post feet dark and damp up to the waterline with a green algae band, a rolled algae rim 3 to 5 cm wide 5 mm above water on stones that really touch water (measure which stones touch: of 15 pond-edge stones only 7 plus one rock did). Moss colour from the palette (olive #6a6a2e lit to #2a2d24 shaded; albedo values calibrated on a crop), warmer and yellower in sun, darker and cooler in shade, never a flat sticker. Shader design for patches on planks: a COARSE world-position noise picks 'moss zones' 40 to 60 cm long so a patch runs over two to four neighbouring planks and most ends stay clean; inside a zone strength = zone x proximity (plank-end distance, damp attribute, edge distance) x (1 - walking line); a fine noise makes the edge soft and rounded; a lighter rim from mask x (1 - mask); a debug view switch (moss red, mould green, wear blue) so the share can be counted from a mask picture. Geometry: moss cap on a rock = polar grid of rays (36 spokes, 10 rings) following the top-facing surface, outline an irregular blob 0.15 to 0.4 m radius, 2 to 6 cm thick with rolled edge, vertex attribute g6_rim (0 middle, 1 edge) read by the material for darker rim and lighter ring; cushion = cluster of 4 round lumps with rolled edge (cushion_mesh with any hit function, stretch and angle so it can follow a hip edge or hug a joint). Concept cap rule: ONE soft cap on each of the 5 big rocks and 4 to 6 pond-edge stones. For cushion banks: sizes 0.6 to 1.5 times in three classes, drop cushions that sit inside a bigger one, a third fewer in a dense bank, six dome shapes of which a third plain round with no pinched crease, low moss mats between touching cushions, a different tone on every cushion, collars as rings of small cushions at the foot of at least 6 rocks.
techniques.measured_results: Plank moss, hero mask picture: first version 9.8 percent (claimed; moss 7.7, mould 8.4 overlapping), straight down 13.7, walking line 0.6 and off it 26.5 percent; fix 8.67 moss + 3.29 mould = 11.62 percent, walking line 0.5 versus 21.4 off it, walking line lighter than plank average by +0.049 (target 0.02 to 0.06), average plank brightness 0.425 to 0.377. Green-looking pixels on the left run: original 0.06, first integration 1.7 (checker 0.6 olive), fix 5.0 percent (re-check: 6.6 by its own colour count, which cannot separate moss from greenish wood). Caps: 10 stone moss caps (5 rocks plus 5 pond stones), 15 roof cushions, 7 lantern pads (largest pad 43 percent smaller, cap moss total 39 percent smaller, pixels 27 percent fewer and 21 percent darker), collars on 15 to 16 rocks plus lantern base, 12 cushions along the plinth foot; cushion bank veranda 536 to 354 (about 66 percent), cushions 1,324 plus 633 mats (was 1,988).
techniques.traps_and_failures: Bean bags: near-identical rounded cushions with the same pinched crease, same size, row after row; the fix only partly worked (banks still read as 'a heap of like-shaped green domes' in the re-check); a repeated stamp is the failure whatever the shape. Stickers: the lantern cap moss was one bright yellow-green leaf-shaped blob; the 'neon-green bands and diamond lines' and wavy 'agate' stripes on rocks were NOT the stone colour scans but three weathering-kit layers (foot splash and tide band, wall-crack lines, wall growth); found by drawing the kit chain layer by layer. The kit reads strengths from custom properties wk_* on each object, so the fix multiplied them (foot 0.35, splash 0.40, tide green 0.30, cracks 0.33, algae 0.35, growth 0.75; lantern foot 0.5, algae 0.2, growth 0.45) from remembered original values. After calming the lantern moss was nearly invisible at hero size. Roof cushions went yellow-green in sun (darkened twice). First 'moss as small olive speckles' did not read. A builder's mask-picture percent is not the picture's percent: count in rendered pixels or by eye, and say which. Wood fixer's step-foot moss was hidden by the ground builder's cushions in the combined scene; two cushions between the steps read like bowls.

techniques.name: Construction logic of a structure (the bridge) and a way to prove it
techniques.what_it_is: Build anything that carries weight from the ground up so every visible part has a visible reason: what carries it and what it carries. Then check it with a contact graph and walkability rays instead of trusting a picture.
techniques.why_it_matters: The old bridge floated on four small stone blocks and six thin sticks, plank runs poked through each other at the turns, nothing was fixed to anything. 'Even for an artistic style' it made no sense to the person. The same stack logic applies to cottages (posts on stones, beams on posts, rafters on beams), a stable, a fence, a cart.
techniques.how_to_do_it: Bottom-up stack for the bridge: flat footing stones on the bed (45 to 60 cm, 10 to 14 cm thick; fix: tops 1 to 3 cm above the water so they read), square posts in pairs just outside the planks (about 0.62 m from the centre line; at nodes 10 to 20 cm bollards, mid-arm posts stop 3 to 5 cm below the deck; random out-of-plumb up to 0.8 degree), bearers (cross beams 12 x 10 cm, 1.14 m long, ends set 2 cm into notches and pegged with two pegs), two stringers per arm about 0.42 m either side (8 x 12 cm, third short one before each turn), planks across overhanging the outer stringer 4 to 12 cm, one diagonal breaker board at each turn on the mitre line, arm planks cut to the mitre, no overlap between runs (at least 1 cm), pegs two per plank at the outer stringers (skip about 10 percent), iron cramps across 6 to 10 joints at turns, bank ends on stone sills at z 0.10. supports(): choose as few interior bearer lines as keep every stringer span at most 1.38 m, moving a line along the arm until both posts stand at least 5 cm under water. Measure support with ray casts and 'rest patches' (a part rests on another when at least 16 cm2 of its underside lies within 8 mm of an up-facing face below it). Contracts with neighbours written in the brief: inside 1.2 m of the bridge centre line the pond bed stays within 0.1 m of the starting scene because the footings stand on it.
techniques.measured_results: Builder: 14 footings, 18 posts, 7 bearers, 10 stringers; test 9 connected structure PASS (51 planks each on at least 2 stringers, every stringer on 2 bearers or a sill, 7 bearers each on 2 posts, 18 posts each on a footing or sill, 0 floating, longest support span 1.04 m); test 10 walkability PASS (147 rays every 5 cm, deck top 0.205 to 0.226, biggest step 1.9 cm, steepest slope 1:86, longest miss 5 cm = one gap, width mean 1.048 m). Re-check on the saved fix scene by its own script: 59 planks, 0 with fewer than 2 supports (26 have 2, 19 have 3, 12 have 4, 2 have 6), longest unsupported stretch 0.85 m, all 18 posts on a footing or pier with about 17 dm2 of contact, walk line top 19.9 to 22.5 cm, all 100 pegs have vertices inside wood. Silhouette overlap with the start bridge in the hero: 0.869 (first), 0.919 (fix); by strict IoU in the final comparison 0.769 hero, 0.801 veranda, share of old shape still covered 0.954 and 0.894.
techniques.traps_and_failures: Re-check found what the builders' own tests missed: 6 of 8 iron straps have one nail head hovering 13.7 to 18.3 mm above the lower plank (the flat strap crosses from the thicker breaker to a lower plank; a shadow shows under it); 14 of the small cramp parts are not inside wood; 3 of 12 footing stones (numbers 3, 9, 10) hang 2.5 to 13.5 cm over the bank slope at one edge (hidden); the four corner rails are held only by crossing the long beams; 4 footings sunk 6 to 20 cm into bank slope. Not modelled: half-lap joints, post notches, moss at the step foot. First round: two plank runs overlapped at the turns; the corner left an open triangle. Test 24 (the four stages together in any order) only partly run by builders. The yardstick for silhouette (IoU versus share covered) was never decided: more posts and feet make IoU fall while nothing shrinks.

techniques.name: Water you can see into, pond life, and tree crowns built as layered pads
techniques.what_it_is: A pond that reads (clear shallow edge over a pebble bed, dark deeper middle, ripples, notched lily pads with flowers, iris, floating leaves, algae rim) and trees whose silhouette follows a designed layered crown (maple as 5 to 8 cloud pads with branches visible between; pine as flat discs with brush-stroke needle clumps on a plated trunk).
techniques.why_it_matters: The first full-size check judged the pond element 'no': at 1200 px it still looked like dark water with a few small pads; the maple became darker and heavier. Water and big trees fill a lot of the frame and decide the first impression.
techniques.how_to_do_it: Water: a per-vertex depth attribute on the water mesh drives a colour ramp (depth metres to linear colour): clear to 0.22 m (fix; was 0.10), dark olive-teal only below 0.34 m, never turquoise (hue 160 to 210 with saturation over 0.35 forbidden) or violet; murk: from depth 0.24 to 0.40 mix up to 50 percent of a dark olive diffuse so the middle reads murky, not a black hole; transmission 1, IOR 1.33, roughness 0.03, specular tint leaning olive-teal; shadow rays pass through (Light Path 'Is Shadow Ray' to Transparent). Two normal maps added as N1 + N2 - Ng: a very soft swell (16 waves with whole numbers of wavelengths on a 3 m tile, RMS slope about 0.012 to 0.035) and ripple rings on a second UV over the pond box (4 to 7 rings, spacing 9 to 13 cm, Gaussian fade, crest slope 0.13), one story per spot (a lily stem, a falling leaf, open water). Bed: lower the bed plate only outside the corridor other builders depend on; real pebble geometry 4 to 12 cm in 7 chunky shapes, densest on the shelf (58 per m2), 51 on the slope, 38 in the middle; 4 flat stones 27 to 36 cm; 8 muted submerged leaves; silt colour #2a2d24 to #423826. Plants: 28 notched pads (cut a 12 to 20 degree wedge, upturned rim, 19 to 40 cm), greener brighter olive with a faint self-light so they stay green in shade; 5 pink-white flowers 16 to 19 cm plus buds; 7 iris clumps with 17 purple flower stems (flowers 45 percent bigger); cattails; reeds; 16 red and orange floating leaves 12 to 17 cm. Maple: keep leaf shape, size, colour ramp and count within 20 percent (56,000 leaves instanced by a copy of the leaf instancer); crown = 7 pads (centre, radii 1.1 to 1.5 m, thickness 0.55 to 0.75 m, tilt toward the sun) with scalloped outline, loose hanging tails on a share of rim leaves, cloud lumps on top, soft top-lit; a bent twisting trunk with root flare and 17 branch meshes; 'windows': leaves in front of a branch, seen from the hero camera, are removed inside a view tube so the branch shows; colour pattern carried from the previous crown by nearest old leaf, ramp positions rank-mapped to the old quantiles so the colour distribution is exactly unchanged. Pine: keep pad places and sizes (its wall shadow must not move), flatten to discs (thickness at most 0.27 of diameter), radial needle sprays with a shorter chunky fringe (mean 14.6 cm, strokes 3.3 times wider), plated bark with real plate depth 0.075.
techniques.measured_results: Water bands hero (same sample points): rim 0.268, edge 0.254, mid-edge 0.221, slope 0.190, middle 0.178; edge minus middle 0.076 (needed 0.04, was 0.048); middle moved +0.005 (allowed 0.03); luminance spread ratio edge to middle 1.72 (needed 1.5). Pond close-up flat windows 59 of 384 (first integration) to 12 to 0 after lightening. Bed plate lowered in 196 of 1117 vertices up to 7.5 cm; 898 vertices inside the corridor unchanged (0.000 m). Maple: pads 7, area after over before 1.012, IoU 0.870, covered 0.936 in the hero; branches visible with at least 120 px: 4 (builder) to 7 plus trunk (fix); mean red 0.4512 (first, too dark) to 0.4668 (fix; original 0.4665); maple box detail energy 8.98 (first; +9.8 percent with other changes, limit 8) to 8.18 to 8.09 (original 8.30). Pine: 8 discs, triangles 65,537 to 64,565 to 51,988, IoU 0.806, covered 0.878.
techniques.traps_and_failures: Veranda water edge band is NOT lighter than its middle (0.141 vs 0.176; it was not before either). The pond reads mostly at 100 percent: pebbles and ripples invisible at 1200 px even after the fix. White shards on the pond were the hall lamps mirrored: fixed by switching the lamps' glossy-ray visibility off (they still light the garden). Light fields such as transmission and volume factor did nothing in 5.1.2 Cycles; use object ray visibility. Pads first smaller and browner than before. Pine fringe first long hairy strands. Maple first two hard slabs, branches hidden in deep shade; opening branch windows cost about 0.004 of the squint score and four windows cluttered the hero (use 2). The builder's idempotence failed on an already staged scene: running the maple step a second time removed the copied node group, which cleared the modifier and the leaves vanished (the ownership hash test did not catch it). The pond close-up camera under the bridge (57 of 384 flat windows) and the one with reeds filling the frame are poor show pieces. Maple tilts lean south-east although the sun is west-south-west (left, matched the previous brightness, not tested). Basin water shares the water material and was not looked at.

techniques.name: The style rule: details are designed parts of the style (and a style note per place)
techniques.what_it_is: A written rule, added on the person's direction ('These things need to be integrated into the style. So it's just part of design.'): every wear mark, moss patch, crack, joint, tuft, flower and ripple is a DESIGNED ELEMENT in the place's own visual language: same simplified, slightly chunky shapes, same edge treatment, same palette, same light. Test: could it sit in a hand-painted game level next to the big rocks and the lantern without looking like it came from a more photographic picture? If it is finer, sharper, noisier or more scan-like, simplify: fewer, bigger, cleaner shapes.
techniques.why_it_matters: The person said 'don't make it more realistic, I still want the art style' AND 'bland, no character'. Without the rule the helpers (and the image painters) drifted photographic: hair-like grass (detail energy 6.9 to 7.5, twice the original), fuzzy moss, leafy hedges, glossy wet streaks. With it character is added as readable design. For the plugin: the rule must be in the first skill a model reads, and a style note must exist before any building.
techniques.how_to_do_it: Write the style note from the picture or target you must match, in this order: (0) the rule above, verbatim, for every builder; (1) form: a few big simple shapes, chunky, a little soft, corners with visible bevel 1 to 3 cm, silhouettes readable (you can name every object from its outline), repeats allowed if each repeat is a clean shape; (2) edges and surfaces: clean, crisp shadow edges, no film grain, flat-ish colour with soft blotches 20 to 60 cm plus a few clear marks; (3) palette: top 10 colours of the reference as hex, warm key against cool shadow, ONE hot accent (the maple), greens olive not fresh, and new detail colours from the same family (moss, mould, iron, lichen, water stain); (4) value range as percentiles and mean saturation; (5) detail per square metre as 'detail energy' per region and one readable feature per 5 to 10 cm on timber, 20 to 30 cm on ground, 50 cm on stone and walls; (6) what the style does NOT have (grain, hair-level grass, pores, glints on dust, lens dirt, depth-of-field on the main subject, modern objects); (7) checklist (designed-in test, squint, palette, detail-energy, light, one story per hand-span). The brief for 'character': a viewer finds one small story per hand-span (a worn corner, a moss rim, a drip stain, a cramp, a peg, a lily flower, a tuft with seed heads), never a hundred tiny details of equal weight. Rules for each kind: plank wear = clean rounded bevel and a few bigger notches, not noise; colour textures = a few big readable marks; normal maps = soft large-scale relief (grain grooves, plank edges, tile ridges), no micro-pore noise.
techniques.measured_results: Reference numbers of the garden picture: brightness percentiles 1/5/25/50/75/95/99 = 0.047/0.067/0.177/0.318/0.474/0.627/0.882 (a dark picture), mean saturation 0.399, saturation 0.405 in the veranda; detail energy (mean size of contrast left after a 2 px blur, 0 to 255) roof 8.0, maple 8.4, sand 7.5, bridge 5.4, deck 4.0, grass 3.6, rocks 3.6, wall 3.4 (photographs of the same things sit well above 12). Allowed ranges set for the round: not below 0.9 times and not above the smaller of 1.4 times and 10. After the round all seven boxes were inside (grass 4.39 = 1.24 times, rock 4.59 = 1.28 times, both under the 5.0 cap). A reviewer (the checker) judged 'art style kept: yes' twice, and 'more character than before: yes'.
techniques.traps_and_failures: Several painter prompts without the rule sentence drifted photographic (Nano Banana Pro hero first round: grass 7.5). With the rule one model went too far: hero_A2_stones became a flat cartoon with dark outlines and turquoise water. The 1.4 times limit was the direction step's own judgement, not the person's. Things the checker said still do not read at normal size: pegs, drip stains, slipped tiles, flowers, ripples (see the readability technique). The style note's boxes are fixed hero-pixel boxes, so every number is tied to one camera. Colours in a style note are rendered colours, not albedos.

techniques.name: Concept images as targets (paint-overs, element sheets, swatches) within a money limit
techniques.what_it_is: Use an image model to paint over the current picture, and to draw element sheets (bridge construction, planks, roof, trees, pond edge, lantern, grass and moss), then use the results as TARGETS for what to build in 3D. They are never pasted onto the scene.
techniques.why_it_matters: The person said 'generate an image of trees and so on in the art style and work from that'. The sheets showed how a bridge is built, how a plank is shaped, where moss sits, and gave measurable detail levels. A small model cannot invent these details; a target picture does it.
techniques.how_to_do_it: 1. Pick the painter by test: same prompt on three models. Nano Banana 2 kept the composition and the style best (with the rule sentence); Nano Banana Pro kept the composition but drifted photographic (hair grass, many flowers); Flux 3 stays in style but moved the composition (camera pulled back, lantern smaller, bridge shortened) and was rejected for paint-overs. 2. Prompt = guard paragraph (keep camera, framing, perspective, positions, colours, value range, art style; 'do NOT make anything more realistic, brighter, more saturated or more yellow'; no film grain; detail at the size of a hand-span) + the rule sentence + a short list of what to add + 'no people, no animals, no text'. Name the construction you want in words (posts on stone footings, cross beams, planks across with narrow gaps, round pegs, iron cramps) and what not to do ('NO posts, rails or poles rise above the deck': obeyed only partly). 3. Element sheets with one style paragraph ('ELEMENT SHEET in EXACTLY the same stylised art style... dark dusky background, each item separated, no text, no labels') plus a subject paragraph with panels (side elevation, plan, joint detail). 4. Read each result with the same measures as a render (detail energy per box, mean luminance and saturation) and an edge-structure correlation with the original (0.84 to 0.92 for all: every paint-over moves small things, so read as a target for look, never overlay). 5. Mark per picture FOLLOW and DO NOT COPY in the direction note. 6. Swatches: only as colour or mark vocabulary after a half-shift seam test; repair seams by repainting the centre cross; grade toward the palette. 7. Budget: price each call before it (fal price tool), one ledger row per call (time, step, model and settings, price, request id, running total), one call each unless a reason is written, user_intent passed verbatim, send only garden pictures or the style board (never anything personal), keep prompts in files, upload with prepare_upload then curl PUT.
techniques.measured_results: 29 paid calls, worst case US$3.86, best about US$2.84 to 3.68, of US$15; Fal's request history for 22 October lists exactly those 29 ids (the re-check matched them one to one); prices: Nano Banana Pro US$0.15 per image at 1K and 2K, Nano Banana 2 US$0.08 at 1K and 1.5 times at 2K (US$0.12), Flux 3 edit US$0.048 per megapixel (worst case US$0.383). Output sizes are not 3:2 (Pro 2528 x 1696, NB2 2528 x 1686, Flux 2496 x 1664). Detail energy (roof, bridge, grass, rock): original 8.09, 5.39, 3.57, 3.61; V3 (NB2) 6.35, 5.92, 3.59, 3.19 (closest); V1 Pro 9.17, 6.61, 4.15, 3.89; V2 Pro grass 6.89 (twice). Concept images ranked: sheet_bridge, sheet_plank2, sheet_roof, sheet_pond, sheet_grass, sheet_lantern, sheet_trees and hero_V3 as targets; hero_A2_stones, V2, r1 Pro/Flux rejected.
techniques.traps_and_failures: A message sent to the concept helper woke a second copy of it; the two copies ran at once and made 8 extra paid calls (about US$0.70) before one stopped; sheet prompt files may have been overwritten. Targets contain flaws to name: a moon in the sky, a ghost of the house above the tree sheet, corner posts rising like railings, dark outline strokes, glossy wet streaks, turquoise or violet water, deep-red maple shift, leafy photographic hedge, yellow ground drift. Swatches: sw_pondbed has a blurred reflection of the whole garden in its lower part; sw_grass has big bushes and flowers that repeat; sw_moss reads as dragon scales; sw_roof is flat saturated blue; only the plaster swatch tiled and was used. Sending the hero picture for flat swatches makes the painter paste it in (send the style board). Nano Banana 2.1 and GPT image models show only '1 unit = US$1', so a call's price is unknown beforehand. Search_docs answers are very large, submit answers repeat the prompt.

techniques.name: Measures on pictures: value range, detail energy per region, squint test with a where-it-loses map, flat-colour windows, saturation, silhouette, light-group sum
techniques.what_it_is: A small set of numbers computed from rendered pictures that say whether new detail stayed inside the style: brightness percentiles and mean saturation; detail energy per region; the squint test (structural similarity of 12-pixel-blurred luminance against the previous picture); flat-colour windows; share of strongly saturated and turquoise pixels; silhouette overlap per object group; and whether light groups add up to the picture.
techniques.why_it_matters: Without them a 'more character' round can quietly make the picture more photographic, brighter, busier or different at thumbnail size. They are also the only objective yardsticks a fresh checker can re-run. They are NOT proof of quality: the checklist is a guide, the eye decides.
techniques.how_to_do_it: All in numpy inside Blender (PIL is not there). Luminance = 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B. Percentiles at 1/5/25/50/75/95/99 percent; mean saturation = (max - min) / max. Detail energy = mean of |L8 - gaussian blur(L8, 2 px)| in a fixed box of the picture (L8 = luminance x 255 rounded): compare after to before per region (allowed: 0.9 times up to the smaller of 1.4 times and 10). Squint: blur luminance 12 px, local SSIM with a 6 px Gaussian window (constants 0.01 squared, 0.03 squared), target 0.92 against the previous picture; also at 24 and 36 px. Where-it-loses: give regions (maple, pond, lawn, rocks) first-come-first-served, report each region's mean score, its share of the total missing score (sum of 1 - score), a 4 x 6 grid, and the score if one region were unchanged; draw a red heat map. Flat windows: 96 x 96 windows with step 48 below the sky (y from 38 percent of the height) whose luminance std is under 0.010 (limit: none outside sky, hills, paper, glowing windows; under 2 percent below 0.014). Palette: share of pixels with saturation over 0.70 outside the accent (maple), and turquoise (hue 160 to 210, saturation over 0.35) outside sky and hills. Silhouettes: render alpha masks per object group at both cameras (everything else set to holdout, film transparent, Cycles 4 samples), IoU of before and after masks AND share of the old shape still covered. Light-group check: sum of the Combined_<group> layers of the multi-layer EXR against Combined (relative error), limit 2 percent. A flat-colour ID map is better than fixed boxes for a new place: take regions from object masks.
techniques.measured_results: Hero percentiles before to final: 0.047/0.067/0.177/0.318/0.474/0.627/0.882 to 0.048/0.075/0.171/0.311/0.467/0.613/0.882; saturation 0.399 to 0.396; veranda median 0.331 to 0.3065 (limit 0.03), 99 percent 0.747 to 0.7396 (limit 0.80), saturation 0.405 to 0.4244 (limit 0.44). Detail energy (before, first integration, final) roof 7.88/8.33/7.79, bridge 5.32/5.28/5.29, grass 3.55/4.08/4.39, maple 8.30/9.11/8.09, sand 7.38/7.59/7.71, wall 3.39/3.31/3.68, rock 3.60/4.57/4.59. Flat windows hero 5 to 0 of 931, veranda 3 to 0. Squint: first integration 0.895 hero 0.882 veranda; after fixes 0.883 and 0.873; at 36 px 0.933 and 0.920; the maple region scores 0.748, pond 0.802, lawn 0.900; maple 43 percent of the missing score, pond 29, lawn 10, rocks 4, rest 9; the re-check's stricter box-window formula gave 0.844 and 0.829 (and said hero would pass at 0.957 if maple and pond were identical). Silhouettes (IoU / covered, hero): bridge 0.769/0.954, roof 0.855/0.986, maple 0.868/0.910, pine 0.806/0.878, lantern 0.982, walls 0.924. Light-group sum error hero 1.24 percent, veranda 1.37; close-ups denoised bridge 1.55, eave 0.51, pond 3.10, grass 2.41, and undenoised pond 1.98, grass 0.97. Strongly saturated pixels outside the maple: 1.45 (original), 1.76 (final, limit 1.0, already over before; the re-check by its own mask: 2.25 vs original 1.99).
techniques.traps_and_failures: The squint target 0.92 was the direction step's judgement; it was missed by every fixer and the fix round made it WORSE (0.895 to 0.883) because chunky tufts, moss, bigger pads and the layered maple add structure at 12 px. The yardsticks conflict with the concept: following the concept (layered maple, readable pond) breaks the squint test, and nobody decided which counts. Silhouette IoU fails for a bridge that gained posts (area 1.2 times) while 'share of old shape covered' passes. Hero-pixel boxes mean the veranda picture cannot use them (the veranda's maple sits in the middle, so its saturation share of 12 to 15 percent is meaningless). The turquoise region still included hills (3 percent); the maple cut-out was rough. The metric scripts crashed on float64 buffers when shrinking 2400-wide pictures (fixed, cost a rerun). Detail-energy numbers on 1200 px previews are lower because the script scales up. 'Veranda detail boxes' were never judged. Light-group layers are not denoised, so the sum check is exact only without denoising.

techniques.name: Owning stages, tagging every new thing, idempotent stages that restore what they changed, and a conflict check after every stage
techniques.what_it_is: A way to let several builders change one scene without breaking each other: each stage owns named objects and materials, tags everything new with custom properties and puts it in its own collection, never edits a shared material or node group in place (copies it), can be run twice with the same result, and a chain step fingerprints the whole scene after every stage and reports any change outside the owner's list.
techniques.why_it_matters: Four builders worked side by side on one starting scene. A stage that quietly renames, deletes or edits a shared material destroys another owner's work, and old names the weathering kit relies on must survive. A plugin workflow that builds a place in parts needs this discipline or the parts will not combine.
techniques.how_to_do_it: Rules written in the brief: one starting file, read-only, never saved over; each builder delivers stage_<name>.py with apply(options) that works on the open scene, prints a report of objects created, changed, deleted, and is idempotent (it first removes what it created, found by garden_owner plus a 'new' flag, and restores what it replaced). New objects: collection G6 <owner>, custom properties garden_owner and garden_role (stone.natural, stone.dressed, timber.deck, timber.frame, roof.tile, wall.plaster, wall.cap, ground.earth, ground.gravel, growth, water, glow, leaf, bark), materials named 'G6 <owner> / <what>'; never rename or delete another's object; never edit a material or node group anyone else uses ('GARDEN scan *', 'WK *', 'CT / *'): make a copy under your own name and point your objects at it; keep membership in the light-link receiver collections; frozen list (cameras, sun, lights, world, hills, render settings, pond outline, water level, route within 0.15 m). Restore recorded edits: when a stage changes an input of an owned original material (unlink a socket, set a default) it records the old link or value in a custom property on the material so cleanup can put it back; when it replaces a mesh it keeps the original (renamed, fake user) for restore; UV layers and colour attributes it added are recorded too. Chain step: snapshot() fingerprints objects (matrix, mesh hash incl. UVs, material slots, modifiers, collections, light linking, light group), materials and node groups (node and link hash), collections and their members, frozen state (render, cycles, view settings, world, compositor, view layers), light links, weathering-kit node count; after each stage diff against the previous snapshot and report as violations: object or material or node group or collection removed, foreign object or material changed, new object without garden_owner, existing node group changed, frozen state or light linking changed, kit nodes lost; warnings: new object without garden_role or outside its collection, new names ending in .001 that duplicate an existing stem. Run in the plain order and the reverse order. Finally add shared preview cameras, pack images, save compressed, re-open, re-check normal maps and the triangle count.
techniques.measured_results: Plain order wood, roof, ground, pond, final: 0 violations and 0 errors in every stage, both orders; no object or material changed by two stages; lights, light links, world, compositor and render settings unchanged. Per stage (first integration, seconds): wood 2.7 (24 added, 30 changed, 13 materials added, 10 changed), roof 20.5 (41 added, 40 changed, 44 materials added), ground 8.4, pond 1.4. Scene: objects 180 to 348, materials 147 to 220, triangles with instances 3,570,312 to 4,073,307 (+14.1 percent), kit nodes 989 to 1,374 (none lost). Re-opened saved file draws the same triangle count (4,073,307). Idempotence: each stage run twice gives the same counts (wood 204 objects and 707,432 vertices; ground 212 objects 3,655,750 triangles, file sizes within 0.003 percent; pond 219 objects).
techniques.traps_and_failures: Order independence is not exact: reverse order gave 1,955 more triangles (0.05 percent) and later 3,330 more (the roof cushions depend on what the camera sees when the wood stage ran). The checks missed the maple idempotence bug (hash only). The report sentence 'nothing vanished' was wrong for the saved file: 58 unused materials (56 old 'Astra / planks tone' plus 'GARDEN ground.earth' and 'Life / pond bed') and the node group 'Life / maple leaf instancer' were dropped on save because they had no users. The saved scene carried 48 leftover preview cameras (wood 10, pond 7, roof 6, ground 5, final 20). The ground builder did not copy the scatter node groups as briefed but swapped its own group; no one noticed until read. Fix stages were only chained once (each fixer first used the builders' original other stages), the four fixed stages together were run only in the second integration; applying the chain twice on one scene was not tested. No report.md could be written by the sub-agents (tools refused: 'subagents return findings as text'), so reports lived only in the structured answers.

techniques.name: Roles and placeholders: let later stages cover objects they never saw
techniques.what_it_is: Every new object gets garden_role (and an owner); builders that only make geometry give it a one-colour placeholder material 'GARDEN placeholder <role>'; the surfaces stage replaces placeholders by role, finding old objects by name patterns and new ones by garden_role.
techniques.why_it_matters: A surface-and-wear pass must work on objects made later by another builder (or model) without knowing their names. This is the mechanism that makes 'apply the full treatment by itself' possible for a plain request: geometry first, roles on everything, then the treatment keyed by role.
techniques.how_to_do_it: Roles list (stone.natural, stone.dressed, timber.deck, timber.frame, roof.tile, wall.plaster, wall.cap, ground.earth, ground.gravel, growth, water, glow, leaf, bark). NAME_RULES regexes for old objects, ROLE_TO_FAMILY for new ones, a NEVER list (glow, leaves, water, hills, sky). A mesh keeps its slots when reshaped; a new object gets one placeholder. Test with odd-named test objects tagged with roles: all got the right material in both looks, none left a placeholder, the kit gave each its right role from garden_role alone. Also the kit's set file follows the same names (^Rock \d+$, ^Lantern (base|post|gallery|firebox|cap)$ ...), so owners keep existing names.
techniques.measured_results: 10 test objects with odd names: all right material, no placeholder left, correct kit role; cross-check on 70 new objects of the shapes stage: none left without a surface material; the kit left 2 objects without a role (Basin bamboo spout, Basin ladle: tagged growth with the bamboo material, intentionally unweathered).
techniques.traps_and_failures: Several objects shared one material with something else (hall plaster, three garden walls, lantern finial, pine); the stage had to give them their own (10 slots changed) before treating each by family. In-place patterns are needed for shared originals, with a PRIMARY_FAMILY table deciding which family keeps the original datablock. Painted and real looks switching in one session leaves residue: reopen the start file. Names are still the main router; garden_role is used only as fallback and may be missing.

techniques.name: The weathering kit on a place: what to switch on, per-object dials, camera dot size, and the sticker problem
techniques.what_it_is: The project's reusable kit (dust-and-algae film, runoff under caps and eaves, damp foot, plaster hairlines and stone chips, wall growth, dirt, patch moss; also steps, paint, ground cracks, iron, puddles, wetness, joints, rubbish, 3D growth) applied from a settings file and a look, with each object's strength read from wk_* custom properties.
techniques.why_it_matters: It is the 'dirt, grime, weeds, weathering' layer the person wants every place to carry automatically. The garden shows how to switch it for a different place, and that it can produce stickers that must be tuned per material.
techniques.how_to_do_it: Layers on for the garden: soot, runoff, foot, wallgrowth, wallcracks, dirt, groundmoss; off: steps, paint, groundcracks, iron, growth (3D growth owned by the plant builder). Weeds near zero, wet = darker, greener, glossier, no puddles. The set file declares the sun direction (the kit assumed north = +y and latitude 35; the stage reads the brightest sun lamp's real direction and writes it into the set file, rebuilding the where-pictures (mask pack: height above ground, damp, shade, moss sites) when others changed geometry or the sun moved, about 20 to 60 s). Call camera_for_picture(camera, picture_height) before each picture: marks are sized in picture dots (the render harness sets Dot Angle on every node tagged wk == 'scale': 120 to 159 nodes). Per-material first guesses: lichen about off on plaster and wood, strong on natural stone; moss weaker on plaster, stronger on stone and roof; moss_vs_stone 0.9 to 1.0 on grey stone; on dark surfaces (roof, dark timber) use pale marks only; dark grime to about a quarter of a surface. Kit fixes made in a private copy: bark role matches curves, roof.deck matches nothing (removed), never patterns, roles may list several custom_props alternatives (garden_role), garden_kept look. Remove() takes everything off again.
techniques.measured_results: Kit nodes 989 to 1,367 to 1,374 across the chain (none lost). Street unchanged by the kit patches except one extra link (default keeps the street the same). On the garden the first layer-by-layer sweep located the pale-mint stone blotches (patch moss) and the agate stripes and neon bands (foot splash and tide band, wall cracks, wall growth). Fix: multiply the per-object numbers on stones (see moss technique).
techniques.traps_and_failures: Kit moss draws flat painted tones, built for the film's painter, so on a photographed surface it looked like paint (pale lime, then 'polka dots'); at film size on the street the kit added little a viewer could see except rust and small weeds; geometry instances read the instanced object's wk numbers; roof materials inside geometry nodes were invisible to the kit until patched. Applying it twice is wrong ('do not apply weathering twice'). The kit needs its whole folder (integrate dependency). Moss on a scan that already carries moss doubles.

techniques.name: Light, sky, hills, light groups and a finish that can be rebalanced for free
techniques.what_it_is: A light stage that replaces a flat wash with a graded sky, keeps the key light's direction, cools the fill, adds a rim lamp linked to chosen objects, builds hills that go all the way round, sets Cycles light groups, and a compositor finish; plus a regrade script that rebalances after drawing.
techniques.why_it_matters: Place surfaces look right only under graded light with warm key and cool shadows; a model that lights a village with one lamp gets flat results. Light groups let the glow be rebalanced after the (paid) render for free.
techniques.how_to_do_it: World: replace the one flat orange by a graded sky (warm horizon band, blue above) with a glow round the sun's REAL direction taken from the sun lamp, and a separate cooler dimmer 'lighting sky' for light that falls on things (camera and mirror rays see the pretty sky, everything else is lit by the cool one, so shadows turn blue-violet not orange). Hills: 4 to 5 ridges all 360 degrees (nearer darker and cooler, farther paler and more lilac, tops take the sky peach so they fade by colour, no blur), plain continued to the horizon in colour steps; backdrop only (does not light the scene). Lights: sun strength 12 kept in direction, fill cooler weaker (2600 W), one warm rim sun-type lamp linked ONLY to maple and roof, one soft roof lift lamp linked only to the roof, lantern dim (18 W; flame strength 7; window 3.3 stops over the stone, evening 6.2). Light groups sun, rim, sky, fill, hall, lantern, rest on the view layer; every other emitter put in 'rest' so layers add up. Finish: compositor mild bloom threshold 2.0 (only screens and lantern), vignette 0.55, no blur, caustics off, AgX Punchy, exposure 0.5. Evening variant: sun off, deep blue world, dimmer fill, lantern 1800 to 2200 K. Regrade: read the multi-layer EXR (the Image node must be told layer 'ViewLayer' in 5.2 or it shows no light-group layers), multiply each group by a gain (one or three numbers), add, denoise the sum once, bloom, vignette, same view transform and exposure, write PNG in about a second. Shadow lift ('toe') at the end of the compositor: out = in + tint * L0 * T / (T + luminance(in)), parameters T 0.03, L0 0.014, tint (0.75, 1.0, 0.95), to remove black holes under the bridge. Pond shards: switch the glow lamps' glossy-ray visibility off.
techniques.measured_results: Hero value study (original / real): sky band brightness 0.551 / 0.462, screens 0.726 / 0.778, screens divided by sky 1.32 / 1.68 (target: sky well below screens), edge over centre 1.11 / 0.87 (target 0.8, not quite reached), roof band mean 0.139 / 0.255, roof share nearly black 9.7 / 4.2 percent, shade blue over red on white wall 0.87 / 1.12 (cool shadows), sunlit 0.80 / 0.79 (low sun stays warm), mean 0.331 / 0.314, 5th percentile 0.081 / 0.043 (darker darks: weak point, toe lift added). Layer shares of the frame: sun 29, sky plus hills 30, hall glow 32, fill 9, rim 0.35, lantern 0.35, rest 0.4. Groups add up to the picture within 0.6 percent undenoised and about 2 percent denoised; regrade with all gains 1 reproduces to 0.7 of 255. Pictures 960 x 640 at 192 samples took 2.5 to 6 s; a 360-degree picture 4.9 s; full-size final about 36 to 44 s.
techniques.traps_and_failures: First sky too cool and lilac (lost the golden mood); rim lamp first an area lamp (0.04 percent of the frame), then a stronger sun-type lamp; group-sum check first read every layer as the same (argument error); regrade first found no layers (needs layer 'ViewLayer') and was noisy (layers are not denoised); painted-look sky colours forgotten for two rounds; light fields (transmission, volume factor) did nothing in 5.1.2 Cycles: use object ray visibility, record it as artistic separation; the evening maple stays bright because its leaf material emits a little light; Lantern light inside the glow box is blocked in Cycles; pond reflection of the lantern not visible from the hero camera; the hero camera was renamed 'photo' because the kit's set file calls it that. A rejected darker version, spotlit lanterns and a veil that erased the hall were all tried and dropped: keep a broad connected glow with a few dark interruptions.

techniques.name: Cheap rendering on rented cards (pay per second): previews, finals, close-up cameras, ledger and the stall
techniques.what_it_is: Draw everything bigger than a tiny test on a rented GPU through the pay-per-second client, with one job per round and many pictures in it, previews at small size, finals at full size, and a ledger of billed seconds.
techniques.why_it_matters: This computer is slow (a small EEVEE picture of the hooked scene took over 3 minutes); the card draws a full 2400 x 1600 final in 36 to 44 s. Models must know the rhythm and the failure modes, and must never put keys, endpoint ids, machine ids or volume ids into plugin files (the garden scripts here contain none; they call a client in the scratch folder).
techniques.how_to_do_it: Rhythm: build the combined scene on the card and save it ONLY on the store (about 81 MB; .blend, EXR, full PNG never downloaded); preview round at 960 x 640 (or 1200 x 800) with 96 samples adaptive denoised (about 6 to 10 s each), many cameras in one job; judge thumbnail against the original first, then 100 percent crops; final 2400 x 1600 at 512 samples, seed 7, same exposure and compositor, with the multi-layer EXR and --check-groups, --require-gpu; close-ups 1600 x 1067 (17 to 24 s). Download only JPG previews under 400 KB and small text files. Pick close-up cameras by drawing 16 candidates and keep the best (cameras are checked for line of sight, distance to hedges and a lit-lawn box, or the picture is black). At most 3 jobs run account-wide; batch. Each job logs billed work seconds and wake-up seconds to a ledger (rpwait.py). Set the weathering kit's Dot Angle for each picture height. Per-builder budgets: wood 11 jobs 1,550 s, roof 20 jobs 2,750 s then 34 jobs 3,760 s in the fix, ground 1,760 s then 2,900 s, pond 3,090 s then 3,650 s, wood fix 2,184 s, integration 437 s, second integration 1,327 s; all about US$0.4 to 1.15 each at US$1.10 an hour. A final stays under 90 s and under 12 GB of card memory; at most 1.5 million added triangles per builder.
techniques.measured_results: Finals on RTX 4090: hero 37.7 to 44.3 s, veranda 36.4 to 39.7 s, close-ups 16.7 to 24 s, light-group error 1.2 to 1.4 percent; cold start of a worker 18 s the first time, 0.7 to 2.3 s later. Costs: ledger files add to about 11,354 s plus about 2,900 s without a ledger, about 4 hours or US$4.4 at US$1.10 an hour; the story quotes US$10.89 by RunPod's hourly bill for about 4 hours of card time, which does not match; test machine about US$0.03; image calls US$2.84 to 3.86.
techniques.traps_and_failures: Stall 1: from 07:31 to 08:30 UTC jobs waited with workers reported 'idle' and none were taken, restarting the workers did nothing; cause: RunPod balance US$0.13 (it does not hand jobs to pay-per-second workers with a balance that low); an ordinary machine on the same store proved nothing was broken. Lesson: check the balance (GraphQL myself.clientBalance; read the user's own settings at run time, never store them) before a long job and whenever jobs wait while workers sit idle. Integration had separately seen jobs not start 07:37 to 08:30, purged its own three waiting jobs and resubmitted, which ran; cause unknown, a different explanation than the credit note. The container restarted twice (about 02:48 and 09:40); jobs carried on; the second restart lost the second checker's work; disk here fell to 0.39 GB (limit 0.4 GB; clear npm cache, stale tars, never download PNGs or EXR). Mistakes: a build job sent before its job file existed; a start-scene path not on the store; the metrics step crashed on float64 buffers; direction test run with wrong plane size; a command refused by the safety check (rm -rf of a scratch folder inside a quoted string) left a 1 MB folder on the store. The full pictures were once downloaded by mistake (11 MB) and deleted at once. Cold-start billing unknown. Idle 'standby' workers cost nothing according to RunPod's hour-by-hour bill (a checker had worried).

techniques.name: Fresh checkers and claim checking
techniques.what_it_is: Helpers who did not build the thing look at the result with their own code and eyes, re-measure what the builders claimed, test the claims one by one (holds / does not hold, with evidence), and write problems with the cheapest fix. A second kind checks money and process.
techniques.why_it_matters: Several builder claims were wrong or unproven, and the problems the person cares about (pale clean planks, bean-bag moss, stamped knot) were found only by looking at 100 percent crops and re-counting. A plugin that lets a builder grade itself will pass work that fails the person's own complaint.
techniques.how_to_do_it: Checker brief: say what to check (art, construction, normal maps, money), give no builder reports as proof, ask for own scripts (the checkers wrote fp.py, struct.py, nm_struct.py, nm_dir.py, nm_sem.py, plank_stats.py, warp_stats.py, uv_check.py, crops with before and after strips at 100 percent), a different formula where possible (box-window SSIM versus Gaussian), and a verdict per element (yes / nearly / no) with why, a claims_checked list with holds true or false and evidence, problems each with the cheapest fix, should_fix_now, and an honest statement of what was not tested and that the checker was not blind. Fixers then get the checker's findings plus the main session's own list (note 32: tufts thin, leaves and flowers too small, moss blotches on the path like camouflage, agate stripes on rocks, pond still dark, pine needles fuzzy) and one owner each. The re-check re-runs the claims. Check the money against the ledger and the fal request history (ids match one to one), the RunPod ledgers against reports, grep all code and reports for the person's e-mail and name, '.runpod', keys, tokens (none found; one price lookup printed the account holder's name, not copied anywhere).
techniques.measured_results: Claims that did NOT hold: moss plus mould 9.8 percent of planks (checker 0.6 percent olive on the left run; the builder read a mask picture it never showed); 'at 50 percent scale a reviewer names at least 12 of 16 features' (first check 7 to 11, re-check 9 to 13 and not blind); 'all pegs and cramps seated' (6 of 8 straps with a floating nail head 14 to 18 mm; 14 cramp parts not in wood); 'nothing vanished' (58 materials and 1 node group gone on save); 'plank normal map fails in X (+0.061)' was false (wrong plane size; +0.55); 'moss plus mould 11.6 percent' after the fix not confirmed (colour count cannot separate); builder idempotence for the maple failed on a staged scene; the stripes-on-rocks claim 'from the old stone colour' held as 'not new' but the cause was kit layers (found by the roof fixer). Claims that held: value range, squint miss (reproduced 0.8827 and 0.8734 exactly, with a stricter formula 0.844 and 0.829), detail energy, budget (29 calls), leaf colour distribution (hue histograms), supports (all 59 planks on at least 2 supports, longest unsupported stretch 0.85 m), 85 normal-map materials from 17 images wired right (8 maps re-tested +0.55 to +0.99), RunPod seconds add up to the reports (11,354 s), no personal details in code.
techniques.traps_and_failures: The checker is not blind to the feature list, so the 12-of-16 reading test was never done by a blind reviewer. The second check (construction, normal maps and money) running since 08:57 was lost in the 09:40 container restart and had to be re-run; its first result is null in workflow_result.json. The checker's disk fell to 392 MB (other helpers' files) and it kept going with a tiny footprint, deleting its downloads. Checkers can over-trust a builder's own test files: the integrator copied the builders' direction results without re-running them; the plank X test result came from a wrong plane. 'Should fix now' flipped from True to False after the fixes while the squint test stayed missed; the re-check said show it now and say plainly it was missed. Builders also asked for report.md files; the tools refused for sub-agents ('return findings as text') so there are no report.md files.

techniques.name: A workflow that builds a place in parts: concept, direction and briefs, builders, integration, checkers, fixers, re-check
techniques.what_it_is: The order of work that was actually run for the character round, with what each step handed on.
techniques.why_it_matters: It produced a believable, in-style, more characterful garden that a fresh checker accepted on style, character and bridge logic, with 85 normal-mapped materials and no ownership violations. The plugin's fourth requirement (a workflow that builds a place in parts with fresh checkers) can copy this shape.
techniques.how_to_do_it: 1. Concept step (paid image model, within a limit): paint-overs, element sheets, swatches, a style note with the rule. 2. Direction step (a fresh pair of eyes): verdict on every concept picture (FOLLOW / DO NOT COPY), element-by-element table with owner, what the scene already has (measured: no normal maps, no UVs, planks boxes), the normal-map method, the guard against realism (numbers), the split into owners with names, frozen things and contracts between owners, running and cost rules, 25 acceptance tests (global look, wood and bridge, roof walls stones, ground, pond and trees, normal maps, UV hygiene, ownership and idempotence, combined scene, reports). 3. Four briefs, one per owner, each with: read first (direction note, style note, pictures, matching skill, normal_tools), rules for every builder, steps in PRIORITY ORDER with time-box (about 2.5 hours; a stop leaves something coherent), concept pictures to follow and not copy, own / do not touch lists, normal maps for you, guard numbers for your boxes, preview views list (cameras named 'G6 <owner> cam n'), deliverables, own checks with named tests, image budget at most US$1.00 with a written reason. 4. Four builders in parallel, each testing alone on the starting scene (stage on a card, test report, previews, sheets for the person). 5. Integration: chain, conflict check in two orders, save combined scene, preview round, pick close-ups, finals, measures, sheets. 6. Two fresh checkers in parallel (art; construction, normal maps and money). 7. Fix round restructured to four fixers in parallel, one per owner, each given the checker's findings plus the main session's own list; no paid images; then one integration of the fixed stages and finals; then a fresh re-check; stop (do not chase the 0.92 squint number; show it and say plainly). 8. Plain-words final: what was done, tested, not tested, failed, seconds used, money, where saved.
techniques.measured_results: Time and cost: about 2.5 hours per builder, 11 to 20 jobs each, fix round 13 to 50 jobs per fixer; hero and veranda finals 36 to 44 s; whole round about 4 hours of card time; image money US$2.84 to 3.86 of US$15. Outcome (re-check): style kept yes, more character yes, bridge makes sense yes; elements: bridge yes, planks yes, deck nearly, roof nearly, walls yes, grass nearly, moss nearly, pond yes, maple yes, pine yes, rocks yes, lantern nearly. Squint test missed (0.883, 0.873).

techniques.name: Ranking what matters and making small things readable at normal size
techniques.what_it_is: Decide what to build first by how much of the picture it fills times how wrong it looks, and make character readable at the size the viewer sees it: bigger, bolder or fewer, not more numerous.
techniques.why_it_matters: Many 'character' items were invisible at 1200 px: pegs, drip stains, slipped tiles, flowers (0.02 percent of the picture), ripples. A model adding 100 tiny details of equal weight makes noise and still fails the person's test of 'one small story per hand-span' that a viewer can find.
techniques.how_to_do_it: 1. Count frame share per group from a flat-colour ID render at the main camera; rank improvements by share times wrongness (plan table of 11 items). 2. Choose the order of builder steps by that ranking so a stopped job leaves a coherent result. 3. For every small feature say how big it must be in the picture: set pixel widths at the real viewing size (flowers 11 to 32 px at 2400 px; red leaves 22 to 76 px; pegs 1.5 times bigger; drip stains 50 percent longer and 90 percent wider; slipped tiles 50 percent further; footing stones raised to the waterline; pads 27 to 40 cm; flowers 16 to 19 cm). 4. Make them bigger or stronger in dials, not more of them. 5. Use a reading test: at 50 percent scale (1200 x 800) a reviewer who has not seen the list names at least 12 of 16 features (pegs on the bridge, posts on footings, plank variety, moss at post feet, roof tile variety, roof moss, drip stains, slipped tile, tufts with seed heads, small flowers, worn path, moss cushions, shallow pebble edge, ripples, lily flowers, maple pads or branches). 6. Judge thumbnail first, then 100 percent crops.
techniques.measured_results: Reading test: first check 7 to 11 of 16 (clear: posts, plank variety, roof tile variety, tufts with seed heads, worn path, moss cushions, maple pads; borderline: moss at post feet, roof moss, lily flowers, cramps; not readable: pegs, drip stains, slipped tile, small flowers, shallow pebble edge, ripples). After the fix 9 to 13 (not blind), about 11 to 12 with a kind reading; still not readable: drip stains, slipped tile, ripples at 1200 px. Flowers 0.02 percent to 0.11 percent hero. Roof moss cushions read; lantern moss now nearly invisible at the hero.
techniques.traps_and_failures: Features sized by their real size are unreadable at the viewing size; fixing by size does not help the squint score. The test was never done by a blind reviewer. The roof close-up still looks more scanned than the lantern and rocks (blotchy lichen on tiles). The hero shows lantern moss only a few pixels wide while the concept has more. The pond close-up chosen for the person's sheet was a poor showpiece (reeds fill the frame).
