techniques.name: B16. Picture measures: value range, detail energy, squint test, flat windows, palette, silhouettes
techniques.what_it_is: Numbers that say whether a new picture kept the old one's look.
techniques.why_it_matters: They are cheap, objective and caught what eyes missed (the squint miss, the saturation limit).
techniques.how_to_do_it: VALUE RANGE: luminance percentiles 1, 5, 25, 50, 75, 95, 99 and mean saturation of the new picture within the old one's (median and 5 and 95 percent within 0.03, 99 percent not above 0.92, saturation 0.36-0.44). DETAIL ENERGY: mean of |L - blur(L, 2 px)| x 255 inside named boxes. SQUINT TEST: structural similarity of the 12-pixel Gaussian blurred luminance of new and old, window 6 px, target 0.92; squint_regions.py says where the points were lost and each region's share of the missing score. FLAT WINDOWS: 96x96 windows (step 48) below the sky with luminance standard deviation under 0.010 (none allowed; at most 2 percent under 0.014). PALETTE: outside the accent at most 1 percent of pixels with saturation above 0.70, at most 0.3 percent turquoise (hue 160-210, saturation above 0.35), no pure-white pixel group over 30 pixels outside lit glass. SILHOUETTES: before and after silhouette PNGs (alpha above 0.5) give IoU and the share of the old shape still covered (sil_iou.py). READS AT NORMAL SIZE: a reviewer who has not seen the list names at least 12 of 16 features at 50 percent scale. DESIGNED-IN TEST: 100 percent crops of the new next to the old show the same picture language. Light: value study at thumbnail size against the old picture; one change at a time on a fixed camera; light groups (sun, sky, fill, hall glow, lantern) in an EXR whose sum must match the picture within 2 percent; do not hide lights' glow in the plan: check the compositor sum.
techniques.measured_results: MEASURED on the garden: value range held (hero 0.048/0.075/0.171/0.311/0.467/0.613/0.882 against 0.047/0.067/0.177/0.318/0.474/0.627/0.882; saturation 0.396 against 0.399); squint missed: first integration 0.895 and 0.882, after fixes 0.883 and 0.873; checker's stricter formula 0.844 and 0.829; in the hero the maple (0.77) and pond (0.83) caused about 64 percent of the loss, with those two equal the hero would score 0.957; palette: outside-accent saturation above 0.70 was 1.76 percent (integrator) or 2.25 percent (checker) against the limit 1 percent, original 1.99 percent by the checker's mask; silhouette IoU below 0.85 for bridge (0.77 hero, 0.80 veranda), pine 0.81 and veranda maple 0.81 but 0.88-1.0 by 'old shape still covered'; light-group sum error 1.24 and 1.37 percent on the main finals, 3.1 and 2.4 on two close-ups.
techniques.traps_and_failures: The detail-energy boxes are in hero pixel coordinates only (veranda not judged); a measure with a hard-coded maple corner is garden-specific; a checker's mask and the integrator's mask gave different palette numbers, so name the mask; 'the squint test missed' was never accepted or fixed: decide who may accept it.

techniques.name: B17. Concept images as targets for character (paid), and how to spend the image budget
techniques.what_it_is: Paid image generation was used to see what the added character should look like before building: paint-overs of the two views, element sheets (bridge construction, planks, roof, trees, pond edge, lantern, grass and moss) and swatches.
techniques.why_it_matters: The person said: 'Generate an image of trees and so on in the art style and work from that.' Builders worked from these as guides for shapes, not as textures.
techniques.how_to_do_it: (1) Put the person's rule sentence into the prompt: 'a moss patch is one soft rounded shape, a crack is one clean dark line, a peg is one small round shape, a grass tuft is 5 to 9 simple blades'. (2) Ask for element sheets that explain construction (side view plus plan plus three details of the bridge; six plank studies; roof with chips, slipped tile, moss in valleys, drip stains; pond with shallow pebble edge). (3) Keep what builds: positions of posts, plank wear shapes, designed moss blobs; do not copy outline strokes, blurry ground texture, a moon in the sky, rows of studs, glossy wet streaks, railings the real scene does not have. (4) Swatches: seam-test with the half-shift test; use as colour pictures only after grading, and only their marks (knot, check, mould blotch) not the tile; send the style board only (sending the hero picture makes the painter paste it in). (5) Price check with the live price before every call, a ledger row (time, step, model and settings, price, request id, running total), person's request passed word for word, only pictures of the scene or the style board sent, never a name or email. (6) Each builder gets a small extra allowance with a written reason (US$1.00 here, one call each).
techniques.measured_results: MEASURED/BILLED: 29 calls (4 Nano Banana Pro at US$0.15, 24 Nano Banana 2 at US$0.12 for 2K, 1 Flux 3 at up to US$0.383) = US$3.86 worst case of the US$15 budget; fal's request history matched the 29 ledger rows exactly. Painter choice: Nano Banana 2 with the rule sentence kept the style; Pro was too photographic; Flux 3 moved the composition (up to US$0.38 to find out). Concept pictures match the original layout only 0.84-0.92 (edge-structure correlation), so they are looks to follow, not overlays; detail energy of the best concept 6.3/5.9/3.6/7.8/8.9/3.4/3.2 against the original 8.1/5.4/3.6/8.5/7.6/3.4/3.6.
techniques.traps_and_failures: A message sent to the concept helper woke a second copy that made 8 extra paid calls (about US$0.70) before it stopped, and all 8 were made before the 'part of the design' rule reached it; instructions 'no posts above the deck' were only partly obeyed; several concepts added things (a moon, a ghost of the house, turquoise water).

techniques.name: B18. The renderer rule, EEVEE against Cycles, Cycles on the card, and light groups
techniques.what_it_is: The person's rule: Cycles where lamps, windows or fires are lit; EEVEE when they are off. Measured side by side on the wet street.
techniques.why_it_matters: It decides cost and mood; plain code will otherwise pick one engine for everything.
techniques.how_to_do_it: (1) Choose per scene: lit lamps, windows, lanterns, fires, glowing paper or wet reflections: Cycles. Unlit or quick geometry looks: EEVEE. (2) For Cycles on a card: set prefs.compute_device_type to OPTIX (then CUDA, HIP, oneAPI, Metal), enable only those devices, scene.cycles.device = 'GPU', print the devices, and stop with --require-gpu if none; the saved scene may say CPU because the choice lives in the preferences, not the file; prove with one tiny picture first. (3) Finals about 384-512 samples with a denoiser, caustics off, AgX with the look the old picture used; record engine, device, samples, seed, view transform, exposure, size, camera, seconds, Blender version and SHA-256 of the scene and outputs next to every picture; keep failed attempts. (4) Light groups (sun, sky, cool fill, glow of lit rooms, lantern) in a multi-layer EXR beside the PNG so glow can be rebalanced for free; check that the groups add up. (5) EEVEE in this plugin: shadow memory must be big enough, a log with 'Shadow buffer full' or 'Could not allocate shadow atlas' is a failed picture (plan_lights.py render-log); under a virtual screen locally; on a rented card no virtual screen is needed. (6) Value work on small previews first (1200x800 at 96 samples took 6-10 s on a 4090).
techniques.measured_results: MEASURED (log 26, same file, camera, lights): main street wet 3.7 s EEVEE against 14.1 s Cycles, lockout plate 2.8 against 25.3 s, close cottage 1.6 against 15.4 s; wet ground, lamps and house fronts mirrored in puddles and gutters only in Cycles; road brightness 0.336 against 0.183 (warm light reaches the road); clean gutter water in Cycles, sandy grain in EEVEE; EEVEE joints a little crisper; Cycles leaves true dark (6-7 percent crushed against about 1.5); EEVEE streets cold blue, Cycles warm gold, and the painter follows the mood; the cause is mostly one EEVEE setting (light threshold 0.01 against 0.0001 in the study's jobs): lowering it brings EEVEE close but as slow as Cycles; bricks and walls looked about the same (0.86-1.22 times). Garden finals 44.3 s and 39.7 s on a 4090.
techniques.traps_and_failures: Unexplained: the fire drum lit orange in Cycles only, a bright speck at one roof corner in wet Cycles only, sky dome and some glowing meshes darkened Cycles; not tested: moving pictures (denoising may flicker) and whether the painter paints better from Cycles pictures. Light fields like transmission and volume factor did nothing in 5.1.2 Cycles, so use object ray visibility to separate things. The Scenario texturing skill defaults to EEVEE finals, which contradicts the rule.

techniques.name: B19. Working on a small shared computer, money, privacy and safety rules
techniques.what_it_is: Habits that kept the job safe on a computer with about 2.5 GB free and a shared bill.
techniques.why_it_matters: Several failures here cost time or money, and one leaked a personal detail.
techniques.how_to_do_it: (1) Keep big files (.blend, EXR, large PNG) on the rented store; download only JPG previews under 400 KB and small JSON; one downloaded folder of full-size PNGs cost 11-20 MB each time and was deleted at once; if free space falls under 0.4 GB, stop and report. (2) Small tests only here: tiny CPU Cycles pictures (the normal test: seconds), Workbench previews, structural proofs; a small EEVEE picture of a hooked scene took over 3 minutes; run Blender with -t 2 when six helpers share the machine. (3) Stop a job by the process number you saved, never pkill -f (it stopped the session's own shell). (4) Money: price before every paid call, ledger row per call, check fal's request history against the ledger, a per-helper cap, 'a vague reply is not a yes'. Check the RunPod balance before long jobs. (5) PRIVACY: a helper once wrote the person's email into the identity line of two download scripts and two outside websites received it with each request (log 28); never put a name, email or personal detail into any request, header, prompt or file; the Poly Haven fetch uses a generic agent name only; plugin.json and README line 15-16 already carry a personal handle (pre-existing; ask the person). Never read, print, copy or move anything in ~/.runpod; no key or id in notes, prompts, logs or the plugin; the plugin's push check (plan_budget.py push) refuses files that look like keys but knows no RunPod pattern. (6) Never change the film project from a helper; keep the old file beside a new one so going back is a few renames.
techniques.measured_results: MEASURED: local disk fell to 392 MB once (65 MB of stale tar files in /tmp, a 123 MB npm cache cleared); disk now 2.8 GB free; RunPod hourly bill for the garden character job US$10.89; a test machine about 3 US cents; storage about US$0.006 an hour for two stores.
techniques.traps_and_failures: Container restarts (twice) end background jobs silently; a RunPod balance of US$0.13 stalled all jobs for about an hour; two checkers' wrong test and one false 'recovered after purge' claim sit in the record.

techniques.name: B20. Blender 5.2.2 traps found while building (a checklist for the kit)
techniques.what_it_is: API and behaviour traps each found or confirmed by a build or checker.
techniques.why_it_matters: A smaller model reinvents these mistakes one by one.
techniques.how_to_do_it: (1) Generated images: set colour space right after images.new and before writing pixels; never again. (2) Image rows in Blender run bottom-up, numpy rows top-down (flip). (3) Geometry nodes: a multi-input socket reads links in reverse; end in Realize Instances before applying; count realised triangles against what you meant. (4) use_auto_smooth is gone (4.1+): Smooth by Angle or set_sharp_from_angle. (5) modifiers.new('ARRAY') is the legacy Array; the new 5.x Array, Curve to Tube and Scatter are node-group assets not available from a bare script. (6) Principled v2: Subsurface Weight, Specular IOR Level, Coat, Emission Strength default 0 (a set colour with strength 0 does not glow); Mix node by name (A, B, Result), by index only if you must (RGBA A=6, B=7, Result=2). (7) Bump Distance default is 0.001 since 4.5 (nearly flat): 0.01-0.1 for a one-unit tile and Filter Width 1-4 for steps; Bump Distance is a real height, lower it rather than Strength. (8) Bevel, AO, Pointiness and Random Per Island are Cycles-only and stochastic: EEVEE shows no Bevel edges; bake before thresholding. (9) Noise does not tile; use 4D donut noise. (10) Set the displacement method on the material. (11) An Attribute node reading a missing custom property gets 0. (12) Replacement objects must join the light-linking receiver collections. (13) Images made by a script are not saved with the .blend: pack or save them. (14) Cycles device is a preference, not a file setting. (15) Without a virtual screen Blender stops with 'Couldn't open libEGL.so.1' as soon as anything draws locally (xvfb-run -a). (16) Headless: --python-exit-code 1, --disable-autoexec, --factory-startup. (17) bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings is refused inside the MCP sandbox (use read_homefile(use_empty=True, use_factory_startup=True)). (18) The Blender program's Python has numpy but no Pillow and no OpenCV. (19) Coplanar faces flicker or render black: keep 1-2 cm apart; horizontal quad panels need the ground not at exactly the same height. (20) View transform: Standard for colour pictures, Raw for data maps; AgX turned a photographed 0.5 into 0.667. (21) Mirror-tiled normal maps need a channel flip. (22) The weathering kit's reader needs system cv2, appended by masks.ensure_cv2().

techniques.name: B21. What to carry from the Scenario Blender skills (MIT) and what not
techniques.what_it_is: Seven Scenario skills are installed in the project (not in the plugin): expert, texturing and shading, UV and baking, geometry nodes, lighting and rendering, export, previs. They carry an MIT licence file each, edited to say 'do not install anything'.
techniques.why_it_matters: They hold the best generic checks, but their defaults conflict with the person's rules and the project's lessons.
techniques.how_to_do_it: Carry ideas or scripts with the LICENSE file and a note of origin (Scenario Inc., MIT, version 0.59.0, commit 6e7b8c3 of 20 Oct 2026). Worth carrying: the delivery gate (bx_audit.deliverable: floating parts and fragments, closed parts inside out, negative scale, z-fighting, unapplied scale, faces into a part, duplicate faces, no UV under an image texture; profiles game, render, print, roblox); value_report (albedo 30-243 sRGB under 2 percent outside, metal above 180, fractional metallic under 5 percent, roughness spread above 0.01); audit_material (colour spaces by role, no image straight into Normal, explicit UV maps, Bump Distance at most 0.05, normal plus displacement flagged, non-Cubic displacement image, Noise Detail above 6); the scatter builder with counting checks; light-and-dark study and a colour-setting audit. Stance lines worth quoting: data maps are Non-Color; masks not painted colour; micro detail in roughness; judge in honest light in both engines; bake after thresholding. Do not carry: the EEVEE default, 'never both' without the displacement nuance, subject verdicts built for faces, fixed review views that suit one object, the web export that squeezes shapes (up to 52 mm), the live-window and add-on parts.

design.plan:
DESIGN FOR PLUGIN 1.4.0 (explainer-film): SURFACES, WEAR AND CONSTRUCTION

0. THE IDEA IN ONE PARAGRAPH
Today the plugin says almost nothing about surfaces and wear. The inventory reader built a deliberately flat hut (three plain-colour boxes, no normal maps, no wear) with the plugin's own model kit and the plugin's own model_lint printed Verdict PASS, exit 0. So a smaller model asked 'build a village in the forest' makes flat boxes and stops. Version 1.4.0 carries what the project learned over the last days (real normal maps proven to point the right way, displacement, roughness and colour variation, dirt, grime, weathering, wetness, cracks, chips, edge wear, moss, rust, weeds, rubbish, believable construction, real sizes, the style rule, picture measures, fresh checkers, cheap Cycles on rented cards) and makes it automatic in four ways: (1) ROUTING: the skills a model reads first make the surface-and-wear pass and the construction check required steps, and their descriptions carry the words so they get picked; (2) ONE COMMAND PER JOB: `explainer-film-place VERB` backed by a generic kit (`kit/place-kit/`), settings per place, presets for looks and surfaces; (3) A PREFLIGHT STAGE called `place` that FAILS when a material or the scene lacks a required treatment; (4) A WORKFLOW `build-a-place` that builds a place in parts with owners and fresh checkers. Everything is generic: no town, harbour, mine, farm, garden, interior or forest word may sit in code (a lint enforces it); places differ only in their settings file, look and facts table.

1. WORDS (one word for each thing; every file uses these and no others)
- role: what an object is (for example wall.timber_frame, ground.dirt_road). Every visible mesh gets exactly one role.
- owner: the builder (one agent) responsible for a part. part: one piece of the place built by one owner (roads, cottages, stable, props, forest).
- surface: a recipe that makes a material (height picture, normal strength, displacement depth, roughness range, colour palette, tile size). Ids like dirt_road, thatch, timber_weathered.
- layer: one wear effect put on a material (dirt, grime, weathering, wetness, cracks_and_chips, edge_wear, moss_and_algae, rust, rubbish). 3D pieces (plants, litter pieces) are scattered separately.
- treatment: a thing the audit checks for. Sixteen of them (names fixed below). A layer or a surface step makes a treatment; the audit lists, per material and per object, which treatments it has.
- look: a mood preset of dial values (kept, lived_in, neglected, derelict). state: dry, damp or wet.
- mask: a 'where-picture': a number for every place on the ground or object that says where dirt gathers, where water stands, where feet walk, where nothing may grow.
- the pass: tag roles, shape roads, give surfaces, age, grow, set picture size, check construction, audit. 'finish' runs the whole pass.
- audit: place-audit.json, the facts table of the scene. judge: calculators/place_audit_check.py, which turns the audit into pass, look or fail using house numbers.
- store: the rented card's saved folder. preview / final: a small / a full-size picture. fresh checker: a helper who did not build the thing and recomputes its claims.

2. THE PIECES AND WHO BUILDS THEM (folders never overlap; the three builders run at the same time)
(a) SKILLS AND DOCS owns: skills/**, README.md, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, /home/user/Music/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json, kit/docs/**, kit/kit-sync-notes.md, kit/place-kit/data/templates/*.md and *.json (prose and format templates), kit/calculators/tests/test_place_skills.py and its fixtures.
(b) KIT CODE owns: kit/place-kit/** (except data/templates/*.md|json), bin/explainer-film-place, bin/explainer-film-preflight, bin/explainer-film-setup, kit/calculators/{place_audit_check.py, picture_measures.py, preflight.py, plan_budget.py (push guard only), README.md}, kit/film-settings.json, kit/paper-film/blender/{model_lint.py, model_kit.py, textures.py}, optionally kit/calculators/{paint_request.py, templates/paint-prompt.txt}, and the tests test_place_data.py, test_place_roles.py, test_place_audit_check.py, test_picture_measures.py, test_preflight_place.py, test_place_blender.py, test_place_combine.py, test_place_render.py plus edits to test_house_rules.py, plus fixtures under kit/calculators/tests/fixtures/place/.
(c) WORKFLOW owns: workflows/build-a-place.js, agents/place-planner.md, place-builder.md, place-integrator.md, place-renderer.md, place-checker.md, kit/calculators/tests/test_build_a_place_workflow.py, tests/workflow_harness.mjs, fixtures under tests/fixtures/place-workflow/.
Agreement rule: the names in ENTRY POINTS below are the contract. If a builder must change a name, keep the old one working as an alias and write the change in kit/place-kit/DEVIATIONS.md (builder (b) creates it empty; (a) and (c) read it last and fix their text). A cross-check test (test_place_skills.py, owner (a)) fails when a skill or agent names a verb, option, file or house number that does not exist.

3. A PLAIN REQUEST WALKED THROUGH (concrete example first)
Request, verbatim: 'Build a village in the forest. Needs unkept dirt roads like they've been driven down by horse and carriage, an empty stable, a few cottages, some scattered mediaeval props.' Nothing about surfaces. What happens with 1.4.0:
1. The model's skill list shows make-3d-models, build-and-paint-a-place and surfaces-wear-and-construction. All three descriptions name 'village', 'build ... in Blender' and the surface words, so one of them loads. The first screen of each says: REQUIRED for every place you build (block text below).
2. It runs the workflow build-a-place (or follows the same steps by hand). The planner splits the village into parts (roads_and_ground, cottages, stable, props, forest_edge), writes a facts table (door heights, cart gauge, thatch pitch, each with number, source, confidence), a style note, a draft place-settings.json and an ownership table.
3. Each builder shapes its part with the kit's part helpers (every object gets place_owner and place_role; things are seated on ground_height_at; planks on supports), runs `explainer-film-place finish-part --owner NAME`, and returns claims.
4. The integrator combines the parts (both orders), runs `explainer-film-place finish` (surfaces, ruts and hoof prints, wear, growth) and `explainer-film-place audit`. `explainer-film-preflight place` must PASS before any picture is drawn.
5. The renderer applies the person's rule (lit lantern or window: Cycles on a rented card; otherwise EEVEE), draws previews, measures them and makes the style guard from the first honest picture.
6. Fresh checkers (look, structure, process, and a blind reader) recompute; a skeptic ranks; one fix round by owners; re-check; plain report.

4. WHAT IS CARRIED, REWRITTEN, NOT CARRIED (all sources are the person's own work unless marked; no third-party code is carried)
CARRY AND MAKE GENERIC (builder (b); read first the story file '/home/user/Music/procedural-textures/Procedural textures - project story.md' and '/home/user/Music/procedural-textures/kits/weathering/HOW TO USE.md'):
- weathering core: /home/user/Music/procedural-textures/kits/weathering/apply/{kit,hook,chain,adapters,nodes,layer_template,roles,settings,dials,seed}.py and dial_table.json; apply_weathering.py's one-door idea (apply, set_master, set_layer_master, set_dials, layer_off/on, set_state, report, remove) and DataSnapshot restore.
- layers from walls/{soot,runoff,foot,wallcracks,wallgrowth,walls_common}.py, ground/{dirt,groundcracks,groundmoss,iron,ground_common}.py, growth/{pieces,scatter}.py and species.json; wetness from /home/user/Music/procedural-textures/street_wet/tools/wetness_layer.py (generic code, street numbers dropped); rubbish from street_wet/relief_and_rubbish/rubbish/tools/rubbish_layer.py and rubbish_pieces.py (structure and dial names only; the street's coordinates are not carried).
- mask maths that need only numpy: masks/{footfall,habitat,shade,geom,grid,names,scale}.py.
- tests and lint ideas: harness/lint_no_set_names.py, harness/selftests.py (dial_zero, isolation, determinism, reuse_smoke), harness/test_measures.py (made-up-picture tests).

NOT CARRIED: the OpenCV mask-pack reader (masks/reader.py, make_pack.py, 25 to 80 s a scene; replaced by a lighter numpy-only plan mask, see D4); everything tied to one street or one photo (rubbish_layer numbers, make_places_pictures.py, make_joint_pictures.py, the 1926 look, painter_survival_fit.json, integrate/legacy_*, harness/baseline, .remote_state.json); anything Astra-bound (r_tiles.py, g6_moss.remap_astra_moss, stage_life.py, the pigment tool, life/ship/addon_copy; /tmp/.../astra-upload* and astra-work are never read); render_client_cached.py, direct_to_machine.py, render_job_server*.py, diagnose/*.py and harness/remote.py's fixed client path; anything in ~/.runpod. Poly Haven pictures are CC0 and fetched at run time (generic agent name, no personal data), never shipped.

5. DECISIONS (each says why; kind in brackets)
D1 One door. A plain-Python launcher (kit/place-kit/place_command.py, wrapped by bin/explainer-film-place) parses arguments, finds Blender (BLENDER, then machine-settings.env beside the kit, then PATH) and runs `blender -b --disable-autoexec SCENE --python blender_run.py -- VERB ...`. Code inside Blender uses only bpy, numpy and the standard library (measured by the inventory reader: Blender 5.2.2's own Python has no Pillow and no OpenCV; model_kit.py fails there with ModuleNotFoundError: PIL). Plain-Python tools (judge, measures) may use numpy and Pillow (setup already requires them; I checked this machine: Python 3.13.16, numpy 2.5.3, Pillow 12.3.0, OpenCV 5.0.0).
D2 Facts and verdicts are separate. Blender writes facts (place-audit.json); plain Python judges with house numbers from kit/film-settings.json. So thresholds live in one table and judge tests need no Blender.
D3 Treatments are named; roles.json says which are REQUIRED (fail) or WANTED (look) per role class. Only treatments that the kit really implements and tests may be REQUIRED. Skipping one is allowed only as an explicit entry in the settings file's 'off' list with a reason (and an amount of 0 with no 'off' entry fails). This is what stops silent skipping.
D4 Where-pictures (masks): the proven weathering masks need a 25 to 80 s OpenCV run per scene. 1.4.0 keeps the mask NAMES and FORMULAS (lowness, crown, wall_dist, prop_dist, sheltered, shade, dampness, footfall, keepclear, above_water, litter_dist) but makes them with a numpy-only 'plan mask': a few ray casts from above and sideways on a grid (cell 0.10 m, 0.5 m with --quick), written as small pictures (packed into the .blend) that materials look up by world x and y; wall foot comes from world z minus the ground height picture; edge from the object's own bounds; sheltered under eaves from a per-object pk_top_z. THIS LIGHTER ROUTE IS NOT TESTED ANYWHERE YET (judged by the inventory reader). Acceptance tests below (isolation, dial zero, determinism, keep-out counts) decide; if they fail, builder (b) records it in DEVIATIONS.md and falls back to carrying masks/reader.py behind a flag.
D5 Layer order is fixed (measured on the street): A before water: dirt, grime; then wetness; then cracks_and_chips and edge_wear (stay dull when wet); then moss_and_algae; then rubbish last; rust inside slot A for iron; 3D plants and litter are separate objects.
D6 Geometry and normal maps lead; shader layers stay calm. The re-check of the weathering kit said that at film size it added little a viewer could see except rust and a few weeds, while the garden's designed geometry plus real normal maps gave the visible character. So the surface step (real normal maps, displacement, bevels, shaped ruts, damage as shape) is the first and largest piece, and layers follow the budgets: dark grime on about a quarter of an area and a third darker, pale marks first on dark surfaces, the darkest part of a mark at 0.10 or above, marks sized in picture dots (set_picture_size).
D7 Normal map and displacement together (a conflict in the sources: the Scenario skill says never both; the coal mine used both with normal strength x 0.6; the cookbook measured no doubling). Decision [judged]: a real normal map carries fine grain on every surface; displacement is used only where roles.json says (dirt road, mud, thatch, rock ground) and the mesh is dense or adaptive; where displacement is on, normal strength is multiplied by 0.6. test_place_blender.py renders one low-angle test of both and records the result in DEVIATIONS.md.
D8 Renderer rule (the person's words): Cycles where lamps, windows, lanterns or fires are lit; EEVEE when they are off. One `render` verb applies it; `renderer-for` explains it. The rented-card client reads the user's own settings at run time and never prints or stores them. If jobs wait more than 5 minutes while workers show idle, stop and report; never purge the queue or change the endpoint.
D9 Fresh checkers get the request, the style note, the acceptance list, the scene and the pictures, NOT the builders' reports or numbers. They get the builders' CLAIMS as bare sentences to recompute. They say whether they were blind. A squint-test miss is reported plainly and never 'fixed' by removing character; the person or an accepted entry decides.
D10 Parallel safety: owners, stage_<owner>.py files with apply(options) that are idempotent and restore what they changed, copy-never-edit for shared materials, a fingerprint of the whole scene after every stage, an ownership diff, combine in plain and reverse order.
D11 No third-party code is carried. The delivery-gate ideas of the Scenario skills are rewritten in our own words (floating, inside-out, z-fight, unapplied scale, missing UV). If a builder does copy any third-party code anyway, the licence file and a note of where it came from travel with it (kit/place-kit/SOURCES-AND-LICENCES.md).
D12 The plugin stays standalone: no folder outside the plugin named in code; tests skip with a plain reason (exit 77) when Blender or node is missing, never fail.

6. ORDER OF WORK AND STOP LINES
Builder (b), in this order (a stop after any numbered step must leave a coherent, tested kit; the audit must never require what is not implemented):
 1 data model: names.py, house_numbers.py, settings_file.py, roles.py, data/*.json, check-presets, the lint, film-settings sections, test_place_data/test_place_roles.
 2 the gates: scene_read.py, checks/{construction,scale,scene_audit,normals_test}.py, calculators/place_audit_check.py, preflight stage place, bin/explainer-film-place + place_command.py + blender_run.py, tests that make the flat hut FAIL. (Stop line: the flat hut fails with named treatments.)
 3 surfaces: heights, normals, uvs, materials, bevel, displacement, ground_mesh, roads (ruts, hoof). Hut test: finish makes the audit pass for normal_map, roughness_variation, colour_variation, bevelled_edges, displacement.
 4 wear: carried core, plan mask, the nine layers, dials, age_place. Tests: dial zero, isolation, determinism, undo, visible effect.
 5 growth: pieces, scatter, keep-out counts.
 6 parts and combine: parts.py, undo.py, checks/{fingerprint,ownership,combine}.py, stage_template.py.
 7 picture measures, crops, guard.
 8 rendering: renderer_choice, render_job, client with a fake transport test.
 9 extras: model_lint --surfaces, model_kit fixes, setup regex, push guard pattern, paint-prompt keep-wet option, worn_wood helpers if time.
Builder (a): write against the names here. Order: the new skill and its first screen, the three edits that route to it, the tips guide and README, then the reference files, then the example, then the cross-check test. Builder (c): agents first, then the workflow, then the harness test.

7. RULES FOR ALL THREE BUILDERS (from the hard rules)
Write only inside the plugin and your own scratch folder .../scratchpad/plugin-work/<your step>/. Never commit or push. Never read, print, copy or move anything in ~/.runpod; no key, endpoint id, machine id or volume id in any file; no personal name, email or detail in any file or request (a test scans every new file for email-like strings, '.runpod', long hex ids and key-looking words; the person's existing handle in plugin.json and README is not touched). Plain everyday words, one word per thing, a concrete example before a general rule, say measured versus judged. Code: full plain-word names (remove_empty_rows, not rmEmpty), and a plain note at the top of every file that starts 'What this does'. New files get plain-word names. Disk here is about 2.8 GB free and shared: big files (.blend, EXR, big PNG) stay on the rented store; tests make tiny pictures (64 x 64) and tiny scenes. Baseline before you start (reported by the inventory reader; re-run it yourself): python3 kit/calculators/tests/run_all.py gives 25 files, 22 pass, 1 fail (test_preflight.py: the film stage wants 4 GB free disk and this machine has less; not a fault of ours), 2 skipped; it must give the same one failure and your new files passing when you finish.

files.contents: Front matter, exactly: name: surfaces-wear-and-construction | description: The finishing pass that every place, set or prop built in Blender must go through, whatever the request says: real normal maps and displacement, roughness and colour variation, dirt, grime, stains, weathering, wetness, moss, weeds, rust, cracks, chips, edge wear, damage and rubbish, believable construction (every plank on a support, every support on the ground, nothing floating), real-world sizes, and the place's art-style rule; done by one command (explainer-film-place finish) and proved by a material-and-scene audit (preflight stage place). Use whenever someone asks to build, model or improve a village, town, harbour, mine, farm, garden, interior, street, building, cottage, stable, road or props in Blender, even if they never mention surfaces, textures, wear or realism, and before drawing, rendering or painting any such place. | when_to_use: Any request to make a place, set, building or props in Blender, and before any picture of one is drawn. Body, under 250 lines for smaller models, in this order: (1) the REQUIRED block (exact text in ENTRY POINTS K) as the first thing after the title; (2) a concrete example in 8 lines: the forest village request and what the pass did to it (ruts with hoof prints, thatch with moss, silvered timber, stone footings with moss, barrels with rust bands, nettles at wall feet), pointing to a-forest-village-example.md; (3) 'The words' (the glossary of the plan, five lines); (4) 'The commands' (a table of the 21 verbs: one line each with its main options, no option that is not in ENTRY POINTS A); (5) 'Stop lines': you may not draw, render, paint or call the place built until `explainer-film-preflight place` passes; never lower a requirement to pass; the only allowed ways to skip a treatment are an 'off' entry with a reason in place-settings.json or a signed accepted entry (who, date) in the preflight plan; never tell the user about the pass unless asked, just do it; (6) 'Where a smaller model skips it and what stops that': the 15-row table from how_it_becomes_automatic, as short rows 'you will be tempted to ... / what happens'; (7) 'Rules that conflict and which wins' (displacement and normal map together: D7; Cycles when lit; painter template words for wet places; bump only is not enough; the glTF-has-no-displacement rule is for the three.js card route only); (8) 'Read next': the other reference files, one line each. Every kit file named in backticks must exist (the setup script checks names that start with place-kit/, so write them as `place-kit/...`).

The step-by-step. Steps: 0 write the place's style note, facts table and place-settings.json from the templates in place-kit/data/templates (or let the workflow planner do it); 1 plan parts and owners, one collection 'Place: <owner>' each; 2 shape the parts with the part helpers (begin_part, new_part_object with role and owner, seat_on_ground, ground_height_at, is_keep_clear), real sizes from the facts table, bevels, supports under everything; 3 `explainer-film-place new-settings` then `roles` until no object is unknown (fix by adding a match rule or tagging place_role); 4 `finish` (or `finish-part --owner NAME` per part, then the integrator runs `finish`); use --quick for local trials; 5 read the audit lines FAIL/LOOK/PASS and fix by category (missing treatment: run the verb named in the fix text; floating part: move or add a support; unknown role; stale audit: run audit again after any change); 6 `normals-test` and `construction` for detail; 7 `renderer-for`, draw previews with `render`, `measure --make-guard` on the first honest picture; 8 fresh checkers (workflow build-a-place does steps 5 to 8); 9 `explainer-film-preflight place` PASS, then go on to shots and plates; 10 report in plain words: what was done, what was measured versus judged, what was not tested, every failure. Include a section 'The shortcuts that fail' with the real cases: flat boxes pass model lint; bump only; normal map with flipped green or sRGB colour space; no UVs; displacement node with the material still on Bump Only or on a flat plane; a layer with amount 0 or a missing pk_<layer>_amount property (an Attribute node on an object with no such property reads 0 so the layer is silently off); weeds on the wheel tracks or in puddles; a stale audit after edits; photographic noise instead of a few big designed marks. Include commands with full examples using the village (explainer-film-place finish --scene village.blend --settings place-settings.json --look neglected --state damp --save-as village-finished.blend).

Surface by surface (example first, then the rule). Start with the dirt road: a 2 m tile, soft clod height picture blurred 1 to 2 px at 2048, normal strength 0.8 to 1.0, displacement 6 cm where the mesh is graded (0.12 m squares near the camera growing 1.09 times a step to 5 m), roughness 0.85 to 0.95 dry and about 0.3 in wet ruts, palette dull brown with a few big darker patches. Then one short section each for packed_earth, mud, forest_floor, grass, timber_weathered, timber_planks, log_wall, wattle_and_daub plaster, stone_rubble, thatch (bunch ridges, displacement 4 to 6 cm near camera, strength x 0.6), shingle, clay roof tile, iron_forged, straw and hay, wicker, cloth sack, rope, ceramic, bark, foliage cards, still water, old glass. Each section: how the height is made (soft and large: nothing under about 5 mm, no micro pores), normal strength, displacement depth or none, tile size in metres, UV method (box per face, planar for ground and water, plank: u along the length, v across, random offset per plank, mirror or rotate some planks and switch a knot off on about half, roof tile: UV on the prototype), roughness range, palette note as value range, how repeats are hidden (second lookup at 0.79 scale offset 0.37 and 0.58 blended by slow noise, per-object tint and offset). State the kind of every number: measured (cookbook relief tests, street wet recipe: dry roughness about 0.9, wet about 0.3), judged (garden strengths: moss 0.45, stone 0.8 to 1.0, roof tile 0.9, bark 0.9, plaster 1.0, ground 1.0, planks 1.5; mine depths: mud 6 cm, gravel 4, slate 4, brick 3, wood 3, metal 1.6) or invented. Rules: colour maps sRGB, data maps Non-Color; OpenGL normals (green up); set the colour space right after images.new and before writing pixels (Blender 5.2.2 wipes a generated image to black otherwise); Bump Distance default is nearly flat; never set Strength where the real fix is Distance. Poly Haven section: the slugs read on 22 October 2026 (textures: brown_mud, brown_mud_02, brown_mud_03, brown_mud_dry, brown_mud_leaves_01, brown_mud_rocks_01, forrest_ground_01, forrest_ground_03, forest_ground_05, forest_leaves_02, grass_path_2, leafy_grass, thatch_roof_angled, reed_roof_03, reed_roof_04, riet_01, clay_plaster, clay_roof_tiles, castle_wall_slates, cobblestone_01 to 05, bark_brown_01, bark_brown_02, brick_moss_001; models: Barrel_01, Barrel_02, barrel_03, wine_barrel_01, wooden_bucket_01 and 02, wooden_crate_01 and 02, wicker_basket_01 and 02, wooden_ladder, wooden_ladder_02, tree_stump_01 and 02, dead_tree_trunk and 02, fir_sapling, fir_sapling_medium, fir_tree_01, Lantern_01, wooden_lantern_01, jug_01, metal_jug, spinning_wheel_01, rusted_wheel_rim_01 and 02; NOT found: cart, hay or straw bales, trough, anvil, well, stable stalls, thatched cottage: script those). Say: pick a photo surface by drawing a small test plate, open every downloaded picture at full size and look for stickers, brands and digits (judgement), and remember scans alone read bland: designed marks and geometry go on top.

Where each kind of wear goes, how much, how big, in which order. Start with the concrete example: an unkept lane driven by a horse and cart: two wheel ruts a gauge apart (cart gauge about 1.2 to 1.5 m, judged, confirm in the facts table), each rut 12 to 20 cm wide and 5 to 15 cm deep (invented; the mine yard used 4 to 9 cm), a raised bank beside each rut (about 0.3 of the depth), a trodden centre strip with hoof dimples about 12 to 14 cm across every 0.8 to 1.0 m (invented), a grass crown between the wheel lines on a lightly used lane, puddles in the low rut bottoms, dried rings round old puddles, dung lumps and straw near the edges, weeds and nettles on the verge, and nothing growing in the wheel tracks (exact zero). Then the layers in their fixed order with the person's words: dirt (soil film, mud splash at wall feet, dust, polish on worn lanes, dried puddle rings); grime (soot on thatch above hearths, run-off streaks under eaves and sills, damp bands, tide marks, stains); weathering (silvering of timber, sun fade, bleaching, patina); wetness (darker, smoother, film coat, puddles by depth; roughness map does the work, not the specular map; no shine on walls); cracks_and_chips (split planks, plaster loss, chipped stone corners, thatch sag); edge_wear (worn bevels, pale rubbed edges); moss_and_algae (damp plus shade, never on trodden or keep-clear dots); rust (iron: height bands, collars at joins, runs below); rubbish (leaf litter, straw, wet straw, mud, dung at wall feet, gutters and the lane edge, never on the crown); 3D plants and litter pieces (nettle, fern, bramble, tufts, leaves, sticks, needles, dung lumps; chunky designed shapes). Numbers with their kind: grime budget about a quarter of an area at about a third darker (measured on the street; more is mush); keep the darkest part of a mark at 0.10 or above and its surround at 0.18 (measured, painted plates); marks sized in picture dots: marks 5 dots at contrast 0.08, lines 3 dots at 0.11, patches 15 dots at 0.04 (measured, painted plates only); pale first on dark surfaces; exact-zero gates for plants: footfall 0.6, crown 0.7, keepclear 0.5; plants in puddles 0; litter clearance 5 cm; rubbish on the crown 0 (measured). Say what each look does (kept, lived_in, neglected, derelict) and how to switch state dry, damp, wet. Honest note: at film size on dark, edge-on walls soot, run-off and damp bands mostly vanish (measured on the street); make walls' marks few, big and pale-first, and lean on normal maps, shape and 3D plants.

Concrete first: the garden bridge. It 'made no sense' (boxes overlapped, nothing fixed to anything). It was rebuilt bottom-up: flat footing stones on the bed, square posts 14 cm with a 1.5 cm chamfer, cross beams pegged to the posts, stringers on the beams, planks across, round pegs, a few iron cramps; no span between supports over 1.4 m. The check proved it: 59 planks, none on fewer than 2 supports, 18 posts on footings. Then the rule: build from the ground up so every visible part has a visible reason (what carries it, what it carries). Houses and sheds the same way: stone footing, sill on stone, posts on sill, wall plate, rafters on the plate, roof on rafters, floor and a threshold so a doorway looks onto something (the coal-mine engine house had a door onto nothing). Cottage and stable stacks with sizes, a fence (posts in the ground, rails on posts), a cart (axle-tree, wheel spokes, bed on the axle), a well, a trough, stable stalls. Real-world facts table method: write each fact as number, unit, source, confidence (strong, weak, guess); put the numbers in the brief as limits and in the acceptance tests; weak facts get a note so builders do not treat them as law; facts set size, the style note sets how much detail. Starter numbers for a mediaeval forest village, ALL from memory and marked judged-weak, to be confirmed or replaced by research: single-storey cottage 4 to 5 m by 6 to 8 m, eaves 2.0 to 2.4 m, thatch pitch 45 to 55 degrees, thatch 25 to 35 cm thick, door 1.6 to 1.9 m high and 0.7 to 0.9 m wide, window openings 0.4 to 0.6 m, stable stall 1.5 to 1.8 m wide and 2.4 to 3 m long, manger 0.9 to 1.1 m high, horse shoulder height 1.3 to 1.6 m, cart gauge 1.2 to 1.5 m, wide boards 20 to 30 cm. Say what the construction check measures and its numbers (judged unless stated): touching within 5 mm, rest patch of at least 16 square centimetres within 8 mm, overlap at least 4 cm, no span over 1.38 m, floating gap over 5 mm fails, coplanar faces within 1 mm fight, inside-out closed parts fail, doorway needs a floor within 0.30 m below the sill (invented), walk rays every 5 cm with steps at most 2 cm; scatter pieces (leaves, tufts, litter) are exempt on purpose and the report says why. Include 'the scene study before building': measure gaps yourself with rays (two studies once gave 6.5 and 8.5 cm for the same gap), and the traps (touching is not carried; shoji rails shortened by 3 mm made a lattice float; a light inside its glow box is blocked in Cycles).

The style rule, verbatim, first: 'These things need to be integrated into the style. So it's just part of design.' Every wear mark, moss patch, crack, joint, tuft, flower and ripple is a designed element in the place's own visual language: same simplified, slightly chunky shapes, same edge treatment, same palette, same light. Test: could it sit in a hand-painted game level next to the biggest, simplest thing without looking like it came from a more photographic picture? If it is finer, sharper, noisier or more scan-like, make fewer, bigger, cleaner shapes. One small story per hand-span, never a hundred tiny details of equal weight (about one readable feature per 5 to 10 cm on timber, 20 to 30 cm on ground, 50 cm on stone and walls; judged). Then how to write a style note (use data/templates/style_note.md): rule, form, edges and surfaces, palette (top ten colours as hex, one hot accent, new detail colours from the same family), value range as percentiles, detail per region, what the style does NOT have, checklist. For a new place with no reference picture: draw the first honest version, measure it, and make the style guard from it (explainer-film-place measure --make-guard). The measures, each with its number and kind (all judged unless said): value range (percentiles 1, 5, 25, 50, 75, 95, 99 within 0.03, 99 percent not above 0.92, mean saturation within 0.04); detail energy per region (mean of the absolute difference between 8-bit luminance and its 2 px blur; allowed 0.9 times the guard up to the smaller of 1.4 times and 10; regions come from a flat-colour picture of role classes, not hand boxes); flat 96 x 96 windows (step 48) below the sky with luminance spread under 0.010 (none; under 2 percent below 0.014); palette (at most 1 percent of pixels over saturation 0.70 outside the accent; at most 0.3 percent turquoise); squint test (structural similarity of 12 px blurred luminance against the previous round's picture, target 0.92; the garden missed it at 0.883 and 0.873 and the fix round made it worse; report it with the region that loses the most and never remove character to chase it; the person decides); silhouette overlap per group (at least 0.85; two yardsticks disagreed, say which you used); light groups sum within 2 percent of the picture (measured). Say what the measures cannot judge (a measure is not a look; the eye decides) and the reading test (at half size a blind reviewer names at least 12 of 16 features; never run blind before; the workflow runs it blind). Note the painter template conflict: 'matte painted finish' and 'never puddles or reflections' tell the painter to remove wet ground (measured on a wet street: it came back dry); wet places keep the sheen.

How to be checked honestly. Example first: in the garden a builder claimed 9.8 percent moss and mould on the planks; a fresh checker counted 0.6 percent. Another claimed 'nothing vanished'; the saved file had dropped 58 unused materials and a node group. A third said a plank normal map failed (+0.061) because its own test plane had the wrong shape; the true number was +0.55. Rules: the checker did not build the thing; gets the request, the style note, the acceptance list, the scene file and the pictures, not the builders' reports or numbers; gets the builders' claims as bare sentences and recomputes each with its own code and where possible a different formula; says plainly whether it was blind to the feature list; lists problems each with the cheapest fix and an owner; says what it did not test. A second kind checks process: money against the ledger, seconds against the reports, privacy (grep for keys, ids, '.runpod', personal details), disk, leftovers (preview cameras, unused data dropped on save). After fixes a different fresh checker compares each old finding with the new pictures and looks for new faults, because fixes make new faults. One fix round, then stop. Include the checker result shape (art_style_kept, lived_in, construction_makes_sense, each_element, claims_checked with holds and evidence, problems, should_fix_now, not_tested, was_blind, measures) exactly as in ENTRY POINTS J, the list of own scripts a checker should write (scene fingerprint, supports by down-rays, normal-map wiring and direction, UV hygiene, ownership diff, 100 percent crops with before and after strips), and the honest limits (reading test never run blind before; checkers can over-trust the builders' own test files; a checker's work can be lost in a container restart, so write results to files as you go).

The generic guide to cheap Cycles on rented cards, with no key and no id in it. Sections: (1) the person's rule, verbatim: 'Cycles looks absolutely incredible. But it could be expensive. You know what? I think it's worth it. But only for scenes where the lights are on. When they're off, eeve is fine.' So Cycles where lamps, windows, lanterns or fires are lit; EEVEE otherwise; `explainer-film-place renderer-for` applies and explains it. (2) Why: this computer is slow (a small EEVEE picture of a hooked scene took over 3 minutes; Cycles 35 to 90 s a frame on 4 cores); a rented card draws a 2400 x 1600 final in about 40 s (measured: 44.3 s and 39.7 s on an RTX 4090; previews 1200 x 800 at 96 samples 6 to 10 s). (3) How it works: a serverless endpoint; a worker starts only when a job waits and stops about 5 s after, so nothing bills while idle; cold wake 20 to 22 s, warm under 1 s; up to 3 workers; about US$1.10 an hour on a 4090 (read the live price; the bill once came out 2.5 times the work seconds and was not explained, so never promise a cost from seconds alone). (4) The one-time set-up the PERSON does, in plain steps: an account and a key that may create endpoints; one network store (30 GB) in one data centre holding Blender 5.2.2 and uploaded files; one endpoint on a plain Ubuntu image with the start command from place-kit/render/worker/start.sh, workers up to 3, idle timeout 5 s, job timeout about 1 hour, cards RTX 4090 then 5090 then 24 GB cards, the store mounted; run copy_libraries.sh once on a machine that has the store. Warn that the job taker runs any shell command sent to it, so the key is the only lock. (5) Settings at run time: environment variables RUNPOD_API_KEY and RUNPOD_ENDPOINT_ID (and RENDER_STORE_FOLDER); or RENDER_SETTINGS_FILE naming a JSON file the person keeps outside any repository; the client never prints, logs or stores them and refuses a settings file inside a git repository. Never write them into a note, prompt, log or the repository. files.contents: The surface pass, numpy and bpy only. heights.py: periodic soft height pictures by recipe id (soft_noise, earth_clods, cracked_earth, planks_grain, log_bark, plaster_blotch, stone_blocks, thatch_bunches, shingle_rows, tile_rows, iron_pits, straw_strands) from garden wood_maps.py and r_maps.py; calibrate by steepest-one-percent tilt (26 to 34 degrees) or target mean slope; nothing under about 5 mm. normals.py: height_to_normal (OpenGL, green up, wrap-around differences), make_normal_image (set colour space Non-Color BEFORE writing pixels), save, add_normal_map_nodes (UV Map to Mapping to Image (Non-Color, Repeat, Cubic) to Normal Map (Tangent, uv_map set) to Principled Normal; keep an old Bump only below 0.3 and fed by the Normal Map), mirrored tiles with channel flips, 16-bit knot pictures; check_direction test light (flat plane, orthographic camera straight down, sun 30 degrees from +X then +Y, Cycles CPU, correlation at least +0.25, flipped-green control must be negative). uvs.py: box UV per face in metres (never mirrored), planar, plank (u along, v across, random offset), prototype UV for instances, mirrored-share report. materials.py: give_surfaces: per role pick the surface, rebuild or upgrade the material in place (never edit a shared material: copy as 'PK <role> / <surface>'), per-object tint and offset, repeat hiding, roughness map or noise-driven roughness, macro colour variation, scale from the surface's tile size. displacement.py: set material.displacement_method DISPLACEMENT or BOTH, Displacement node (Midlevel 0.5, Scale = true depth), material max_vertex_displacement, adaptive subdivision with dicing 1 to 2 or a graded grid; refuses (reports) a flat plane; normal strength x 0.6 when on. ground_mesh.py: graded grid 0.12 m near the camera growing 1.09 times a step to 5 m (from the mine yard). roads.py: shape_roads from the settings polylines: two wheel ruts a gauge apart with wobble and depth variation, raised banks, trodden centre with hoof dimples, optional grass crown, puddle hollows, vertex attributes for wet and rut; keeps the shape a pure numpy height function so it tests without Blender. bevel.py: Bevel modifier with harden normals plus Weighted Normal by role width (walls 0.8 to 1.5 cm, trims 6 mm, planks 6 to 12 mm). Also: a lazy PIL-free PNG writer (zlib) for use inside Blender.

The wear pass. Core carried from kits/weathering/apply: kit.py, hook.py (six-port bundle: Colour, Roughness, Specular IOR Level, Coat Weight, Normal, Metallic, plus Wet Normal; wire-or-constant splice), chain.py (ordered list rebuilt every time, so apply twice then remove gives the same node counts), adapters.py (materials made of shader groups), nodes.py, layer_template.py (Amount 0 gives exactly the input; every mix factor contains the amount; values clamped before division), dials.py (resolve from table, look, settings, per-object overrides), seed.py (random numbers from pk_seed, the Seed dial and position, never a name). Fix the seven courtyard gaps while carrying: roof geometry-node instances read their own pk_ properties (copy them to instances), a 'front' role for walls facing the camera, role multipliers honoured by EVERY layer (isolation test), lichen only on rough stone flag read, moss not brighter than stone, plinth as stone not ground, validate_look timing. masks.py: the plan mask (numpy only): ground height, lowness, crown, wall_dist, prop_dist, sheltered, shade, dampness, footfall, keepclear, above_water, litter_dist, from ray casts and footprints; written as small pictures packed in the .blend; footfall.py and habitat.py carried (shapes band_along, lines_along, polyline, rect, around_role, auto_door_strip; habitat site = formulas with exact-zero gates). Layers (one file each, nodes group 'PK <Layer>'): layer_dirt.py, layer_grime.py, layer_weathering.py (new), layer_wetness.py (generic from street wetness: darken, smoother, film coat, puddles by depth 40/40/20 percent from wobble, lowness, relief), layer_cracks_and_chips.py, layer_edge_wear.py (new; edge from object bounds, pale rubbed edge), layer_moss_and_algae.py, layer_rust.py, layer_rubbish.py. door.py: age_place(settings, look, state, owner) returning the Wear handle (set_master, set_layer_master, set_dials, layer_off, layer_on, set_state, report, remove); writes pk_<layer>_amount on every object of a role that needs the layer (the silent-zero trap) and set_picture_size(camera, height_pixels).

3D plants and litter. pieces.py: ragged chunky designed shapes built in code (tufts of 5 to 9 simple blades or folded leaves, clover, nettle, fern, bramble, moss cushion cluster with rolled edge, leaf, pine needle clump, stick, straw, dung lump), at least 8 tuft meshes, scale range at least 3 to 1, a few tints, colour pulled 45 percent toward its own grey; no seed-head ordering bug: geometry-node multi-input sockets read their links in reverse, so count realised triangles against the pick table in a test. scatter.py: Poisson scatter by probability = site x liking x gates x rubbish rule x existing-growth avoidance x distance fade, one node group per kind, pieces tagged pk_scatter so the construction check exempts them; calibrated cover (weed_cover 0.01 means about 1 percent). keepout.py: counts roots inside keep-out (footfall 0.6 or more, crown 0.7 or more, keepclear 0.5 or more), in puddles, on wheel tracks, within 5 cm of litter; writes the counts into the audit's scatter section; all must be 0.

files.contents: The checks. construction.py: loose parts and BVH trees; contact graph from ground upward by rest patch (at least 16 square centimetres within 8 mm); carried by search from the ground; floating (gap over 5 mm), short (gap between 5 mm and the part's expected carrier), hung (carried from above, allowed only for roles with may_hang), unsupported span along planks and beams by down-rays every 5 cm (longest run against the role's max_span), ground seating, doorway floor (ray down from the opening's sill centre), inside-out closed parts (negative signed volume), coplanar overlapping faces within 1 mm (z-fighting), buried lights (ray parity), walkability rays along declared routes; scatter exempt and said so; writes construction.json. Rewritten in our own words from the garden's struct.py, seat.py and bridge_check.py. scale.py: sizes against real_world_facts.json (plus the place's facts file); warn at out of range, fail beyond the fail factor. scene_audit.py: gathers the facts into place-audit.json (schema in ENTRY POINTS E): materials and objects with their treatments, roles, UV, pk_ amounts, geometry (plain box, bevel), construction, scale, scatter counts, normal map wiring, displacement, renderer decision; hashes the saved scene and the settings; refuses an unsaved scene (exit 2). normals_test.py: wiring check (Tangent, Non-Color, mean blue at least 0.85, mean red and green 0.47 to 0.53, reaches the Principled Normal, at most 4 image maps a material, UV layer on every user, mirrored share at most 2 percent, no unfed Bump above 0.3) and the test light on every unique image with the flipped control; image size from the picture, plane shape from the picture's aspect (a wrong plane once made a good map read 0). fingerprint.py: whole-scene fingerprint (objects: matrix, mesh hash with UVs, slots, modifiers, collections; materials and node groups by node and link hash; collections; light links; frozen state: render, cycles, view, world, compositor). ownership.py: diff two fingerprints against ownership.json (violations: foreign object or material changed, removed, new object without place_owner, existing node group changed, frozen state changed; warnings: new .001 names). combine.py: run stage files in order, fingerprint after each, report; plain and reverse order; idempotence run twice.

files.contents: Rendering. renderer_choice.py: renderer_for_scene returns CYCLES with reasons when any visible lamp other than the sun has energy, any visible emissive material has strength above 0 and a non-black colour, or a glow-role object exists; else EEVEE. render_job.py (Blender side): one start draws many pictures from a job file (ENTRY POINTS I): previews 1200 x 800 at 96 samples adaptive denoised, close-ups 1600 x 1067, finals 2400 x 1600 at 512; Cycles: pick OptiX then CUDA then others, print devices, stop with --require-gpu failure if none; EEVEE: shadow rays 4, steps 16, 32 to 48 samples; the render-log check for 'Shadow buffer full' or 'Could not allocate shadow atlas'; optional flat id picture using Cycles with a flat emission override (no virtual screen needed); sets the picture size on the wear layers before each picture; writes a JSON log per picture (engine, device, samples, seed, view transform, exposure, size, camera, seconds, Blender version, SHA-256 of scene and files). client.py: plain-Python rented-card client with the actions status, upload, run, job, wait, download, balance (best effort; says unknown when it cannot ask); reads RUNPOD_API_KEY and RUNPOD_ENDPOINT_ID (and RENDER_STORE_FOLDER) from the environment or from the JSON file named by RENDER_SETTINGS_FILE; never prints, logs or stores them; refuses a settings file inside a git repository; uploads folders as one bundle with checksums (skip unchanged), 6 MB pieces, a User-Agent that names the client; has a pluggable transport so tests use a fake; contains no purge call and no endpoint-changing call; stops and says so when workers show idle and jobs wait more than 5 minutes. worker/: handler.py (put, get, info, run, ping; 7 MB pieces) rewritten from the proven job taker without the session path mirroring (one store folder setting instead), start.sh (runs the handler with the Python inside Blender, so no custom image), copy_libraries.sh, cycles_check.py (one tiny picture proving OptiX). No key, id or path of the person in any of them.

A calculator in the house style (note 'What this does', --help, --json, --out, --report, --settings via calculator_output.add_output_options and finish; exit 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 input missing). Verbs: check AUDIT.json [--blend FILE.blend] [--place-settings FILE] [--facts FILE] (judges the audit with house numbers; the finding list in ENTRY POINTS F), fresh FRESH_CHECK.json [--audit AUDIT.json] (judges a fresh checker's result: a claim with holds false fails unless the finding is accepted; missing was_blind or not_tested gives a look), compare BEFORE.json AFTER.json (which treatments appeared or vanished per object). Pure Python, no bpy, no numpy needed. Prints plain lines starting FAIL, LOOK or PASS.

A calculator (house style as above) for pictures; numpy and Pillow. Verbs: measure PICTURE... [--regions FILE | --id-map PICTURE --id-colours FILE] [--previous PICTURE] (percentiles 1/5/25/50/75/95/99 of luminance 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B, mean saturation, detail energy per region, flat windows, saturated and turquoise shares, squint against a previous picture with a where-it-loses table per region), make-guard PICTURE --out GUARD.json (the guard from the first honest picture), check PICTURES... --guard GUARD.json [--previous PICTURE] (findings with check names 'place pictures: value range', '... detail energy', '... flat windows', '... palette', '... squint'; squint is a look, never a fail, unless the guard says squint_gate true), squint A B, crops PICTURE --boxes x,y,w,h ... --out-folder DIR [--previous PICTURE] (100 percent crops with before and after strips). Large pictures are shrunk with a float32 buffer (a float64 buffer once crashed the metric). Tests use made-up pictures with known answers (a flat grey has every window flat; fine noise has a known detail energy; blur lowers it; identical pictures squint 1.0).

Add the stage place exactly as in ENTRY POINTS G: STAGES (after shots), STAGE_WORDS, GUARDED, INPUTS keys (place_audit, blend, place_settings, place_pictures, previous_pictures, style_guard, real_world_facts, fresh_check), STAGE_INPUTS['place'], stage_place(run, item, where) after the pattern of stage_plates (run.need, run.run_tool of calculators/place_audit_check.py check and calculators/picture_measures.py check, run.add_check for the freshness check made inside the preflight by comparing the audit's scene_sha1 with the sha1 of --blend), STAGE_RUNNERS, build_parser (a group 'place' with the option names), EXAMPLE_PLAN['place'], the module note's stage table. In stage_plates add optional blend, place_audit, place_settings: when blend is given, place_audit becomes required and its failures block the paid painting. Existing behaviour and tests must not change when none of the new inputs is given. No change to the accepted-entry rules.

Add the sections and keys listed in ENTRY POINTS H, each as {value, unit, kind, source} with an 'about' line per section and date_read on prices; sources name the project files in the house style. The table now has 517 entries and 44 invented; the test allows invented up to a tenth of the table, so keep the new sections to at most 15 invented entries and mark the rest measured or judged with a real source. Do not change another section.

explainer-film-preflight: only the header comment (add the stage place, say nine stages). explainer-film-setup: extend the file-name regex in the embedded check from (paper-film|narration-tools|examples|docs)/ to also include place-kit/; print one line about the rented-card settings (whether RUNPOD_API_KEY and RUNPOD_ENDPOINT_ID are set, never their values; 'not set (only needed for rented cards)'); note that Blender's own Python lacks Pillow. Run it once into a scratch folder with npm unavailable and read the line 'files the skills name: N checked, 0 missing'.

Push guard only: add to SECRET_PATTERNS a RunPod key pattern (RunPod keys are believed to start with rpa_; pattern r'\brpa_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}\b', labelled 'a RunPod key (judged: format not verified against the person's own account)') and a pattern for a pasted endpoint id written as 'endpoint_id' or 'endpoint' followed by an assignment and a 12 to 40 character alphanumeric value. Add a test case to test_plan_budget.py that the pattern fires on made-up strings. No other change.
Add place_audit_check.py and picture_measures.py to the calculator list with one line each and an example call.

model_lint.py: new flag --surfaces (default off, so existing fixtures and tests do not change): for .glb files report the share of triangle area whose material has no normalTexture, no roughness variation (constant roughness and no metallicRoughness texture) and no vertex colours, as findings; FAIL above the house number place_surfaces share, LOOK below; inside Blender the same on the open scene. The preflight plates stage passes --surfaces when a place_audit is given. model_kit.py: _finish_part bevel with harden_normals=True plus a Weighted Normal modifier (the notes call the old setting wrong and build_street.py soften already does it right); import textures lazily so the module imports inside Blender's own Python without Pillow (use a numpy and zlib PNG writer when PIL is missing). textures.py: lazy PIL import; save normals as PNG not JPEG. Existing tests must still pass.

OPTIONAL, last: add a --keep-wetness option to paint_request.py request (and 'keep_wetness': true in a check file) that swaps 'matte painted finish' for 'painted finish that keeps the sheen of wet ground' in the first line and drops 'puddles or reflections' from never_rest, adding the sentence 'Keep the wet ground exactly as in image 1: its sheen, puddles, mirrored lights, joints and gutters.' Without the option the template text and every existing test stay as they are. If this cannot be done without risk to test_paint_request.py, leave the code alone and say so in DEVIATIONS.md (the skills already tell models to edit the words by hand).
