Each opens with 'What this does', uses checks.Checker, skips with exit 77 and a plain reason when Blender is missing, never names a folder outside the plugin, makes tiny pictures (64 x 64) and tiny scenes. test_house_rules.py: extend to every .py under kit/place-kit (a 'What this does' note; --help for scripts that run). Fixtures: hand-written audit JSONs (flat hut, finished hut, stale, unknown role, off without reason, amounts missing), the hut builder script, made-up pictures made at test time, a fake render transport.

The workflow in the style of build-pages.js and critique-film.js: export const meta (pure literal: name 'build-a-place', description, whenToUse, phases with the titles below), const A = args ?? {}, required-argument check, schemas, phase(), parallel(), agent(prompt, {label, phase, schema, effort}), log(). Specified in ENTRY POINTS J: args, phases (Plan, Build parts, Combine, Audit, Render, Check, Fix, Re-check, Report), every schema, the stop rules (no render unless the audit passes or fails only on accepted items; at most 2 pre-render repair rounds routed to owners; exactly one fix round after the checkers; no paid step; no commit), parts built in parallel with a cap (args.maxParallelBuilders, default 4), builders told to run only tiny tests locally and anything bigger on a rented card or with --quick, checkers get no builder reports, a blind reader plus keyword matching in the script for the reading test, a skeptic that merges and ranks findings, plain-words report returned as text (sub-agents may not be able to write report files). Uses agentType only if verified; otherwise each prompt begins 'First read ' + A.plugin + '/agents/place-<role>.md and follow it'.

Five agent files in the format of agents/page-builder.md (front matter name, description, effort: medium; the workflow may raise effort for checkers). place-planner: reads the new skill and its templates, researches facts (with sources and confidence marks; a number from memory is marked guess), writes plan/style-note.md, plan/real-world-facts.json, plan/place-settings.json (draft), plan/ownership.json, plan/acceptance.json, and returns the PLAN schema. place-builder: builds one part (or fixes one part in a fix round), only its own objects and collections, stage_<owner>.py idempotent, runs finish-part and its own checks, never spends money, never commits, never writes keys, returns the PART_REPORT with claims as bare sentences and numbers measured by named tools. place-integrator: combines stages in plain and reverse order, runs finish and audit, makes one audit repair by editing settings, role tags and dials only (geometry goes back to owners), returns the COMBINE_REPORT. place-renderer: applies renderer-for, checks balance and workers before any long job, draws previews (and finals only if asked), downloads only small previews, measures, makes the guard from the first honest picture, stops and reports when jobs wait over 5 minutes with idle workers (never purges the queue or changes the endpoint), returns the RENDER_REPORT with seconds. place-checker: modes look, structure, process, blind_reader, recheck; recomputes with its own scripts; says whether it was blind; returns the CHECK schema; may not edit anything.

test_build_a_place_workflow.py: skips (77) when node is missing; copies the workflow to a temp .mjs, runs node --check, then runs it in workflow_harness.mjs, a small harness that defines args, agent, parallel, phase, log and answers each agent call with a canned object chosen by label from fixtures/place-workflow/*.json. Cases: happy path (all phases run in order, returns every key); a missing required arg throws with a plain sentence; an audit that fails twice stops before Render and returns the problems; an audit that fails once is repaired and goes on; exactly one Fix round; checkers' prompts contain no builder numbers (the harness greps the prompt text for the claim numbers planted in the part-report fixture); no prompt names a verb that is not in explainer-film-place --verbs; no prompt contains a key, id or the person's name; a part that returns null is reported as missing, not silently dropped; parts above the cap are queued, not skipped.

design.entry_points:
THE CONTRACT. All names below are exact. Kind words: plain python = no Blender needed.

A. COMMAND LINE: bin/explainer-film-place VERB [options]   (wrapper -> kit/place-kit/place_command.py)
Exit codes everywhere: 0 pass (read the LOOK lines), 1 fail, 2 an input is missing or unusable (a plain sentence names the file and the tool that makes it). Plain output lines start FAIL, LOOK or PASS (the preflight reads them). `explainer-film-place --verbs` prints one verb per line; `explainer-film-place VERB --help` prints that verb's options.
Global options (every verb): --scene FILE.blend | --settings FILE (default place-settings.json beside the scene) | --out FILE (JSON result) | --json | --report FILE | --kit DIR | --blender PATH | --quick (trial sizes: maps 256 px, mask cell 0.5 m) | --owner NAME (only that owner's objects) | --save-as FILE.blend (for verbs that change the scene; refuses to overwrite the input unless --overwrite).
Verbs (21):
1 new-settings --scene S --place NAME --type TYPE [--out place-settings.json]   drafts settings from names, collections, material names; prints roles it guessed and objects it could not classify, each with the cheapest way to classify it. Blender.
2 roles --scene S --settings P [--write]   one role per object; --write sets custom property place_role (needs --save-as); exit 1 when an object is unknown and not covered by a never rule. Blender.
3 surfaces [--map-size PIXELS] [--maps-folder DIR]   UVs, normal maps, roughness and colour variation, bevel, displacement settings by role. Blender.
4 roads   shapes graded ground, ruts, banks, hoof prints, grass crown, puddle hollows from settings.roads. Blender.
5 age [--look ID] [--state dry|damp|wet] [--master X] [--layers a,b] [--layers-off a,b] [--mask-cell-metres X]   the wear layers in their fixed order. Blender.
6 grow [--density X]   3D plants, cushions, litter pieces with keep-out gates. Blender.
7 finish --save-as OUT.blend [--look ID] [--state S] [--map-size P]   the whole pass in this order: roles, roads, surfaces, age, grow, picture size, construction, audit; idempotent (run twice = same counts); prints the audit lines; exit as the audit. Blender.
8 finish-part --owner NAME --save-as OUT.blend [--out part-audit.json]   a part builder's version: only that owner's objects, wear masks from that part alone (audit field masks_from = 'part_only'), audit of those objects. Blender.
9 construction [--out construction.json]   the construction check alone. Blender.
10 normals-test [--size 96] [--samples 24] [--out normals.json]   test light on every unique normal-map image with the flipped control. Blender, Cycles CPU, no screen needed.
11 audit [--out place-audit.json] [--no-judge]   gathers the facts (schema E), then runs calculators/place_audit_check.py check and prints FAIL/LOOK/PASS. Blender (the judge is plain python).
12 undo --save-as OUT.blend   removes everything the kit added (everything with pk_made) and restores material slots. Blender.
13 combine --stages stage_a.py stage_b.py ... [--order plain|reverse] [--owners ownership.json] --save-as OUT.blend [--out combine-report.json]   runs each stage's apply(options), fingerprints after each, reports violations. Blender.
14 fingerprint [--out fp.json]   whole-scene fingerprint. Blender.
15 ownership-diff --start FP1.json --end FP2.json --owners ownership.json [--out diff.json]   plain python.
16 renderer-for   prints CYCLES or EEVEE and the reasons (lit lamp, emissive window, lantern, fire; daylight sun only = EEVEE) [--out]. Blender.
17 render --job JOB.json [--where rented|local|auto] [--engine auto|cycles|eevee] [--finals]   draws the job's pictures with the renderer rule; writes pictures and per-picture log JSON; default previews only. Blender (local) or via the client (rented).
18 rent status | upload LOCAL [--remote PATH] | run 'COMMAND' [--cwd FOLDER] [--timeout SECONDS] | job ID | wait ID [--limit SECONDS] | download REMOTE [--local PATH] | balance   the rented-card client. Plain python.
19 measure PICTURE... [--guard G] [--make-guard] [--regions FILE | --id-map PICTURE --id-colours FILE] [--previous PICTURE] [--out]   plain python (calls calculators/picture_measures.py).
20 crops --picture P --boxes x,y,w,h [x,y,w,h ...] [--previous P2] --out-folder DIR   100 percent crops with before and after strips. Plain python.
21 check-presets   every number in data/*.json carries kind and source; roles, surfaces, looks, facts agree with each other; the lint (no place word from data/examples or the fixtures in any kit code); privacy scan (email-like strings, '.runpod', long hex ids, key-looking assignments) over kit/place-kit and the new skill, agents and workflow. Plain python.

B. PYTHON API inside Blender (import place_kit as pk after adding kit/place-kit to sys.path; every function is idempotent)
pk.read_settings(path) -> Settings | pk.new_settings(scene, place, place_type, out_path=None) -> dict | pk.tag_roles(settings, write=True) -> {'by_role':{}, 'unknown':[]} | pk.give_surfaces(settings, owner=None, map_size=None) -> report | pk.shape_roads(settings) -> report | pk.age_place(settings, look=None, state=None, owner=None) -> Wear (methods set_master(x), set_layer_master(layer, x), set_dials(layer, **dials), layer_off(layer), layer_on(layer), set_state(state), report(), remove()) | pk.grow_things(settings, owner=None, density=None) -> report | pk.set_picture_size(camera_name, height_pixels) | pk.check_construction(settings, owner=None, out_path=None) -> dict | pk.test_normal_maps(size=96, samples=24) -> dict | pk.audit_place(settings, out_path, judge=True) -> dict | pk.finish_place(settings, look=None, state=None, quick=False) -> dict | pk.finish_part(settings, owner, quick=True) -> dict | pk.undo_finish() | pk.renderer_for_scene() -> {'engine':'CYCLES'|'EEVEE','reasons':[...]} | pk.fingerprint_scene() -> dict | pk.combine_stages(stage_files, owners, order='plain') -> dict.
Part helpers for builders: pk.begin_part(owner) | pk.new_part_object(owner, role, name, mesh_or_object, collection=None) | pk.forget_part(owner) | pk.seat_on_ground(obj, sink=0.0) | pk.ground_height_at(x, y) -> float | pk.is_keep_clear(x, y) -> bool.

C. NAMES (one place: place_kit/names.py)
Object custom properties: place_owner, place_role, pk_made (1 on everything the kit creates), pk_seed, pk_scatter (1 = exempt from construction), pk_top_z, pk_<layer>_amount (layer keys below), pk_<layer>_<dial>. Layer keys: dirt, grime, weathering, wetness, cracks_and_chips, edge_wear, moss_and_algae, rust, rubbish. Collections: 'Place: <owner>' for a part, 'PK made' for kit objects. Materials the kit makes: 'PK <role> / <surface>'. Node groups: 'PK <Layer>' (for example 'PK Dirt'). Images: pk_<surface>_nor, pk_<surface>_height, pk_plan_<mask>. Treatment keys (sixteen): normal_map, displacement, roughness_variation, colour_variation, bevelled_edges, dirt, grime, weathering, wetness, cracks_and_chips, edge_wear, moss_and_algae, rust, rubbish, plants, litter_pieces. Object checks: uv, carried, scale_ok. Look ids: kept, lived_in, neglected, derelict. States: dry, damp, wet. Stage file: stage_<owner>.py with apply(options). Preview cameras: 'Place <owner> cam <n>' (deleted by finish).

D. DATA FORMATS (kit/place-kit/data/)
place-settings.json: {about, place, place_type, look, look_by_role:{role:look}, state, seed, picture:{camera, height_pixels}, owners:{name:{collections:[],objects:[regex],materials:[prefix]}} or path to ownership.json, roles:[{role, match:{names:[regex],collections:[],materials:[regex],properties:{}}, surface, dials:{layer:multiplier}}], never:[{match, role, reason}], off:[{layer, roles:['wall.*'], reason}], require_more:{class:[treatment]}, roads:[{name, polyline:[[x,y]], width, gauge, rut_depth, rut_width, hoof, centre_grass}], footfall:[shape], keep_clear:[shape], ground:{roles:[], water_level_z, bounds}, habitat:{}, species:[], facts, style_note, style_guard, cameras:[{name, role}], renderer:'auto'|'cycles'|'eevee'}. Shapes: band_along, lines_along, polyline, rect, around_role, auto_door_strip (as the weathering kit).
roles.json: {about, classes:{class:{requires:[treatment], wanted:[treatment]}}, roles:{id:{class, surface, displace, may_hang, needs_support:'ground'|'part'|'none', max_span_metres, scale:[fact ids], dials:{layer:x}, kind, source}}}.

design.how_it_becomes_automatic:
FOUR LEVERS, EACH WITH A STOP

1. ROUTING (skills and docs). A model that gets 'build a village in the forest in Blender' has no film word, so the master skill would not load; make-3d-models and build-and-paint-a-place would. All three descriptions and the new skill's description carry: village, town, harbour, mine, farm, garden, interior, building, cottage, stable, road, props, 'in Blender', and the surface words (normal maps, displacement, dirt, grime, weeds, moss, weathering, damage, wetness, rubbish, construction, real sizes), and say 'even if the request never mentions surfaces'. The first screen of each (the REQUIRED block) turns the pass and the construction check into steps 2 and 3 of a three-step list. make-explainer-film's 'Before you start (always)' item 5 and its stage table (`place` row) send any Blender place work to the new skill. The README and the tips guide (section 8a) say it again. test_place_skills.py fails if any of these words or blocks is missing or drifts.

2. ONE ENTRY POINT PER JOB (kit code). `explainer-film-place finish` does the whole pass in one call; `finish-part` does a builder's share; `audit`, `construction`, `normals-test`, `renderer-for`, `render`, `measure` each do one job. Settings come from one small place-settings.json per place (new-settings drafts it from the scene), looks and surfaces are presets, roles are data. The model never splices nodes, writes a normal-map converter, or invents a renderer rule.

3. A PREFLIGHT STAGE THAT FAILS (kit code). `explainer-film-preflight place` reads place-audit.json and FAILS when a material or the scene lacks a required treatment, has an unknown role, a silently-off layer, a bad or flipped normal map, a missing UV, an unusable displacement, a floating or inside-out part, a wrong scale, a plant on a wheel track or in a puddle, or a stale audit (scene file changed since). The plates stage refuses a paid painting when a blend is named and its audit fails. Skipping is only possible in two written, signed ways (an 'off' entry with a reason; a preflight 'accepted' entry with who and date), and both show up in the report as KNOWN.

4. A WORKFLOW THAT BUILDS IN PARTS WITH FRESH CHECKERS (workflow). build-a-place: plan (facts, style note, settings, ownership), parallel part builders that each run the pass on their own objects, combine in both orders with an ownership and conflict check, the audit, render with the renderer rule, fresh checkers that recompute the builders' claims without seeing their numbers (look, structure, process, blind reader), a skeptic, one fix round, a different fresh re-check, a plain report.

THE PERSON'S ITEMS (what makes each automatic; what checks it)
- normals: surfaces step makes soft height pictures, converts to OpenGL tangent normal maps, writes UVs first, wires the Normal Map node; audit 'normal_map' plus wiring plus the direction test with a flipped control plus UV check.
- displacements: dirt road, mud, thatch and rock ground are roles with displace true; ground_mesh grades the mesh, displacement.py sets the material method, depth and max displacement; roads.py shapes real ruts and hoof prints; audit 'displacement' (method not Bump Only, mesh dense or adaptive, not a flat plane).
- dirt, grime, stains: layers dirt (soil film, wall-foot splash, polish on worn lanes, dried puddle rings) and grime (soot, run-off streaks, damp bands, tide marks) from masks (lowness, wall foot, sheltered, footfall); required for every hard-surface class.
- weeds, moss: growth/ plants and moss cushions by habitat gates plus the painted moss_and_algae layer; exact-zero keep-out; audit scatter counts must be 0 on wheel tracks, crowns, doorsteps, puddles.
- weathering: its own layer (silvering, sun fade, patina) so it is not confused with dirt.
- damage, cracks, edge wear: cracks_and_chips and edge_wear layers plus bevelled_edges in shape; required for walls, timber, stone, props.
- wetness: layer with state dry, damp, wet (roughness does the work); puddles by lowness; ruts hold water.
- rubbish: painted muck plus litter pieces (leaves, straw, sticks, dung lumps) from a mask of gutters, wall feet, lane edges; never the crown.
- rust: iron roles.
- construction logic: build rules in the skill; check_construction (carried from the ground up, floating, short posts, spans, doorway floors, inside-out, z-fight, buried lights); required, exit 1.
- scale: real_world_facts table plus the place's own facts; audit 'scale'.
- the style rule: first line of the style-rule file and of the planner's style note; the guard made from the first honest picture; picture measures; fresh look checker.
- measures: picture_measures.py (value range, detail energy per role region, flat windows, palette, squint) and the preflight's picture check.
- fresh checkers: workflow phases Check and Re-check; preflight 'fresh_check' input.

WHERE A SMALLER MODEL WOULD SKIP IT, AND WHAT STOPS IT
1 Never loads the skill: descriptions and first lines carry the words; README and tips repeat it.
2 Builds flat boxes with the model kit (these pass model lint): `finish` replaces plain materials by role; place stage fails; model_lint --surfaces warns on glb files.
3 Razor-edged boxes: bevelled_edges is required for wall, timber, iron; finish adds a bevel with hardened normals; audit 'plain boxes'.
4 No UVs: finish writes them; audit 'uv' fails an object under a normal-mapped material without a UV layer.
5 Bump only, flipped green or sRGB normal: audit wiring and the direction test with a flipped control.
6 Displacement node on a flat plane or with Bump Only: audit 'displacement'.
7 A layer with amount 0, or an object missing its pk_<layer>_amount property (the layer silently reads 0): audit 'layer amounts' fails; an amount of 0 needs an 'off' entry with a reason.
8 Weeds on wheel tracks, in puddles, on doorsteps: exact-zero gates and the audit's keep-out counts.
9 Skips moss and weeds because 'it does not need them': they are required by role and look; the only way out is a reasoned 'off'.
10 Floating or unsupported parts: construction check is required and exits 1; the part helpers seat things.
11 Wrong size (a 1 m door, a 0.5 m stall): the facts table and the scale check.
12 Photographic noise instead of designed marks: the style rule on the first screen, look presets with few big marks, budgets, the guard and detail-energy bands, the fresh look checker.
13 Claims success without evidence: claims are rechecked by fresh checkers who never see the builders' numbers; reports must say measured or judged.
14 Wrong or slow renderer, wasted money: renderer-for and render apply the person's rule; the guide's balance and worker checks; a stale or stalled queue stops and reports.
15 Stale audit after edits: scene_sha1 against the file; --gate closes when inputs change.
16 Parallel builders overwrite each other: owners, idempotent stages, fingerprint diff, both orders.
17 Secrets or personal details: the client reads settings at run time; check-presets and a test scan every new file; the push guard knows a RunPod key pattern.
Also: the plain-request trial (below) is the proof that it works without the request mentioning surfaces; the plugin ships no hook, so routing rests on descriptions and first screens alone (said plainly in the risks).
design.tests:
BASELINE FIRST. Re-run python3 kit/calculators/tests/run_all.py before and after. The inventory reader measured 25 files, 22 passed, 1 failed (test_preflight.py: the film stage wants 4 GB free disk, this machine has about 2.8 GB), 2 skipped; I did not re-run it. After the change the same single failure and all new files passing, no skip hidden by an error. (A builder may fix that failure by passing --free-disk-gb in the test; say so in the report.)
ALL TESTS RUN HERE with Blender at /home/user/work/blender-app/blender-5.2.2-linux-x64/blender, tiny scenes, 64 x 64 pictures, no network, no rented card, no key. Each Blender step must finish in about a minute; a test that cannot find Blender exits 77 with a plain reason.
PLAIN PYTHON TESTS
1 test_place_data.py: every number in data/*.json has kind and source; every role names a class, a surface and facts that exist; every class lists only the sixteen treatment keys; every look has all layer keys; surfaces have all ids from roles; film-settings place_* sections pass settings.py check; invented entries in the whole table stay at or under a tenth; lint: no word from data/examples or fixtures appears in any code file under kit/place-kit (the weathering kit's no-place-names lint, rewritten); privacy scan over kit/place-kit, the new skill, agents, workflow and bin/explainer-film-place (email-like strings, '.runpod', hex ids of 24 or more characters, key-looking assignments): 0 hits.

3 test_place_audit_check.py: the judge on hand-written audits. The flat hut audit FAILS and names normal_map, roughness_variation, colour_variation, bevelled_edges, dirt, grime, weathering, wetness, cracks_and_chips, edge_wear per material; a finished hut audit PASSES; stale scene_sha1 fails; unknown role fails; amount 0 without an 'off' reason fails; with a reason it is KNOWN; a plant on a wheel track fails; a floating plank fails; a door 1.0 m high fails and 1.7 m passes; a WANTED treatment missing is only a LOOK; accepted entries (stage place) turn a finding into known; a made-up fresh-check result with one false claim fails.
4 test_picture_measures.py: made-up pictures with known answers (28-check style): flat grey has every window flat; uniform noise at a known amplitude gives the known detail energy; a 2 px blur lowers it; identical pictures squint 1.0 and a shifted one less; a saturated patch gives its exact pixel share; a cyan patch counts as turquoise; percentiles of a ramp; guard made from a picture passes that picture and fails a flattened copy; float32 shrink does not crash on a 2400-wide picture.
5 test_preflight_place.py: `--list` shows stage place and each input's maker; place with a passing fixture audit exits 0; a failing one exits 1 and prints the first failure; no audit exits 2 naming the file and the tool; stale audit (blend sha differs) fails; --gate closes after the audit file changes; an accepted entry makes a failing finding KNOWN and a too-broad entry stops with exit 2; plates with a blend and no audit exits 2; plates without the new inputs behaves exactly as before (the existing test_preflight.py keeps passing).
6 test_place_render.py: renderer_for on a tiny scene with a sun only gives EEVEE, with a point lamp or an emissive window gives CYCLES with reasons; the client with a FAKE transport: missing settings give one plain sentence and exit 2; keys never appear in output or logs (capture and grep); a settings file inside a git repository is refused; upload skips unchanged files by checksum; workers idle with a waiting job for over 5 minutes stops and reports; a text search proves the client has no purge and no endpoint-change call; the push guard fires on a made-up RunPod-style key.
BLENDER TESTS (test_place_blender.py, test_place_combine.py)
7 The flat hut (a builder script in fixtures: ground, four wall boxes, a roof, a door, a plank floor with one floating plank): `explainer-film-place audit` exits 1 and lists the missing treatments and the floating plank. NEGATIVE PROOF: this is the test that shows the audit can fail.
8 `finish` on the hut then `audit` exits 0 (only LOOK lines allowed); normal maps are OpenGL, Non-Color, wired; normals-test passes for every image and the flipped control fails; displacement set on the ground role; every object under a layered material has its pk_<layer>_amount.
9 Dial zero: with every master dial at 0 the picture (64 x 64, Cycles CPU, 8 samples, fixed seed) equals the picture before the wear pass to 16-bit tolerance (the courtyard once got 0.52 percent of dots over one step: report your number). Isolation: a layer alone changes only its roles' dots; each role multiplier changes only its objects, in EVERY layer. Determinism: two draws identical. Undo: undo leaves material slots and node counts as before; finish twice gives the same counts. Visible effect: the pass changes at least 5 percent of the hut's dots (judged).
10 Roads: the rut height function (plain numpy) has two ruts a gauge apart at the right depth, a bank beside each, hoof dimples at the stride, and zero change outside the lane width; the keep-out count of scattered plants on the wheel tracks is exactly 0 and in puddles exactly 0.
11 Construction: a plank on two stringers on two posts on the ground passes; the same plank lifted 2 cm fails (floating); a post 4 cm short of its beam is reported short; a door with no floor behind it is flagged; an inside-out box and two coplanar faces are flagged; scatter pieces are exempt and the report says so.
12 Combine: two stage files that each add objects and one that edits another owner's object: the violation is reported; the reverse order gives the same result; running the chain twice gives the same counts; the ownership diff names the owner.
13 D7 test: render a rough surface at a low angle with normal map only, displacement only and both (strength x 0.6); write the numbers into DEVIATIONS.md.
CROSS-CHECKS (owner (a) and (c))
14 test_place_skills.py (above) and test_build_a_place_workflow.py (above): run the real workflow file under a harness with canned agents; no real agent is called.
15 test_house_rules.py now covers kit/place-kit.
OTHER CHECKS TO RUN ONCE AND REPORT
16 python3 kit/calculators/settings.py check; explainer-film-place check-presets; explainer-film-setup into a scratch folder (npm unavailable) and read 'files the skills name: N checked, 0 missing'; bin/explainer-film-preflight --list.
17 One real rented-card smoke test by the MAIN SESSION only, through the proven client in the scratch runpod folder (not through the plugin's client, which cannot read the person's settings without them): render the finished hut's Cycles preview, check the log JSON, report seconds. If jobs wait over 5 minutes with idle workers, stop and report.
PLAIN-REQUEST TRIAL (a later step, not in run_all): give Sonnet only the person's words ('Build a village in the forest. Needs unkept dirt roads like they've been driven down by horse and carriage, an empty stable, a few cottages, some scattered mediaeval props.') with the plugin installed and nothing else. Pass lines: the transcript shows it loaded a plugin skill by itself, ran explainer-film-place finish and audit, and `explainer-film-preflight place` passed; the pictures show ruts, thatch, moss, silvering and plants. Fail lines are recorded as findings, not hidden.
WHAT THIS DESIGN CANNOT PROMISE: the tests prove the gates and the plain mechanics; they do not prove the village looks good. That is for the fresh checkers and the person's eyes.
risks: The lighter numpy-only masks are not tested anywhere (the proven masks need OpenCV and 25 to 80 s a scene). If isolation, dial-zero or keep-out tests fail, builder (b) must fall back to carrying masks/reader.py behind a flag and say so in DEVIATIONS.md; wall foot from world z minus ground height, and edge wear from object bounds, are my judgement.

The weathering layers were tuned in EEVEE on a street and a courtyard; Cycles was never run with the kit, and the re-check said that at film size it added little a viewer could see except rust and a few weeds. The design therefore leads with normal maps, displacement and shape, but the village look itself is unproven until the fresh checkers and the person look.

Contract drift between three builders working at once is the biggest process risk. Mitigations: exact names in ENTRY POINTS, DEVIATIONS.md, test_place_skills.py and the workflow harness test that parse the real verbs, files and house number keys. A builder who cannot meet a name must keep the old one as an alias.

Builder (b)'s list is long. The audit must never require a treatment the kit does not yet make, so roles.json 'requires' may only contain implemented and tested treatments; the rest go in 'wanted'. If time runs out, stop at a numbered step of the order of work, not in the middle of one, and report what is missing.

Real-world numbers in the facts starter list (cart gauge, door and stall sizes, thatch pitch, rut and hoof sizes) are from memory or invented, not researched; they are marked guess or weak and the planner must confirm or replace them with sources. A wrong 'fact' enforced by the scale check would build the wrong place.

Normal map plus displacement together: the sources disagree (Scenario: never both; the coal mine used both with strength x 0.6; the cookbook measured no doubling). I settled it as judged (D7) and one low-angle test must confirm it.

The generic rented-card client cannot be tested against the real endpoint without the person's settings; its tests use a fake transport. The balance check needs an API the client may not be able to call; 'balance' may return 'unknown'. The 22 October note in the render guide says the endpoint was switched fully off by the person; if renders wait, the workflow stops and reports, and the local fallback is very slow (a small EEVEE picture of a hooked scene took over 3 minutes here).

The RunPod bill for the garden job (US$10.89) was about 2.5 times the work seconds and is unexplained; the guide must not promise a cost from seconds. The key pattern for the push guard (rpa_ prefix) is my belief and was not checked against the person's account (I may not read ~/.runpod).

Blender's own Python has no Pillow or OpenCV, so any module that imports them inside Blender fails (model_kit.py already does). check-presets and a test must catch an import of PIL, cv2 or scipy in kit code that runs in Blender.

Sub-agents may be refused when they try to write report files (seen in the garden job); the workflow returns reports as text and agents are told to save evidence as JSON or txt. A container restart can lose a running checker's work; checkers write results to files as they go.

The blind reading test uses keyword matching on a blind reader's free text, which is crude; it measures only whether planned features are mentioned. It was never run blind before, so its 75 percent line (12 of 16) is a judgement.

The squint test and the silhouette yardsticks conflicted with the concept in the garden round. The design reports them and never gates on squint; who may accept a miss is left to the person or a signed accepted entry.

Required wear layers on imported Poly Haven props may be too strict or look wrong (lime-bright moss on scans, stickers); roles such as prop.imported count their own maps as present, and 'accepted' entries exist, but per-role tuning will be needed after the first village.

The plan adds a ninth preflight stage, a new bin script, new house-number sections and a changed preflight.py (1,959 lines) edited by one builder while others read it; existing tests assume eight stages in places (--list counts, error text). Builder (b) must run the whole suite after each preflight change.

I wrote this design without running Blender or the test suite myself; baseline numbers (22 pass, 1 fail, 2 skipped; flat hut passes model lint; 'sys.exit' codes from a --python script) come from the inventory readers and still need to be confirmed by the builders. I did check: Blender 5.2.2 exists at the named path, Python 3.13.16 with numpy 2.5.3, Pillow 12.3.0 and OpenCV 5.0.0 are on the system, film-settings.json has 517 entries with 44 invented, about 2.8 GB of disk is free.

I did not add a plugin hook (a prompt-time reminder when a message mentions Blender or a village) because the plugin has no hooks folder, the hook format was not verified here, and a broken hooks file could stop the plugin loading. Routing therefore rests on skill descriptions and first screens; if the plain-request trial shows Sonnet still skips the skills, a hook is the next lever and is the person's decision.
The plugin.json author field and README handle lines carry a personal handle (pre-existing, not touched). Nothing new may add any personal detail; the person should say whether those lines stay.

The 'finish' verb changes a scene in many ways at once; undo is only as good as the pk_made registry. A kit bug that edits a shared material in place would damage other owners' work in parallel builds; copy-never-edit is enforced by the ownership diff, not by the code.

Parts built in parallel cannot see each other's ground and walls, so a part's own wear preview uses masks from that part alone (masks_from part_only) and can differ from the final; only the combined pass is judged.

The 'plain request' route still relies on the model following a skill. Nothing in the kit can force a model that never loads a skill or never runs the command; the only hard stop is that later steps (plates, paid painting) refuse without a passing audit when a blend is named.

critic.verdict: Not ready to hand to the three builders as written. The design is strong on gates (audit, judge, preflight stage, fingerprints, fresh checkers) and on honesty about what is untested. But I found 6 blocking faults and about 20 smaller ones. Blocking: (1) it tells builder (a) to edit /home/user/Music/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json, which is outside the allowed folder (I confirmed the file exists there); (2) the REQUIRED block says "do not tell the user about it", which hides work and failures and misreads the person's "don't tell it that" (that was about the test prompt, not the final report); (3) the audit checks that a treatment is present, not that it has a visible size, so a small model can pass with amounts of 0.01, 3 weeds, 256 px maps from --quick, or a free-text 'off' reason; (4) the data is tilted to the medieval village (no brick, concrete, tarmac, sand, steel, tile-floor or sea-water surfaces, and no mine, harbour or interior roles), which breaks the 'any place' goal; (5) damage and variation made as shape (chipped corners, no two planks alike, sag, missing tiles), which the garden showed was what actually read at film size, has no verb and no check; (6) the ground is built in parallel with parts that seat themselves on it, so ruts and regrading will leave props floating. Fix those six, plus the routing and runnability items in required_changes, and the design can go ahead. Without them a small model asked for 'a village in the forest' will still skip ruts, geometry damage, minimum wear amounts and the real renderer rule, and will pass the audit anyway. What I checked: the plugin on disk (no hooks folder; bare bin names are the convention; preflight needs no --project; film-settings.json has 518 entries, 44 invented; test_house_rules wants a docstring starting 'What this does'; make_check_file.py does not record the scene path; seat.py is under checker3 not checker2; eight carried garden files contain Astra add-on object names). I did not run Blender or the suite; the inventory baselines are the readers' numbers.
missing: Damage and variation as SHAPE has no verb, module or check. The garden showed this is what read at film size: chipped corners, individually different planks (width 9-17 cm, thickness, bow, cup, twist), replaced boards, missing or slipped tiles, sag, leaning posts. wood_geo.build_plank, r_stones.chip_rock and the tile-variant method are in the carry list but have no home in the file list (surfaces/ has only heights, normals, uvs, materials, displacement, ground_mesh, roads, bevel). Add a treatment 'shape_damage', a verb (for example 'damage'), a generic module, and a check that siblings of one role are not identical (dimension spread, share of exact copies).

Ruts and hoof prints are not a treatment and nothing checks them. 'roads' needs polylines in settings, and new-settings cannot infer them. Add: derive lane centre lines from curve objects or from the road mesh, and a generic object-level check 'ground_relief' (cross-section relief of the ground mesh above a house number; ruts as the road case). This also covers farm furrows, mine tracks and paths.

Ground built in parallel with parts that seat on it. A part seated on the starting ground floats or sinks once the ground owner adds ruts, banks and a graded mesh. The garden had a contract ('bed within 0.1 m inside 1.2 m'). Add a phase 'Ground first' (serial, frozen height function or baked ground), have ground_height_at read it, and add a reseat pass in combine before the construction check.

Lighting and backdrop. The garden's light stage (graded sky, separate lighting sky so shadows go cool, key/fill/rim, lit windows and lanterns with ray-visibility set, light groups, toe lift, hills all round) and Scenario's value study (clip under 0.5 percent) are absent. A scene with no world or lights renders black or flat, and the renderer rule depends on lit lamps that nobody adds. Add a minimal 'light' verb (sun, sky, fill, glow lamps for glow roles, backdrop) and a light audit.

Joints and mortar (stone paving, stone and brick walls, plank gaps) and a lighting-robustness test. The street needed joints darker, duller and sloped, and tested dry, wet, flat and side light (6 of 22 pictures passed before, 21 of 22 after). The design has neither. Add a 'joints' layer or surface step and a two-light check (flat/wet/side) on the first preview.

No budgets. The garden capped added triangles (1.5 million per builder), final draw time (90 s) and card memory (12 GB). The audit has counts.triangles but no limit and no scatter cap. Add place_budget house numbers and a check.

Blend between neighbouring ground roles (road, verge, forest floor) and seams between tiled materials. roads.py writes wet and rut attributes only, so two meshes with two materials meet at a hard line or z-fight. Add a mask-driven blend or a single ground mesh with attribute-driven material, as the mine yard did.
Role per material slot. One role per object breaks joined meshes and imported Poly Haven props with several materials (barrel wood and iron bands). Add per-slot roles or per-material matching.

Roles for doors, windows, barrels, wheels, chimneys, carts. roles.json has none, so the scale facts ('door 1.0 m fails') cannot match anything. Facts need the same matcher as roles (names, roles, a place_kind property).

Surfaces and roles for other places: brick (wall.brick exists but no brick surface), concrete, tarmac, sand, snow, rock or ore, steel plate, painted metal, tile or stone floor, carpet and fabric, sea or river water, wet planks, furniture, boats, rope and net. Plus place_types presets for mine, harbour, farm and interior that name the 'allowed off' items (see wrong_or_risky). Without these the plugin is a medieval-village kit.

Wall-foot band must be measured from each object's own lowest z (wk_zmin style), not from world z minus ground height. The street lesson: stone plinths 15-46 cm high hid the band. Every cottage on a footing hits this.

A concept or target step for a new place. The garden got its character from paid concept pictures as targets (within a ledger). The design has none, so the style guard is made from the first honest picture, which locks in whatever the first (probably bland) picture looked like. Add an optional budget-gated concept step, or absolute detail-energy floors per region class from the plugin's own measured table, and mark a guard made from the first picture 'provisional'.

A Blender-MCP/live-scene route. make-3d-models already documents the MCP route, and this environment has mcp__blender__ tools. The design only has a headless file route (finish --save-as writes a new file, so a live scene goes stale). Add a documented in-process route (import place_kit, pk.finish_place) and 'save, finish, reopen' steps.
A fake-proof or at least staleness-safe audit hand-off: say what happens when the model re-saves the finished file (file hash changes, audit goes stale) and test open-and-save equality.

Fake users for replaced materials and meshes. Blender drops zero-user data on save (58 materials vanished in the garden), so undo_finish cannot restore unless originals keep a fake user. Not mentioned.

Unapplied scale, negative scale and the model_lint checks (stripes from squashed UVs, same-plane, floors over ground, '.001' names, glass, glow) are not run by the place audit. model_lint already exists in the plugin; the audit should call it in scene mode instead of re-implementing coplanar faces with different thresholds.

A Blender 5.2 traps list for smaller models (image rows bottom-up, packed images, Attribute node reads 0, geometry-nodes multi-input reversal, device is a preference, EGL, no Pillow, use_auto_smooth gone). Only a few appear in the new docs.

Lessons not carried: kit.report() 'problems/skipped' as a visible list in finish output; wetness colour ratios measured only for stone and brick (nothing for timber, thatch, plaster, so say 'unmeasured'); the multiply-versus-colour-layer trap (a colour layer hides layers below); moss must not be brighter than its stone (listed only as a courtyard fix).

Keyword-to-look mapping is absent. The plain request says 'unkept'; nothing tells a model that means look 'neglected' (kept, tidy, clean = kept; unkept, overgrown, abandoned = neglected; ruined = derelict).
not_automatic: Loading any of the skills. Routing rests on descriptions only and the plugin ships no hook. The example request has no 'Blender' in it, and the descriptions key on 'in Blender'. A model using the Blender MCP tools directly may never open a plugin skill.
Running 'explainer-film-place finish' at all. Nothing runs it unless the model chooses to. The preflight place stage only runs if the model calls it.
place-settings.json. It must exist before finish, and the REQUIRED block does not say to draft it first (new-settings). Roads, footfall, keep-clear shapes and owners cannot be inferred from names.
Roles for hand-built objects. If finish stops at roles on an unknown object (exit 1), a small model will stall or skip. The design does not say whether finish auto-assigns a fallback role.

The 'plates' guard. It only fires if the model passes --blend. The existing film route (preflight plates without --blend) is unchanged, so a flat plate still goes to paid painting. make_check_file.py does not stamp the scene path, so nothing can find the audit by itself.
Staleness: without --blend the preflight place stage only warns 'not checked', so a stale audit passes.

--quick. The skill tells models to use --quick locally (256 px maps, 0.5 m masks), and the design never says the audit or preflight rejects quick output for a final. A model on this slow machine will always use it and pass.

Minimum wear. Presence is checked, size is not: amount 0.01, three weeds, density 0 with a node group present, or a 'master 0.05' all pass. The audit says 'amount 0 needs a reason', which a one-word reason defeats.

'off' reasons are free text with no cap, no who/date, and no list of reasons a place type may legitimately use. Interiors and mines must write many offs (moss on walls is required for the whole wall class), so models will write 'n/a' for everything, or put moss in a living room.
Fresh checkers, the style note, the facts table and the blind reader exist only inside the build-a-place workflow. A plain request gets none of them. The fresh_check input is optional and only warns.
Picture measures run only if the model calls 'measure', and need a guard that only exists after a first picture.

The renderer rule. 'render' applies it, but a model can call Blender directly. The rule is also undefined for a lit scene when no rented card is set up (silent fall back to EEVEE would break the person's rule; very slow local Cycles needs an explicit decision).
Real period sizes. The scale check uses only the generic table; period facts need the planner's research, which only the workflow does.
Geometry damage, ruts and ground relief (see missing). A plain request gets shader wear and normal maps, but nothing makes or checks damage as shape.
Concept targets and lighting (see missing): no step and no gate.
wrong_or_risky: Writes outside the allowed folder: owner (a) is told to edit /home/user/Music/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json. Remove it and list it as a to-do for the main session or person. A junk file entry '/home/user/Music/plugins/explainer-follow-placeholder' (action ignore) is also outside the plugin: delete it.

REQUIRED block and skill step 5 say 'do not tell the user about it unless asked / never tell the user'. This contradicts the writing rule (report what you did, tested, did not test, every failure) and the plugin's own honesty rules. Replace with: 'do it without being asked; in your report say plainly what the pass did, what the audit measured and what you skipped'.

REQUIRED block commands will fail as written: finish needs place-settings.json, which does not exist on a plain request; 'explainer-film-preflight place' with no --place-audit exits 2 (INPUTS are options only); the freshness check needs --blend. Give the exact full commands, let finish draft settings when missing, and let 'audit' print the exact preflight line to run.

'--quick' can produce an audit that passes the final gate. Record quick: true and the map sizes in the audit and make preflight place fail (or LOOK-then-fail for the plates stage) when a final is built from quick output. Add a minimum normal-map size check (house number; the garden check was 1024 px).
'dry' state versus 'amount 0 fails': wetness at state dry is legitimately 0. The judge must exempt wetness amount when state is dry, and moss and rubbish under look 'kept'.

Normal-direction test is too strict. 'Flipped-green control must be negative' fails legitimate maps: the water swell control read +0.87, and the plank map has almost no X slope (+0.061 on a wrong plane). Test only axes where the map has slope energy and report 'not informative' otherwise. For kit-made maps compare against their own height in plain numpy (exact, no Blender). Keep the Cycles test light as one end-to-end wiring test. Say whether direction 'not run' fails (it should, except under --quick).

Virtual screen: D1 says 'xvfb-run only for verbs that draw with a screen (none by default)'. The existing skills and the hard rule say local EEVEE needs a virtual screen (libEGL error), and the task says xvfb-run -a for anything drawn here. place_command must wrap render (local EEVEE) and normals-test in xvfb-run -a when available, and tests must cover both with and without.

Lint contradiction: check-presets forbids words found in data/examples and fixtures from kit code, but code recipe names such as thatch_bunches, shingle_rows, plaster_blotch, straw_strands come from the same words. Define an explicit banned place-noun list (village, town, harbour, mine, farm, garden, interior, forest, cottage, stable, street, courtyard) in a data file; material words are allowed in code recipe ids.

check-presets will trip on its own fixtures and docs: the push-guard test string 'rpa_...' would be flagged by the person's own push check if written literally (the existing test builds its sk- key at run time: copy that), and a scan for 'key-looking words' will hit every document that says api_key or endpoint_id. Scan values (long quoted strings, hex ids, rpa_ patterns, emails, '.runpod'), not words. The key format 'rpa_' is a belief, not verified; say so in the pattern label (the design does).

Rendering guide text must not carry session facts or personal money details: 'on 22 October the endpoint was reported switched off' (the task says it is switched on; delete), 'a balance of US$0.13', the US$10.89 bill, US$3.86 of US$15 budgets, '3 workers' as the person's setting. Say 'a nearly empty balance stalls jobs while workers show idle'. Keep dated generic prices with date_read. Quote the person's rules as 'the film owner's rule' and fix the typo 'eeve' (paraphrase, do not copy verbatim).

Carried garden files are not clean for a generic plugin: g6_common.py, g6_world.py, struct.py, plank_stats.py, own_diff.py, bridge_check.py, seat.py and build_character.py contain Astra / CT add-on object and material names; almost every carried file hard-codes /home/user or /tmp/claude-0 paths; kits/weathering/walls/remote_walls.py and harness/remote.py mention ~/.runpod. The design lists 'Astra-bound' files to skip but not these. Add 'Astra', 'CT /', '/home/', 'claude-0' and '.runpod' to the privacy and name lint over kit/place-kit. Also: seat.py is in checker3/scripts, not checker2/scripts.

mine-scene (ground_and_yard.py, mine_common.py) is not in the authorised SOURCES list. Either have the person approve it or limit builders to ideas; mine_common's SURFACES table is the person's uploaded pictures (already excluded).

Plan masks at 0.10 m cell have no cap. A 200 m village is 2000 x 2000 per mask, times about a dozen masks, packed into the .blend (disk is about 2.7 GB free), and millions of Python ray casts. Add cell = max(0.10, extent / 1500) (house number), single-channel 16-bit or stacked RGBA packing, a time budget and a recorded resolution in the audit. The design admits the lighter masks are untested; add timing to the acceptance test.

Stage name overlap: 'shots' is already 'before building or drawing a place's views'; 'place' is 'after building and before drawing'. A model will run one and think both done. Make the STAGE_WORDS and tips explicit about order (shots, then build, then place, then plates), and print the next stage in each report.

Builder (b) owns about 60 files across 9 steps, and a stop line leaves the 'required' list unbuilt. Split it (see required_changes). Also roles.json 'requires' must be enforced by a test (each required treatment names a made_by function that imports and has a test), not by a builder's promise.

Template ownership collision: (a) owns kit/place-kit/data/templates/*.md|json inside (b)'s tree. check-presets (b) must skip data/templates and data/examples, and the real_world_facts_template.json placeholders must not fail 'every number has kind and source'. stage_template.py in the same folder is (b)'s and falls under test_house_rules (docstring starting 'What this does').

Path ambiguity for (c): 'tests/workflow_harness.mjs' and 'tests/fixtures/place-workflow/' have no base. Use kit/calculators/tests/... in full. The skill file entry also mixes front matter with body instructions ('when_to_use: ... Body, under 250 lines...'); tell (a) that only the first sentence is the when_to_use value.

Blender tests skip (exit 77) when Blender is not found, and Blender is not on PATH here. A green run_all with BLENDER unset hides every Blender test. Require the builders' final report to list pass and skip per new file, run with BLENDER set, and fail if more than the two known project-picture skips remain.

Blender claim in blender-mcp-notes edit (1): 'displacement works in Cycles and EEVEE'. EEVEE displacement was never tested in 5.2.2 here (the cookbook says EEVEE was not tested). Test it under xvfb or soften the sentence.

Audit hash timing: the audit hashes the saved file, then the model may re-save. Specify that audit never re-saves and a test proves open-save-hash equality, or the preflight will mark good work stale (or worse, miss a changed file).

Roads and surfaces 'refuse a flat plane' but finish needs to regrade automatically (graded grid) and regrading changes UVs and heights for objects already seated: order finish as ground regrade, reseat, then surfaces.

The handler shipped in place-kit/render/worker runs any shell command it is sent; the design notes 'the key is the only lock'. Also say in the guide that the plugin never exposes the endpoint, and keep 'rent run' out of agent permissions by default (place-renderer may run it only with a job file).

Skills description length is fine (840 and 887 characters, under the listing cap), but make-explainer-film's description still has no place words in its main sentence; only the added tail. Keep the tail within the first 1,500 characters.

Invented-number cap: the settings test allows invented up to a tenth of the table. The table has 518 entries and 44 invented; the design adds about 15 invented. That passes only if at least about 80 new entries are added at the same time (limit = 0.1 x total). Check with test_settings.py after each edit.
critic.required_changes:
"BUILDER SPLIT AND CONTRACT
1. Split builder (b) into three kit builders. b1: place_kit core, data/*.json, roles/looks/surfaces/facts, launcher (bin, place_command.py, blender_run.py), checks/{construction,scale,scene_audit,normals_test}.py, calculators/place_audit_check.py, picture_measures.py, preflight stage, film-settings, plan_budget guard, setup, model_lint/model_kit, and their tests. b2: surfaces/, wear/, growth/, new geometry-damage module, light verb, and their Blender tests. b3: parts/undo/fingerprint/ownership/combine, render/ (job, client, worker), extras. b1 publishes names.py, treatments.json, roles.json and the settings schema within its first step so b2 and b3 can start. Keep the DEVIATIONS.md rule.
2. Remove from (a): the edit of /home/user/Music/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (note it for the main session). Remove the placeholder entry outside the plugin folder. Write every path in full (kit/calculators/tests/..., not tests/...).
3. Add an enforced rule: a treatment may appear in a roles.json 'requires' list only if its made_by function exists and has a passing test; test_place_data.py checks this.

WORDS AND ROUTING (a)
4. Rewrite the REQUIRED block (same text in the three skills): drop 'do not tell the user'; use: 'do it without being asked; in your report say plainly what it did, what the audit measured and what you skipped'. Give the full commands: new-settings (or finish drafts it), finish, audit, then 'explainer-film-preflight place --place-audit place-audit.json --blend FINISHED.blend'. Add the in-process route for a live Blender (import place_kit; pk.finish_place) and 'save, finish, reopen'.
5. Add keyword mapping to the skill: kept, tidy, clean = kept; unkept, overgrown, abandoned = neglected; ruined, collapsed = derelict; wet, rainy = wet or damp; and a rule for a place with no 'Blender' word (village, town, set, level, scene, props, in 3D).
6. Ask the main session or person about one optional lever, a small hooks/hooks.json (UserPromptSubmit reminder, keyword-gated, prints the REQUIRED block). Verify the format first from the plugin-authoring or update-config documentation; add a test that the JSON parses and the script prints the block. If the format cannot be verified, say so in DEVIATIONS.md and leave it out.
7. In rendering-on-rented-cards.md: delete the 'endpoint reported switched off' sentence; replace the balance, bill and budget figures with plain statements; paraphrase the person's rules as 'the film owner's rule'. In blender-mcp-notes: soften or test the EEVEE displacement claim. Add a short Blender 5.2 traps file (list in missing).

AUTOMATIC STRENGTH (b1/b2)

What the kit now does. One command, `explainer-film-place finish --scene X.blend`, gives every object a role. It then adds real normal maps, roughness and colour variation, bevels with hardened normals, and displacement where the role needs it. It adds the nine wear layers: dirt, grime, weathering, wetness, cracks and chips, edge wear, moss, rust and rubbish. It bends and chips shapes, lays wheel ruts as real geometry, scatters 3D weeds and litter that stay out of ruts, and adds a light if the scene has none. Then it saves, reopens the saved file and audits it. Blender writes only facts. A separate plain-Python judge (`place_audit_check.py`) decides, using house numbers from `film-settings.json`. `explainer-film-preflight place` and `plates` run that judge, so a place that was never audited cannot reach a paid painting. report.summary:
I wrote the build-a-place workflow, its five helper files, a test harness with canned helpers, and the test and fixtures. The workflow takes the person's plain words as they are and adds the plugin's own steps itself, so the request never has to mention surfaces or wear. It has ten phases: Plan, Ground, Build parts, Combine, Audit, Render, Check, Fix, Re-check and Report. Two things differ from the design. The Ground phase was added on the critic's advice (the ground is built first, alone, and frozen before the other parts are seated on it). There is no paid Concept phase; the workflow accepts reference pictures in args instead.

How it behaves:
- The planner, the builders and the integrator carry the plugin's steps in their prompts: the part pass (`finish-part`), the construction check, the stage-file safety run (`combine` on the part alone), the whole pass (`finish`), then the audit and the preflight stage `place`.
- Nothing is drawn unless the audit passes. A helper's word 'pass' counts only when the preflight exit code is 0.
- At most two repair rounds happen before any picture, each routed to the owners the audit names. The design said both 'at most 2 rounds' and 'fails twice stops'; I used 2 repair rounds, so 3 audits at most.
- The renderer draws with the film owner's rule (Cycles where lit, EEVEE when not). Only the renderer may use the rented card, and only when args allow it.
- Four fresh checkers run: look, structure, process and a blind reader. None sees a builder report or number; they get the claims as bare sentences with measured results cut off.
- The blind reader's prompt is self-contained: it does not start 'First read <agent file>' like the others, and it holds no word of the feature list. The reading test is a keyword match counted by the script (line 0.75, the house number).
- A skeptic merges and ranks the findings.
- Exactly one fix round follows, one fixer per owner with only that owner's confirmed findings, then a recombine, a new audit, a redraw of the changed views, and a different checker plus a second blind reader.
- A final gate runs `explainer-film-preflight place` on the final file with the composed fresh-check object.
- A squint-test miss is reported to the person and never fixed by removing character. This is enforced twice: in the prompts, and in the script, which moves a confirmed squint finding to 'not fixed on purpose' when its cure is to remove detail.
- A part that returns nothing is listed as missing and not combined. More parts than the cap (default 4) wait in a queue.
- If no picture exists (stalled card or empty renderer), only the structure and process checkers run and there is no fix round.
- The plain-words report is composed by the script from structured data, so no failure can be left out.

Design choices you may want to change: builders never use the rented card (only the renderer does, to avoid several wake-ups), and the blind reader never reads the checker agent file.

smoke.summary: I built a 12 m brick canal lock side (near and far brick walls with stone coping, a stone step flight in a trench, a gravel towpath, a two-leaf wooden lock gate with balance beams, five props) using only the plugin's steps and kit. It took about ten rounds because the audit and the construction check kept finding real faults, some of them mine and some the kit's. The main flow works end to end: setup, parts built in a fixed order and combined, `finish` (28 s), `audit`, `preflight place` (PASS, 0 to fix, 2 to look at), an EEVEE 1200 x 800 picture here, a 1600 x 1067 close-up on the rented card (EEVEE per the renderer rule, plus a Cycles one), and every plugin test passes (with Blender: 37 files, 35 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped, 1405 checks; without Blender: 34 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped, 1250 checks). I mark the verification as NOT passed because of one blocking hole and several faults that would trap a newcomer. Blocking: a scene whose objects have no material at all (the way the plugin's own stage template builds) passes the audit and the place stage with zero normal maps, zero wear and zero weeds, once the four unrelated FAIL lines (bevels, shape damage, plain boxes, ground relief) are fixed by hand. Also found: `undo` crashes when the kit itself added the sun; `roads` rebuilt my towpath grid, filled the trench I had cut in it and silently moved the stair stones up 2 m, which the audit then reported as 'floats'; the ground-seat check fails walls beside higher ground for no real reason; the plain-box check fails stone, iron and crate objects that no verb will bevel; the picture stage fails every picture with a plain sky. The wear is visible but subtle in the hero picture (see 'does the picture show' in the evidence). Nothing was changed in the plugin folder; I wrote only in my scratch folder.
smoke.evidence:
WHAT I DID, in order, with results (all runs on this slow computer unless 'card').
1. Setup: `explainer-film-setup` into scratch: 4 s, 70 kit files named by the skills checked, 0 missing; it reported Blender 5.2.2, xvfb-run, and that no rented-card settings are set (yes/no only). The three bin commands are not on the PATH from a clone (the skills say 'once installed'); I put the plugin's bin first on PATH.
2. Followed skills/surfaces-wear-and-construction (SKILL.md, the-required-steps.md, construction-and-scale.md, a-forest-village-example.md, rendering-on-rented-cards.md, the kit README). Step 0: wrote style note, facts file (canal_facts.json), ownership table. Step 1-2: four owners (ground_and_water, walls_and_steps, lock_gate, props) as stage files from data/templates/stage_template.py; used pk.begin_part / new_part_object / seat_on_ground / ground_height_at (all exist). `combine`: ground alone first, then the other three in both orders: idempotent PASS, order PASS. `construction` before the pass: 88 of 88 carried (after I fixed my own gate joinery, see findings).
3. `new-settings --type harbour` drafted settings; I edited look lived_in, state damp, removed two preset skip groups, added a towpath road (rut 5 cm, hoof prints), footfall and keep-clear around the steps.
4. `finish`: 27-28 s each run. Final run: 94 objects, 16 roles, 16 materials, normal maps 1024 px on 94 objects, displacement on 4 objects, 33 bevelled by the kit, 70 objects bent/leaned/lumped by `damage`, nine wear layers in 15 materials, 66 plant pieces and 100 litter pieces, none on a wheel track, worn path or puddle. Audit rounds: round 1 FAIL (5), round 2 FAIL (2), round 3 FAIL (1), round 4 WARN (0 to fix, 1 look: grass has no displacement, wanted not required, 18 passed). `audit --facts canal_facts.json`: 46 sizes fit the facts. `explainer-film-preflight place --place-audit ... --blend ... --real-world-facts ...`: PASS, 0 to fix, 2 to look at (grass displacement; no fresh checker has looked). `normals-test`: 13 normal maps Non-Color, tangent, direction PASS (sun from +X 0.794 vs 0.415, flipped-green control reads the other way). `check-presets`: 6 of 6 groups.
5. Negative tests of the gate (my own scratch copies): (a) plain built scene, never finished: preflight exit 1 (4 FAIL, but only bevel, shape damage, plain boxes, ground relief; nothing about missing surfaces); (b) 9 objects given a flat plain material: audit FAIL 'missing normal_map, roughness_variation, colour_variation, dirt, grime, weathering, wetness, cracks_and_chips, edge_wear, moss_and_algae', preflight exit 1 (it named only role timber.plank for the shared material); (c) stale audit against a changed file: preflight FAIL 'scene file changed after the audit' exit 1; (d) LAZY scene, objects with no material at all: bevel modifiers by hand, then only `damage` and `roads`: audit 'PASS. 17 passed', '0 normal map(s)... PASS', preflight exit 0. That is the blocking hole.
6. Pictures. Hero 1200 x 800 EEVEE, 48 samples, `render --job ... --where local --finals --engine eevee`: 80 s (the verb draws a preview and a final, so 163 s in all; the first tiny draw took 72 s for shader build, later ones 7-14 s). Close-up on the rented card, using ONLY render_client_serverless.py: uploaded the kit bundle (1.17 MB), the 14.4 MB scene and the job file, ran exactly the command line the plugin's own client builds (blender -b ... blender_run.py -- render --job ... --where on-card --finals). Run 1 (first scene): COMPLETED, 32.1 s work, wake-up 14.7 s, EEVEE 1600 x 1067. Run 2 (final scene, two views in one job): COMPLETED, 49.5 s billed work, wake-up 0.9 s, EEVEE close-up 1600 x 1067 and Cycles close-up 1600 x 1067 at 96 samples in 3.7 s on OptiX (RTX 4090). No queue wait, no stall. The plugin's own `rent`/`render --where rented` was not used (it needs the person's settings, which I did not have); it stops with a clear sentence naming the missing settings (exit 2). All three pictures carry the same scene SHA-256 as the audited file (the audit's SHA-1 106968c1...). The sun and sky in the final pictures were added by the kit's `light` step (my first start scene had my own sun; the kit's version gave better contrast and shadows, so I used the no-light start scene for the final).
7. Tests: `python3 kit/calculators/tests/run_all.py`, with BLENDER set: 37 files, 35 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped (test_after_painting, test_sound_gates: need the project's recordings and plates), 1405 checks passed, 5 min 53 s. Without BLENDER: 34 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped, 1250 checks, 1 min 58 s. Skip reasons are in the logs. The tests wrote only to my scratch TMPDIR.
8. Privacy scan of the plugin: no keys, endpoint ids, e-mail or personal details; the only personal string is the author handle in plugin.json and the install line in README (both pre-existing from 1.3.0). Nothing new was written inside the plugin folder by me (checked by file times).
DOES THE PICTURE SHOW THE SEVEN THINGS (measured vs judged)? Normal maps: YES, clearly (judged by eye): brick courses and mortar, cracked flagstone pattern on the coping, wood grain on every gate board, gravel; measured: 13 maps wired Non-Color/tangent, normals-test direction 0.95-0.999 on every map. Displacement: PRESENT but faint (measured: displacement set on 4 objects, towpath relief and ruts found by the audit; judged: only the wavy gravel edge on the towpath shows in the hero; ruts are not readable at that distance). Dirt and grime: visible in the close-ups (dark streaks on boards and brick), faint in the hero; measured with the plugin's own master dial: tiny 480 x 320 pictures with wear on versus master 0 differ by 3.7 percent (hero) and 2.8 percent (close-up) mean pixel change, and 33 and 41 percent of pixels move by more than 8 of 255; judged side by side (picture 04): without wear bright orange brick and tan boards, with wear faded, silvered, grimy. Weeds: YES but sparse (66 plants plus tufts; tall thin blades on the towpath, tufts on the verges; none on the trodden strip, measured by the audit's keep-out count). Weathering: YES in the close-ups (judged; picture 04). Damage: YES as shape: crooked, uneven gate boards and a leaning leaf (70 objects bent or chipped, measured count), hairline brick cracks in the close-ups; coping chips are barely visible. Moss: only faint green marks on boards and brick in the Cycles close-up. Rust: reddish iron strap; the bollards read as clean blue paint. Rubbish/litter pieces and waterline staining: not visible by eye. Overall judged weaknesses: the water is a flat dark slab in EEVEE (no reflections); value range is compressed (luminance 1 percent 0.21 to 99 percent 0.65 in the hero; detail energy 1.4 against my style note's 3 to 9 target; `measure` reports numbers but gives no verdict without a guard); in Cycles on the card the same scene looks far better (reflective wet water, strong relief), so the renderer rule 'EEVEE when only a sun' gives the weakest picture exactly where water is present.
TIMES: setup 4 s; combine 1.6 s; finish 23-28 s; audit 6 s; preflight 0.2 s; normals-test 4.6 s; card work 32 s and 49.5 s billed (a price shown on the day is not a bill).

findings.problem: A scene whose objects have no material at all passes the audit and `preflight place`. The unfinished scene fails only on bevels, shape damage, plain boxes and ground relief; after I added bevel modifiers by hand and ran only `damage` and `roads`, the audit said 'PASS. 17 passed', '0 normal map(s) ... PASS' and the preflight exited 0, with zero materials, zero normal maps, zero dirt, grime, weathering, moss, rust and zero weeds. The material-level treatments are checked material by material, so no material means nothing to fail. The plugin's own stage template builds objects without materials.
findings.where: kit/calculators/place_audit_check.py (treatments by material) and kit/place-kit/place_kit/checks/scene_audit.py (per-object 'missing' lists only bevel and shape damage)
findings.fix: Per object: if a visible object has a role whose class requires normal_map, roughness/colour variation or wear and it has no material (or a plain one), put every missing treatment on that object and FAIL; also require plants/litter per ground role independent of materials. Add a test with a materialless scene.

findings.problem: `explainer-film-place undo` crashes on a scene where the kit itself added the sun and world: 'ReferenceError: StructRNA of type SunLight has been removed' (undo.py line 55, data.name read after the object was removed). On a scene where the sun was mine it worked ('11 objects, 17 materials ... removed, 2 ground meshes swapped back'). A newcomer who adds no light (the normal case) cannot undo.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/undo.py, undo_finish, around line 55
findings.fix: Read the datablock name before removing the object; add a test of undo after `light` added a sun (the existing undo test did not cover it).

findings.problem: `roads` replaced my towpath mesh (a 14 m by 2.4 m strip of 0.1 m squares, 3,108 faces) with its own uniform 0.12 m grid because is_coarse() estimates edge length as the longest side divided by the square root of the face count (0.2512 against 0.25), which misjudges long thin strips. The new grid filled the trench I had cut in the towpath for the steps, `finish` then 'seated again' 7-9 objects and moved the stair stones up 2 m without saying how far, and the audit reported 'Step 1 ... 8 parts float' although the construction check before `finish` had passed everything. Nothing in the output pointed at the cause.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/surfaces/ground_mesh.py is_coarse; surfaces/roads.py make_fine; parts.reseat_on_ground
findings.fix: Judge coarseness from the real mean edge (area per face), leave a fine enough mesh alone, keep holes when regridding (or refuse with a sentence naming the object), and print every object that is moved more than a few centimetres by a re-seat, with the distance. Add a test with a ground strip that has a hole.

findings.problem: The ground-seat part of the construction audit samples the raw bounding-box corners of a part. A wall that stands on the canal bed beside a higher towpath (any quay, canal or retaining wall) is reported 'not seated on the ground (-2.00 m)' when a corner touches the towpath edge, or lies a few millimetres outside the ground object (it reads 0.0 where there is no ground). Three parts failed this way after `damage` grew their boxes by 3 to 6 mm. The printed fix ('seat it again: pk.seat_on_ground, or run finish') changes nothing, because seat_on_ground itself samples points pulled inward and succeeds.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/checks/construction.py (ground_z from the box corners) against parts.seat_on_ground (points pulled in by 0.9)
findings.fix: Use the same footprint points in both; treat 'no ground under that point' as unknown, not 0.0; print which ground object and height it found; fix text should say 'your part's corner lies over another ground object'.

findings.problem: `surfaces` puts bevels only on roles that REQUIRE them (walls and timber), but the audit's plain-box check counts every object: stone coping, steps, trench walls, iron straps and a crate (all with bevel_metres in their surface recipe) stayed sharp boxes and the audit failed '49% of the objects are plain sharp-edged boxes (at most 15%)'. The fix text says to run `surfaces` and `damage`, which were already run; only chamfering the geometry myself (bmesh bevel) cleared it.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/surfaces/materials.py line ~235 (bevel only if bevelled_edges is required) and calculators/place_audit_check.py plain_boxes
findings.fix: Bevel every object whose surface has bevel_metres (or count only objects whose role requires a bevel); and make the fix text say 'chamfer the mesh yourself' when the verbs cannot.

findings.problem: The construction check calls correct joinery a failure. Gate rails tenoned 5 cm into both posts read 'hangs from above' (FAIL) for role timber.beam, because overlap-joined parts count only if their role may hang. A part sunk 6 mm into its carrier (my balance beam on the heel post top, 6 mm because the post had been seated on bumpy ground) is reported 'floats (gap 330 mm)': the touch tolerance is 5 mm and penetration is not tolerated; the number shown is the distance to the next thing below, not the 6 mm. I got out only by using role timber.fence for the rails (its name hints include rail and gate) and a flat bed.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/checks/construction.py (embedded versus rest contacts, touch tolerance); skills/surfaces-wear-and-construction/construction-and-scale.md
findings.fix: Say in the skill which roles may hang and that tenoned frames need one; treat a small penetration (say up to 4 cm) as resting and report the real overlap in millimetres.

findings.problem: A newcomer cannot find the role ids: SKILL.md gives only two examples and never points to data/roles.json (the only mention is about displacement); there is no `roles --list`. There is no role for steps: I used floor.stone, and every preset's skip entries for floor.* ('inside the buildings: dry, nothing grows') would have silently switched off moss, weathering, wetness, plants and litter on my outdoor steps (I only noticed because I read the drafted settings). The step-rise fact is matched by NAME: walls I named 'Step trench back wall' and 'Step trench cheek' failed 'height 2.0 m, step_rise 0.1-0.25', and a solid step block standing on the bed (height 1.83 m) fails the same fact; I had to rename and rebuild the steps as 0.17 m slabs stacked on a core.
findings.where: skills/surfaces-wear-and-construction/SKILL.md and the-required-steps.md; kit/place-kit/data/roles.json, data/place_types/*.json (floors_indoors), data/real_world_facts.json (step_rise)
findings.fix: Point to roles.json (or add `roles --list`) with a one-line meaning per role; add stone.step; limit the indoor skip to indoor floors; apply step_rise to a role, not a name pattern, and measure the top-to-top difference.

findings.problem: The place stage with pictures fails any picture with a plain sky: 'flat windows: 80 of 360 windows below the sky are dead flat ... give those surfaces normal maps' on my hero, where 76 of the 80 flat windows are the sky (rows y=0-144) because the sky mask only exists when an --id-map is given; the sentence 'below the sky' is false and the fix text sends the builder to surfaces that already have maps. The same guard compared with a second view (the close-up) failed value range, mean saturation and 'turquoise 4.37 percent (at most 0.3)' for dark teal water: a garden-specific taste rule in a generic gate. One guard serves all views.
findings.where: calculators/picture_measures.py flat_windows (sky_mask=None) and preflight place pictures check; film-settings.json place_measures.*
findings.fix: Exclude the top part of the frame or any sky-like flat block without an id map, or say plainly that an id map is needed; make the turquoise rule a per-place setting; allow one guard per view.

findings.problem: `combine --order both` fails ('idempotent' and 'order: plain and reverse order give different scenes') when the ground stage is in the list, because every other stage is seated on the ground. The skill says 'ground first' and 'combine in plain and in reverse order' but not how to do both; the way that works is to combine the ground alone into a frozen start file, then run the other stages with --order both from it.
findings.where: skills/surfaces-wear-and-construction/the-required-steps.md steps 1 and 4; kit/place-kit/README.md 'Building in parts'
findings.fix: Add the two-step recipe with the two commands.

findings.problem: Draft settings disagree with the skill: `new-settings --type harbour` writes look neglected and state wet, while the skill's table says 'nothing said -> lived_in' and 'otherwise dry'; a canal is not in the list of types (harbour was the nearest, `generic` exists but is not listed in the skill). `new-settings` prints one PASS line for each of the 94 objects (500 lines in a village). A drafted rut depth of 0.025 m failed 'ground relief at least 0.03 m' later; the draft gives no hint.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/data/place_types/harbour.json; SKILL.md choose-the-look table; commands.py new_settings output
findings.fix: Say in the skill that a type preset sets its own look and state and where to change them; list `generic`; summarise role lines (count per role); validate rut depth against the relief floor in `new-settings`.

findings.problem: The `light` verb treats a world background colour as 'the scene already has light' and adds no sun ('PASS light: the scene already has light (left as it is)'), even with --sun-only; a scene with only a world colour renders flat with no raking shadows, which hides the normal maps the pass is meant to show. Starting with no world and no lamp gave the kit's own sun (energy 3.5) and sky (0.8), which looked clearly better than my hand-made sun.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/light.py
findings.fix: Count only lamps as the scene's light for the sun decision (or let --sun-only force a sun), and say in the skill that a world colour alone leaves the scene without a key light.

findings.problem: `finish` without --save-as does the whole 23 s of work and only at the very end prints 'FAIL this verb changes the scene, so say where to save it'. The 'NEXT run:' line printed after the audit omits --reports, and `preflight` writes its reports to ./preflight-reports of the current folder (a model running it from the plugin folder litters the plugin; the workflow builder did exactly that once). The place's own facts file is accepted by `audit --facts` and `preflight --real-world-facts` (two names) but not by `finish`, whose verdict therefore ignores it.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/commands.py (finish), calculators/preflight.py (default reports folder), the audit's NEXT line
findings.fix: Check --save-as before starting; print --reports in the NEXT line; use one option name for the facts file everywhere.

findings.problem: Rendering instructions: rendering-on-rented-cards.md says the job file format is in place-kit/README.md, but it is only in the top note of place_kit/render/render_job.py. To get a local 1200 x 800 picture one must pass --finals and give width and height in the view; the verb then draws a preview and a final (twice the time, 163 s). `explainer-film-setup` says 'render --where on-card says what is missing' but on-card is the internal value; the user-facing one is --where rented.
