findings.where: skills/surfaces-wear-and-construction/rendering-on-rented-cards.md section 6; bin/explainer-film-setup; place_kit/render/render_job.py
findings.fix: Copy the job-file example into the README and the skill; fix the setup message; add a --size option or let a job ask for 'local, one size'; name files by view and kind once.

findings.problem: The tests prove the gates they cover, not the gaps found here: 1405 checks pass while materialless objects pass the audit, undo crashes after `light` added a sun, `roads` fills holes and misjudges thin strips, the seat check samples raw corners, and the plain-box and step-rise rules misfire on common builds (stone, steps, walls beside higher ground). Every fault above reproduces on a 94-object scene built in about 300 lines.
findings.where: kit/calculators/tests/ (test_place_blender.py, test_place_audit_check.py)

newcomers.plan:
PLAN: a small fishing harbour with a fish market, built in Blender for a film. Nothing is built here. This is the plan I would follow. I read only the plugin folder.

0. WHAT I READ FIRST (free)
README, then skill make-explainer-film with house-rules.md. Then surfaces-wear-and-construction: SKILL.md, the-required-steps.md, wear-recipes, surface-recipes, construction-and-scale, style-rule-and-measures, fresh-checkers, rendering-on-rented-cards, blender-5-traps. Then build-and-paint-a-place, make-3d-models with blender-mcp-notes.md, and the tips guide (kit/docs/LLM tips and tricks.md, sections 0, 1, 4, 7, 8, 8a, 9, 16, 19). Then kit/docs/paper-look - 07 Composing a shot.md.
The request says nothing about normals, displacement, dirt, grime, weeds, weathering or damage. The plugin treats that as normal. Any place built in Blender gets the surface-and-wear pass, the construction check and the preflight stage `place`, and I do it without being asked and without asking.

1. HOW THE WORDS BECOME SETTINGS
These are my own calls. I would log them in project-notes/Decisions.md next to the person's exact words, so any call can be overturned in one line.
- Place type is `harbour` (kit/place-kit/data/place_types/harbour.json).
- Look is `lived_in`. The request says nothing about condition, and the skill's table makes lived_in the default. The harbour preset's own default is `neglected`, so I deliberately do not take it. Per role: `neglected` for the piles, the waterline quay wall and the slipway; `kept` for the market's stone slabs, which are hosed daily; `lived_in` for the rest.
- State is `wet`, which is the preset's default (spray, hosed floor, damp stone). State is global, with no per-role state. So I check that roofs and upper walls do not read glossy in the first preview. If they do, I lower the wetness dial for those roles.
- Renderer follows the plugin's rule. If no lantern, lit window or fire is on, it is EEVEE under a virtual screen, free and local. If any are lit, it is Cycles, which needs the person's rented card and costs money. My default is daylight.
- No people in the first build. Far figures can be added later with build_figures.py under the people rules (backs to camera at 6 m or more, a crowd across the view).
- Route is the built-and-painted place, unless the film uses card models (a .glb in three.js).
I would ask the person only about wants or cost, and only if the film's script or shot list cannot answer. One short message: which words or page the harbour serves; daylight or dusk (dusk means lit lamps, a rented card and a cost); and whether they have a reference picture. Without one, the style note and style guard stay PROVISIONAL. Free steps start meanwhile. Nothing paid happens without their clear yes.

2. SET UP (once)
- Run `explainer-film-setup /path/to/work/film-kit` and read its checks: full Blender 5.2.2, Xvfb, Node 18+, Python with numpy, Pillow and OpenCV, ffmpeg, Chromium.
- Then `set -a; . ./machine-settings.env; set +a`.
- If Blender or Xvfb is missing, EEVEE cannot run, and I say so.
- Work folder: plan/, scene/, stages/, work/, reports/, render/, pictures/, checks/, plus project-notes/ (story, Decisions, Status, Lessons).
- Blender runs headless: `blender -b --disable-autoexec FILE.blend --python SCRIPT.py`, with `DISPLAY=:96` for EEVEE and `--python-exit-code 1`. Turn .blend1 backups off, run one heavy job at a time, stop if free disk falls under about 0.4 GB.
- Blender's own Python has numpy but no Pillow or OpenCV.
- The official Blender MCP server (make-3d-models, blender-mcp-notes.md) is used only to inspect a scene and look up the bundled API docs. Anything I build is saved to a file and audited as that file.

3. PLAN (agent place-planner, or by hand), written into plan/
a. style-note.md from templates/style_note.md.
 - Section 0, the style rule, stays word for word: wear is designed, few, big and clean, never photographic noise.
 - Palette: cool grey-green water and stone, warm silvered timber, ONE hot accent (red hulls and buoys).
 - Poly Haven scans read bland. So shape, normal maps and designed marks carry the place.
b. real-world-facts.json, with sources and confidence.
 - Researched on the web. A number from memory stays GUESS.
 - Covers quay height above water at mid tide, bollard and ring sizes, fish box and barrel sizes, boat length, beam and side height, market table height, roof pitch, door size, cart gauge, tide range.
 - The kit already has generic facts for doors (1.6 to 2.3 m), roof pitch (28 to 62 degrees), crates, barrels, posts, planks and tables. It has NO boat facts, so I add `^prop\.boat$` entries. Otherwise the scale check says nothing about boats.
c. A draft place-settings.json.
 - Run `explainer-film-place new-settings --scene SCENE.blend --place harbour --type harbour --out place-settings.json` once the ground exists. Read its list of what it could not classify.
 - Read the `off` entries it copies in. `floors_indoors` says "dry, nothing grows", which is false for the wet market floor, so I remove it there.
 - `quay_no_growth` (no plants or litter on stone paving) I leave out unless the first preview shows weeds look wrong on a salted quay. Weeds stay at wall feet, bollards and back joints.
 - The under-water seabed is a ground role, and ground roles require plants and litter, so it needs one honest off entry: "under water, nothing the picture shows grows or lies there".
 - Every off entry has a true reason of 15 letters or more. All together they stay under a quarter of the treatments (off_share_max 0.25, invented).
 - footfall and keep_clear cover the quay walking strip, market aisles, door steps, the slipway and the cart line. The audit counts roots there, and the count must be exactly 0.
 - Optional, my call: one short unmade approach lane up from the quay, set with `roads` (two ruts a cart gauge apart, hoof prints).
d. ownership.json (owners, frozen things, contracts) and acceptance.json.
e. Seven parts, each with one owner, a collection `Place: <owner>`, a region, a triangle budget and steps in priority order:
 1. ground_and_water: built first, then frozen.
 2. quay_and_pier.
 3. fish_market.
 4. sheds (net loft, store, a few cottages up the hill).
 5. boats.
 6. props.
 7. shore_backdrop (rocks, headland, grass, a few trees, far houses).
f. Three or more views, all portrait (film frame 1080 x 1920, plate 1536 x 2730 at 64.4 degrees), each with a camera `View <name>`:
 - `wide`: the whole harbour, stacked in depth with rope and boxes near, hall in the middle, boats and headland far. Mast and hoist tops must stay below 0.24 down, because typed words occupy 0.05 to 0.22.
 - `quay_eye`: eye 1.5 to 1.9 m above the quay, with the nearest story thing reaching 0.70 down.
 - `market`: the hall front with slabs, fish and the sign.
g. Sixteen readable features for the blind reading test (12 of 16 must be named from a half-size picture):
 1. wet cobbled quay with puddles
 2. quay wall with a weed band and a tide line
 3. piles with weed and rope wear
 4. rusted bollards and rings
 5. boats with chipped paint and a replaced plank
 6. boats grounded on mud or a cradle
 7. open-sided market hall with a mossy, sagging roof
 8. fish on slabs
 9. stacked fish boxes
 10. net drying on a frame
 11. barrels with rusted bands
 12. coiled rope
 13. lettered market sign
 14. drain channel on a wet floor
 15. lobster pots and baskets
 16. weeds in joints and at wall feet

4. BUILD (agent place-builder, one per part)
4.1 Free Poly Haven picks, adapting the pit-village scripts as patterns (fetch_street_textures.py, props/poly_haven_choices.py, download_poly_haven.py, convert_poly_haven.py; list in polyhaven_choices.json).
 - Surfaces: cobblestone_01 to 05, castle_wall_slates, clay_roof_tiles, clay_plaster, brick_moss_001, bark.
 - Models: Barrel_01/02/03, wine_barrel_01, wooden_crate_01/02, wicker_basket_01/02, wooden_bucket, wooden_ladder, Lantern_01.
 - I open every downloaded picture at full size and look for stickers, brands and digits. Requests carry a generic client name.
4.2 Script what the picks lack.
 - Missing: boats, nets, fish, rope, bollards, hoist, market slabs, lobster pots, floats, handcart.
 - Method: build_scripted_props.py, scripted_kit.py and prop_library.py as the pattern, with model_kit.py tools.
 - Technique: bevels with harden_normals plus Weighted Normal; rope as a beveled curve; Screw lathe for buoys, bollards and barrel bulge; cut then bevel; any geometry-nodes net ends in Realize Instances.
 - Lettering: the market sign and boat names go through paint_prop_pictures.py. lettering-sizes.json is written before the builder runs, with OFL fonts. Names are invented, never real people or brands. I check them with readability_test.py and make_sheet.py, and letters must be 20 px or more at phone size (view_audit.py).
4.3 Order.
 - Ground first, alone, then frozen: seabed below the water, foreshore, cobbled quay apron, slipway, the optional lane, the water plane at a fixed tide height, the view cameras, the world. Its promise to the others is stated: quay-top height, water level, slipway slope.
 - Then the other six parts side by side, at most 4 at once and 2 on a slow computer.
 - Each part is a stage file stage_<owner>.py with an idempotent apply(options), using pk.forget_part, begin_part, new_part_object, seat_on_ground, ground_height_at and is_keep_clear.
 - Every object gets an owner and a role as it is made. A part that finishes steps 1 and 2 is already a valid delivery.
 - Each builder trials with `finish-part --owner X --quick`, then runs `construction`, `normals-test` and `combine --order plain` (it must report idempotent), and draws one tiny picture.
4.4 Harbour construction, from the ground up and at real size.
 - Quay wall on a footing on the seabed.
 - Piles driven down to the seabed.
 - Stringers span 2.5 m or less. Deck planks rest on 2 or more supports with no free span over 1.38 m (judged), gaps 5 to 14 mm.
 - Bollards and rings fixed into the coping.
 - Hoist post on a footing.
 - Hall: footing, posts, tie beams, rafters, roof, gutters on brackets. Doorways have a floor within 0.30 m below the sill. Table legs stand on the floor.
 - Damage as shape: no two planks alike (9 to 17 cm), bowed boards, leaning piles, chipped coping, slipped tiles in different tones, a replaced hull plank, a torn net. The audit lists groups of exact copies.
4.5 A risk to test before the full build.
 - prop.boat must be carried from the ground. Water is exempt, but I have not seen how the check treats a hull resting on the water plane.
 - So I build one hull afloat and one grounded on mud or a cradle, run `construction`, and read the result.
 - Likely choice: a half-tide look with boats on the mud and cradles, plus one hauled out on the slip.
 - An afloat hull is used only if the check accepts it, or if the person signs an accepted entry (who and date). I never lower a requirement.
4.6 Roles. I name objects so the name hints catch them and write explicit rules for what the hints miss.
 - piles to timber.post
 - bollard, ring and cleat to iron.fitting
 - quay wall to wall.stone
 - nets to prop.rope
 - sails and tarps to prop.cloth
 - pots to prop.wicker
 - sea to water.sea
 - sky to never.sky
 - glow to never.glow
 - helpers to never.helper
 - There is NO fish role. I use the nearest (prop.generic), say so in the report, and do not edit plugin data.
4.7 Gaps the kit does not fill.
 - species.json has tufts, clover, nettle, fern, bramble, moss cushions, leaves, needles, sticks, straw and dung only. There is no seaweed, barnacle, shell, fish scrap or foam.
 - The props owner makes chunky designed pieces for these: weed hanks, rope offcuts, torn net bits, ice chips, foam shapes.
 - The tide line and waterline band come from moss_and_algae, the grime layer's damp band and normal maps.

5. COMBINE AND THE WHOLE PASS (agent place-integrator)
- Rebuild ground.blend if the ground changed.
- Run `explainer-film-place combine --scene GROUND.blend --stages ... --order plain --owners ownership.json --save-as COMBINED.blend`, then again with `--order reverse`. Both must be clean and idempotent, and every violation goes back to the owner that did it.
- Run `explainer-film-place finish --scene COMBINED.blend --settings place-settings.json --save-as FINISHED.blend`, never with --quick.
 - It runs roles, ground (reseating everything), surfaces (UVs, real normal maps, displacement only on roads, mud, thatch and rock ground, bevels), damage as shape, the wear layers in their fixed order (dirt and grime, wetness, cracks and edge wear, moss, rubbish) with rust on iron, growth with exact keep-outs, light, and picture size.
 - It then saves, reopens and audits.
- Read the whole output, including what it skipped.
- Run `explainer-film-place audit --scene FINISHED.blend --settings place-settings.json --out place-audit.json`.
- Run `explainer-film-preflight place --place-audit place-audit.json --blend FINISHED.blend --place-settings place-settings.json`. It must exit 0.
- Fix by category, with at most two repair rounds. The integrator edits settings, role tags and dials only. Geometry goes back to its owner.
- Never save the scene after the audit. If I do, I audit again, because the audit records the file's hash.
- Read `explainer-film-place normals-test` and `construction` myself.
- Budgets: triangles 6 million in all and 1.5 million per builder; scatter 400,000 pieces; a final draws in 90 s or less; card memory 12 GB. Over budget means instancing small things and cutting detail nobody sees.
- Order note: build-and-paint-a-place runs `place` before `shots`, and the-required-steps.md says `shots` first. I do the rough camera sums early with frame_geometry.py boxes and reach. Both gates must pass before any plate. I report the inconsistency.

6. LIGHT, RENDERER, PICTURES (agent place-renderer)
- `explainer-film-place renderer-for --scene FINISHED.blend` gives the renderer and why.
- `explainer-film-place light --scene FINISHED.blend` adds a sun, sky and fill when the scene has none. These are starting values, tuned by looking.
- EEVEE case: Xvfb at :96, shadow pool 1024 scaled to the picture, and a render log with no "Shadow buffer full" (checked with calculators/plan_lights.py render-log).
- Cycles case:
 - Needs the person's rented card, set up by them. Settings are read from the environment or a file outside any repository, never written down.
 - Run `rent status` and `rent balance`, and a tiny Cycles proof (it must say OptiX).
 - One job file for all views through `explainer-film-place render --job JOB.json --where auto`. Previews only, finals only if asked.
 - Stop if jobs wait over 5 minutes while workers sit idle.
 - Cost is an estimate (card about US$1.10 an hour, measured on one day; a bill once came out about 2.5 times the work seconds).
 - No card means tiny local Cycles previews, said plainly to be an unfair look.
- Portrait sizes, for example 540 x 960 previews (EEVEE about a minute) and 1536 x 2730 plates (EEVEE 6 to 11 minutes).
- Draw the first view under flat, side and wet light. A mark that vanishes under one light is not carrying the place.
- Then `explainer-film-place measure PICTURE --make-guard --out style-guard.json` (PROVISIONAL, and it locks in whatever that first picture was) and `explainer-film-place crops` at 100 percent and at phone size.
- Measured: value range, detail energy (below 10), flat windows, palette, squint (0.92 target). A squint miss is reported with the region that loses most. I never remove character to chase a number.

7. FRESH CHECKERS (agent place-checker, driven by workflow build-a-place)
- Checkers never see the builders' reports or numbers.
- look: pictures against the style note, with 100 percent crops.
- structure: its own ray and normal-map scripts on the saved file.
- process: money, disk, privacy, leftovers, stale audit.
- blind_reader: half-size pictures only, scored 12 of 16 against the features list.
- skeptic: merges and ranks, and puts anything whose only cure is removing character into "not fixed on purpose".
- Exactly one fix round, by the owners, on confirmed findings only. Then a DIFFERENT checker rechecks for new faults.
- The final gate is `explainer-film-preflight place` with --place-audit, --blend, --place-settings, --place-pictures, --style-guard, --fresh-check and --reports.
- I could run the whole of phases 3 to 7 through `/explainer-film:build-a-place`:
 - Args: plugin, kit, folder, request (word for word: "Build a small fishing harbour with a fish market in Blender for a film."), place, views, references, environment notes, today, maxParallelBuilders 2, effort medium, checkEffort high, finals false.
 - rented false until the person says yes.
 - It spends nothing and commits nothing.

8. FILM SIDE (only after the place passes, and each paid step only on a clear yes)
- `explainer-film-preflight shots` with the place facts (place_facts.py, plan_shot.py, view_audit.py, plan_lights.py plan, plan_effects.py wind for any smokehouse smoke).
- Compose each view with make_check_file.py and check-shot.sh. I fix problem 1 only and rerun, in the order camera, props, light.
- Plate, `plan_lights.py render-log`, then `paint_request.py request`, which checks, writes the prompts and prices them but never sends.
- `explainer-film-preflight plates`. Then ask ONCE with the exact cost, reading fal's live price first (4.8 cents a megapixel last read; about 44 cents per 2k repaint with a style picture), and `plan_budget.py cost` and `ledger`. A vague reply is not a yes.
- Paint the master view first and use it as the style picture. Then `after_painting.py check`, then `explainer-film-preflight paint`.
- Behind and state pictures only if the page needs them.
- Wet place: the painter template's words ("matte painted finish", "never puddles or reflections") strip wet ground. I change them for these views, or use --keep-wetness if `paint_request.py --help` shows it.
- Pages through build-cinema-page (one slide per shot, never a turn, camera_audit.py --built-set), then pages, critique and film stages.

9. HOW I WOULD CHECK AND REPORT
- Gates say pass or fail by exit code. Every FAIL, LOOK, PASS and KNOWN line is quoted with its measured number.
- Measured and judged are kept apart in every report.
- I look at contact sheets, 100 percent crops and phone-size crops with my own eyes.
- Critics, not tools, judge whether:
 - wear reads as designed and not photographic
 - boats read as boats and fish as fish
 - the harbour reads working and not deserted
 - a mark survives at phone size
 - a squint miss is acceptable
 - the period and story are right
- The paid steps need the person's own clear yes.
- The report to the person says what the pass did, what the audit measured, what I skipped and why, what I did not test, and every failure.
- Stop lines I keep:
 - nothing drawn, rendered or painted until `place` passes
 - no requirement lowered
 - no save after the audit
 - no key, id or personal detail written into any file
 - no commit unless asked

NOT TESTED OR LIKELY WEAK (to say plainly)
- The kit was only ever run on a hut and a yard, and the harbour preset is a first try.
- Water, a seabed and boats afloat have no tests.
- There are no seaweed, barnacle, foam or fish pieces in the kit.
- State cannot differ by role.
- Cycles with the kit is untested at village scale.
- The rented-card client is untested against a real endpoint.
- The blind reading test has never been run truly blind.
- The plugin ships no hook, so routing to these skills rests on their descriptions.
- The tests prove the gates work, not that a harbour looks good. Fresh checkers and the person's eyes judge that.

newcomers.plan:
SCOPE. The request is only "build a water mill by a river with its miller's yard in Blender for a film". I would build the place, finish it, audit it, draw previews and have it checked by fresh helpers. I would stop there. Painting the views, narration, pages and filming all cost money or are other steps. They happen only if the person says yes, after I quote the exact cost. I build nothing now. This plan comes only from reading the plugin folder. Where I say "I would check", that is a test I have not run.

0. DECISIONS I MAKE MYSELF (the request names no surfaces or wear, and the plugin requires them anyway)
- The skill surfaces-wear-and-construction is mandatory for any place built in Blender. Its first screen, the README, the master skill, the tips guide (sections 0, 8a, 19) and the skill descriptions all say so. So I load it first and never skip it.
- Place type. The kit has no mill preset. The nearest is `farm` (mud, tracks, carts, timber). The alternatives are `village` and `generic`. Both farm and village allow the one legitimate skip, "floors indoors".
- Look: the person said nothing about condition, so `lived_in` (a working mill). State: `damp` (river spray, shade). I would say so in the report and note that `neglected` or `derelict` is one word away. I would push wetness and moss up through settings `dials` for the water-side roles only. Dial names come from `data/dial_table.json`; a misspelt name is an error.
- Light and renderer. Daylight only (sun, sky, fill; no lit window or lantern) means EEVEE under a virtual screen. A lit window or lamp would flip the rule to Cycles on a rented card. That card is the person's account and costs money, so I would offer it as a dusk variant, not assume it.
- Views. The film is a phone frame (1080x1920), so cameras are portrait: `View wide`, `View wheel_close`, `View yard_lane`, `View bank`. Eye height is 1.5 to 1.9 m.
- Routing. I would use the workflow `build-a-place` (run as /explainer-film:build-a-place) if the Workflow tool exists. Args: plugin and kit paths, a work folder, the request word for word, place "water mill", the five parts below, the four views, an environment note (slow machine, small disk, no spending, rented card off until the person says yes), renderer auto, finals false, maxParallelBuilders 2 to 4, and today's date. If there is no Workflow tool, I do the same phases by hand. I spawn one helper per agent file (place-planner, place-builder, place-integrator, place-renderer, place-checker). Each helper is told to read its own agent file first.

1. SET UP (free)
- Run `explainer-film-setup WORK/film-kit`. It checks Blender, the virtual screen (Xvfb), numpy/Pillow/OpenCV and ffmpeg, and writes machine-settings.env. It only says yes or no about rented-card settings. I never read or write those values.
- Run `explainer-film-place --verbs` and `explainer-film-place check-presets` to confirm the kit's data is consistent. I stop and report if free disk is under about 0.4 GB.

2. PLAN (place-planner, or by hand from `kit/place-kit/data/templates/`)
Files go in WORK/plan: style-note.md, real-world-facts.json, place-settings.json, ownership.json and acceptance.json.
- style-note.md. Section 0 (the style rule) stays word for word. It is marked PROVISIONAL because there is no reference picture. The rule is few, big, clean, designed marks and no photographic noise.
- Facts table. One row per size: number, unit, kind, source, confidence. A remembered number is a GUESS until a real source (web research by the planner) confirms it. Rows needed:
  - waterwheel diameter, width, bucket count and axle thickness
  - wheel-pit clearance
  - launder (water trough) height and sluice width
  - weir crest height, river width and depth, leat width
  - millstone diameter and thickness
  - mill storey heights, doors and hoist door
  - cart gauge and cart height
  - sack size
- Settings.
  - place_type farm, look lived_in, state damp.
  - look_by_role gives the yard mud and tracks `neglected` (trodden).
  - Role rules: an explicit role per object by name (see trap 1).
  - `roads`: one cart track from the yard gate to the lane. Polyline, width about 3 m, gauge 1.2 to 1.5 m, rut depth about 6 to 8 cm, `hoof: true`. It stays on the yard side and never crosses the river.
  - `footfall`: door strips, plus lines down both wheel tracks and the middle hoof line.
  - `keep_clear`: doorsteps, wheel tracks, the wheel pit, sluice walkways and the water margin.
  - `off`: only "floors indoors", with its true reason.
  - picture: portrait.
- Features a stranger should name at half size (12 to 16, with keywords). They feed the blind reading test, which must name at least 12 of 16 (share 0.75).
  1. wheel with wet green lower buckets
  2. mossy stone wheel pit
  3. launder on trestle posts
  4. sluice gate with lifting pole
  5. stone weir with water over it
  6. river with rocks and bank mud
  7. reeds on the bank
  8. wheel ruts with puddles
  9. hoof prints
  10. rubble-stone ground storey under weatherboarded upper storeys
  11. roof with moss and slipped or missing tiles
  12. hoist door and beam
  13. stacked flour sacks
  14. barrels with rusty bands
  15. cart with spoked wheels
  16. leaning millstone
  17. woodpile and chopping block
  18. nettles and ferns at the wall feet
  19. leaves and logs
  I would trim this to the 16 the builders will really make and that show at half size.

3. PARTS AND OWNERS (one collection `Place: <owner>` each; the ground goes first, alone, then is frozen)
1. `river_and_ground` (FIRST).
   - A graded terrain, with the river channel, banks, millpond and leat hollows cut in as height.
   - Water surfaces at frozen levels, role `water.still`.
   - Yard ground (`ground.mud`, `ground.dirt_road`) and the cart track via `explainer-film-place roads`.
   - River bed (`ground.gravel`, `ground.rock`), far-bank forest floor and grass, and the four cameras.
   - Its written promises: water levels, bank lines and the yard slab height.
2. `mill_building`.
   - Stone footing, rubble-stone ground storey, timber-frame and weatherboard upper storeys, tiled roof with some slipped or missing, door and step, shutters, windows.
   - A hoist door and beam.
   - An opening and arch where the axle passes the wall.
   - Floors only if doors open (see trap 3).
3. `mill_works`.
   - Waterwheel, axle, stone bearing blocks and stone wheel pit.
   - Launder on trestle posts and sluice gate with lifting pole.
   - Stone weir and abutments, and tail-race arch.
4. `miller_yard`.
   - Wall or fence and gate, open cart shed, scripted cart (Poly Haven has no cart), sack stacks, barrels, buckets, crates and ladder.
   - Woodpile and chopping block, trough, spare millstone, handcart, a few straw and hay scraps.
5. `banks_and_trees`. Willows or alders and firs, stumps, a fallen log, rocks in the river, reeds, ferns, bramble and nettles. Everything stays off the tracks.

4. BUILD (each builder, in priority order, so a finished step 1 plus 2 is a valid delivery)
- Each builder writes `stage_<owner>.py` from `data/templates/stage_template.py`. It has an idempotent `apply(options)` that calls `pk.forget_part`, `pk.begin_part` and `pk.new_part_object(owner, role, name, mesh)`, then `pk.seat_on_ground`. The ground height comes from `pk.ground_height_at`.
- Build bottom-up at real sizes, so every part is carried: planks on supports, supports on the ground, nothing floating.
- Bevel hand-touched edges. Make no two siblings alike: planks of different width, a bow, chips, slipped tiles, posts a little out of plumb. This is damage as shape, and it is what reads at film size.
- Every object gets its owner and its role as it is made. Roles come from `data/roles.json`. A joined mesh with several materials gets one role per material (a barrel's wood and its iron bands).
- Props. Poly Haven (CC0, fetched at run time, never shipped) via `pit-village/props/download_poly_haven.py` and `convert_poly_haven.py`, using the picks in `poly_haven_choices.py` and `polyhaven_choices.json`:
  - Barrel_01/02, wooden bucket, crate, ladder
  - tree stump, dead tree trunk, fir tree
  - textures such as brown_mud, brown_mud_rocks_01, forrest_ground, cobblestone, clay_roof_tiles, bark_brown
  - Everything the picks list says is not found (a cart, a trough, a well, hay) is scripted with `scripted_kit.py` and `build_scripted_props.py`.
  - The mill-specific pieces (waterwheel, sluice, launder, weir, millstones, sack hoist) are scripted too.
  - Open every downloaded texture at full size and look for stickers, brands and digits.
  - Lint each model with `paper-film/blender/model_lint.py --prop`.
- Each builder's own checks, run on a copy of the frozen ground, all with `explainer-film-place` and `--quick` only for trials:
  - `finish-part --owner OWNER --quick --save-as part.blend`
  - `construction`
  - `normals-test`
  - `combine --stages stage_OWNER.py --order plain --owners ownership.json`, which must say idempotent and report no violations
- Reports are bare-sentence claims (no numbers in them), each naming the tool that measured it. They also list steps finished, failures and what was not tested.

TRAPS SPECIFIC TO A MILL (found by reading `roles.json`, `checks/scale.py` and the construction notes; I would confirm each by running the check)
1. Waterwheel role and name. The word "wheel" in an object name hints `prop.wheel`. That role is tied to the cart-wheel size (0.4 to 1.7 m) and to standing on the ground. A 3 to 5 m waterwheel would fail the scale check beyond 1.5 times the range (2.55 m). So I tag it explicitly at creation as `timber.generic`. That role has no span limit, no size fact, and is carried by a part. I name it "Waterwheel ...". I add the place's own fact `mill_wheel_diameter` with `applies_to_role` timber.generic and `applies_to_name` waterwheel, with its source. The axle, 0.35 to 0.5 m thick, is also `timber.generic`, because `timber.beam` allows only 0.04 to 0.4 m (it fails beyond 0.6 m). The axle rests on stone bearing blocks (`stone.footing`) through a patch of at least 16 cm2 within 8 mm. I would read the construction check's span line for the axle and fix it by geometry or role. I would never change the 1.38 m house number.
2. Spans. A `timber.beam` may span 2.5 m. A `timber.plank` or `timber.floor` may span 1.38 m. The launder needs trestle posts about every 1.3 m with bearers on top. A 6 m wide mill floor needs a row of posts and a summer beam.
3. Doorways. A door needs a floor within 0.30 m below its sill. The upper hoist door either stays shut or gets a real floor behind it. Interior floors skip moss, weathering, wetness and plants via the "floors indoors" `off` entry.
4. Water. The kit has only `water.still` and `water.sea`: a swell normal map, roughness 0.05 to 0.25, no displacement. `water.still` name hints include river and stream. There is no flowing-water or foam recipe. A planar swell map has no flow direction; I would check how it looks. Foam would be a few big designed white shapes made as geometry. I would test which role the `roles` verb accepts for them (try `water.still`, which needs only a normal map). I would tell the person plainly that foam is hand-made and not a kit feature.
5. River versus the ground pass. I would measure the channel depth by rays before and after `finish`. This checks the channel survives the road grading and the graded grid (the old surface height is kept).
6. Keep-out. Plants and rubbish must be exactly 0 on wheel tracks, doorsteps, puddles and crowns. Nothing in the gates mentions a river edge. I would read the audit's keep-out counts and a 100 percent crop of the bank. If plants stand in water, I add a `keep_clear` shape along the water margin.
7. Scale of the site. The kit was proven only on a hut and a 36 x 26 m yard, and never at village size. I keep the mill site to about 50 x 40 m and say that the mask and growth passes at this size are untested.

5. COMBINE, FINISH, AUDIT (nothing is drawn until the audit passes)
- `explainer-film-place combine --scene ground.blend --stages stage_*.py --order plain --owners ownership.json --save-as combined.blend`. Then the same with `--order reverse`. Both orders must give the same scene with no ownership violations.
- `explainer-film-place finish --scene combined.blend --settings place-settings.json --save-as finished.blend`. No `--quick`, because a quick result is refused as a final. It does the following in order:
  - roles
  - ground ruts and re-seating of every part
  - UVs, real normal maps (OpenGL, Non-Color, at least 1024 px) and displacement (dirt road, mud, thatch, rock ground, gravel, earth, stone; normal strength x 0.6 where displaced)
  - roughness and colour variation and bevels
  - damage as shape
  - the nine wear layers in fixed order: dirt and grime, wetness, cracks and edge wear, moss, rubbish, plus rust on iron
  - weeds, ferns, nettles, moss cushions, leaves, sticks, straw and dung as 3D pieces
  - light, save, reopen, audit
- `explainer-film-place audit --scene finished.blend --settings place-settings.json --facts real-world-facts.json --out place-audit.json`, then `explainer-film-preflight place --place-audit place-audit.json --blend finished.blend --place-settings place-settings.json --reports REPORTS`. It must exit 0.
- I read every FAIL, LOOK and KNOWN line. I fix by category, with at most two repair rounds routed to the owner of the named object. I never lower a requirement. A skip is allowed only as an `off` entry with a true reason of 15 letters or more, capped at a quarter, or an entry the person signs. I never write that entry for them.
- I do not save the scene again after the audit. If I must, I audit again (the audit holds the file's hash, and a changed file is reported stale).
- Budgets the audit holds: 6,000,000 triangles in all, 1,500,000 per builder, 400,000 scattered pieces, a final draw within 90 seconds, 12 GB of card memory. I instance small things if over.
- Extra checks: `explainer-film-place normals-test` (each map must agree with its height, and a flipped control must fail) and `explainer-film-place construction --out construction.json`. Both are read in full.

6. LIGHT, RENDERER, PICTURES (place-renderer)
- `explainer-film-place light --sun-only` if the scene has no light (a scene with no light draws black). `explainer-film-place renderer-for` prints EEVEE or Cycles and the reasons.
- `explainer-film-place render --job JOB.json` draws previews. A small EEVEE picture is the free path here; local pictures are capped small (about 480 x 320 at 8 samples) and are not a fair look. Bigger pictures need the person's rented card, which bills per second (about US$1.10 an hour, read 22 October). That is a paid step, so I quote an estimate and ask first.
- I check the render log for "Shadow buffer full" or "Could not allocate shadow atlas". Either means the picture cannot be judged.
- I look at every picture with the Read tool. I look at the first preview flat and from the side; a mark that vanishes under one light is not carrying the place. I also look at a phone-sized copy (about 300 px wide).
- `explainer-film-place measure PICTURE --make-guard --out style-guard.json` makes the style guard. It is PROVISIONAL, because it locks in the first picture. Then `measure ... --guard --previous` and `crops` give:
  - value range
  - detail energy
  - flat windows
  - palette
  - squint
  A squint miss is reported with the region that loses most. I never remove character to chase a number.

7. FRESH CHECKERS, ONE FIX ROUND, FINAL GATE
- Four checkers who did not build it and never see builder reports or numbers:
  - look (pictures against the style note)
  - structure (own rays, normal-map wiring, UV hygiene, leftover preview cameras)
  - process (money, seconds, privacy, disk, stale audit)
  - blind reader (half-size pictures named by number only, told nothing)
- A skeptic merges and ranks the findings. A squint miss or any "remove character" cure goes to the person.
- Exactly one fix round by owners, re-audit and redraw of the changed views. Then a different checker and a second blind reader look again.
- Final gate: `explainer-film-preflight place ... --place-pictures PICS --style-guard style-guard.json --fresh-check fresh-check.json`.

8. REPORT (plain words, house rules)
- What I did. What the audit measured, with numbers. What was measured versus only judged. What I skipped (`off` entries, quick runs). What I did not test. Every failure.
- Decisions for the person: the look and state I chose, the provisional guard, any squint miss, and the foam and flow limits.
- Things only a critic or the person's eyes can judge, per tips guide section 19:
  - whether the wheel and water read as a working mill
  - whether wear reads designed and not photographic
  - whether the ruts read as driven by carts
- Naming of delivered files: a two-digit number then plain words. I do not commit or push unless asked.

9. AFTER THE BUILD (only on the person's yes; I would not do it now)
- `explainer-film-preflight shots` (free) with place facts from `calculators/place_facts.py`, `plan_shot.py` and `view_audit.py`.
- Then `plates` (price and gate; the plates stage refuses a paid painting if the place audit fails), `paint`, pages and filming.

NOT TESTED BY THE PLUGIN, SAID PLAINLY
- A village-size scene.
- Cycles with the kit.
- The rented-card client against a real endpoint.
- A truly blind reading test.
- Any mill-specific sizes (all my numbers start as guesses).
- Whether a smaller model loads the skill by itself (the plugin ships no hook).
The tests prove the gates work, not that a mill looks good. Fresh checkers and the person's eyes judge that.

kit/place-kit (data/roles.json, surfaces.json, place_types/farm.json and village.json, looks, dial_table.json, real_world_facts.json, polyhaven_choices.json, templates/stage_template.py, templates/style_note.md, templates/part_brief.md, README.md, DEVIATIONS.md)

codeReview.summary: Not ready to close. All old and new tests pass, but I found 5 blocking faults when I ran the real commands on small scenes, plus 8 more to fix and several minor ones. I changed no plugin file. I found no key, id, email or person's name, no add-on code and no third-party code. The blocking faults hit the village request directly: curved lane strips are reshaped into rectangles, `finish-part` always exits 1, the ground part cannot create the cameras it is told to make, the rented-card client can print the endpoint id in one error, and the rented-card settings docs disagree with the code.
codeReview.evidence:
TESTS. Full run with Blender 5.2.2 set: 37 files, 35 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped, 1405 checks passed, 5 min 51 s. This matches the kit builder. Without BLENDER: 34 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped, 1250 checks passed, 2 min 33 s. The old test_preflight.py now passes 66 of 66 because the kit builder made it pass --free-disk-gb 40. A checksum of every plugin file before and after both runs was identical, and `git status` is identical. Nothing outside the plugin folder changed and japanese-courtyard is untouched. The only skip message about version is in test_place_skills.py: marketplace.json says 1.3.0 and plugin.json says 1.4.0.

PRIVACY AND LICENCES. Grep for emails, the author name, rpa_/sk-/ghp_ style keys, hex strings of 24 or more characters, ~/.runpod, the scratchpad paths and /home/user paths found nothing new. The only hits were older comments and examples, the author handle that was already in plugin.json and the README, and the provenance text inside film-settings.json. `explainer-film-place check-presets` passes 6 of 6. I compared the place kit, the calculators and the docs with the Astra add-on (3-line identical code windows: no overlap, 2-line: four generic lines) and with the Scenario skills (8-word windows: only generic Blender idioms). The only Scenario overlap is in make-3d-models/blender-mcp-notes.md and it was already there before this work. SOURCES-AND-LICENCES.md claims no third-party code and I found none. The `runpod` library is imported only on the card.

NAMES AND LINKS. I checked 190 `explainer-film-place VERB --option` strings and 42 `explainer-film-preflight STAGE --option` strings in every md, js, py and json file: all match the real parsers. The exceptions are deliberate bad fixtures and one option name written inside a sentence. Every `place_*` house-number key used exists in film-settings.json. Every role id in the docs exists in roles.json. Every `pk.` function in the docs is defined. Every file named in backticks resolves. plugin.json and all data JSON files parse. `settings.py check` reports 0 problems. Skill and agent front-matter descriptions are under 1024 characters. The workflow follows the Workflow tool rules (pure-literal meta, matching phase titles, no clock or random).

RUNS I MADE in scratch scenes, with Blender 5.2.2. The scratch folder is deleted.
- Small hut: `finish` passes in 9 s. `finish` twice gives the same counts. `preflight place` passes with one LOOK. A 191-object village finishes in 24 s.
- `finish-part` on the hut printed a FAIL for "quick output" and exited 1.
- A curved 160 m² lane strip lying on a ground slab came out as a 39,198-square grid over its whole 50 x 11 m box, with relief 0.0225 m against 0.08 m set. The audit failed it.
- A wall with scale -1 (and a roof on top of it) was reported "inside out", "twin faces flicker", and the roof "floats, gap 2400 mm".
- A sun lamp at the default position was reported "light inside a solid" by the `construction` verb.
- A red curve with bevel floating 3 m up, a text sign and a collection-instance prop all got PASS because only mesh objects are looked at.
- A scene with nothing in it crashed `finish` with "cannot convert float infinity to integer".
- The ground stage creating the view camera, as the workflow tells it to, gave "frozen camera settings changed" plus "new object has no place_owner".
- A lettered sign whose material has a picture (kept as is) failed the audit for roughness_variation, and re-running changes nothing.
- A 45-degree wall was silently not size-checked.
- An error message forced by a fake dead network contained the fake endpoint id.
- A JSON settings file written as the docs describe was read as "not set".
- A local `render` worked in 15 s and honestly failed a black picture.
- `combine --order both` with the shipped stage template passes.

findings.problem: Shaping a road destroys any lane that is a separate curved strip. `make_fine` replaces the ground object's mesh with a grid over its whole bounding box. In my test a 160 m² ribbon became a 39,198-square rectangle (50 x 11 m) lying on the forest floor. The measured rut relief was 0.0225 m against 0.08 m set, so the audit's ground-relief check fails (minimum 0.03 m) and re-running `roads` cannot fix it. `ground_objects_for` treats every `ground.*` object whose box meets the road box as ground. No doc says the lane must be part of one ground mesh, and no test covers a strip.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/surfaces/roads.py (make_fine, lines 104-150; ground_objects_for, line 92) and surfaces/ground_mesh.py regrade_object
findings.fix: Do not replace a non-rectangular ground object by its box grid. Subdivide it in place (subdivide, or a Subdivision modifier made real), or keep only grid squares inside the old outline. Or refuse with a plain LOOK: 'this ground object is not a rectangle; put the lane into the ground mesh'. Make the audit fail when a ground object's area grew more than 1.5 times. Add a curved-strip test. Say in SKILL.md and the builder and planner agents how a lane must be built.

findings.problem: `finish-part` always exits 1 and prints FAIL. It forces quick (`quick=True if not parsed.quick else True`), then `finish_place` audits with allow_quick left False. The judge fails 'place: quick output' and prints 'The place is not finished: do not draw...'. Every builder in the workflow is told to run `finish-part --quick` and read every FAIL, so each one sees a failure it cannot clear. Tests only check that it touches no object when the owner owns nothing, not its exit code.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/commands.py lines 212 and 376-381 (verb_finish_part, finish_place, run_audit_on_open_file)
findings.fix: Pass allow_quick=True when owner is set, so a part's audit gives a LOOK that says 'quick part pass; the integrator runs the full finish'. Replace the silly expression with quick=True. Add a test that a clean part exits 0. Fix the wording in SKILL.md and the-required-steps.md if a part ever ends with FAIL for another reason.

findings.problem: The documented ground-part flow fails the checker. The planner and builder agents and the workflow tell the ground part to make the view cameras, the lights, the world and the render settings, while also marking cameras, lights, world and render as frozen. `ownership.diff` raises 'the frozen camera settings changed' for any actor, including the ground owner, and a new camera without place_owner is a second violation. In my test the ground stage failed `combine` with 2 violations. The workflow then counts the combine as unclean and spends its repair rounds on it. No test covers the ground part creating a camera.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/checks/ownership.py line 75 (frozen loop) and the diff() added-object rule; agents/place-planner.md step 4; agents/place-builder.md lines 36 and 83-85; workflows/build-a-place.js groundBlock
findings.fix: Add a field to ownership.json, for example frozen.may_change_by: ['roads_and_ground'] or --ground-owner, and skip frozen violations for that actor. Treat cameras and lights as owned by the actor that made them, or exempt objects named 'View ...' from the owner rule. Make the planner write that field, and add a test of the ground stage making a camera.

findings.problem: The rented-card client can print the endpoint id. `WebTransport._send` raises 'no answer from the rented-card service for {method} {url.split("/v2/")[-1][:40]}' without scrubbing. That text starts with the endpoint id, and `main_command` and `render_command` print it to stdout. Tested with a fake dead network: the fake id appears in the message. The module note promises 'never prints a key or an endpoint id'. A model will paste such a line into a report.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/render/client.py line 151 (also check lines 143-149 and every f-string with a URL)
findings.fix: Never put the part of the URL after /v2/ into an error. Name only the action ('GET /health'). Pass every RentFailed message through settings.scrub before printing. Add a test with a fake endpoint and a dead network that asserts the id is not in the output.

findings.problem: The rented-card settings docs disagree with the code. The docs say `RENDER_SETTINGS_FILE` names a JSON file `{"api_key", "endpoint_id", "store_folder"}` and that the default store folder is `explainer-film-places`. The client reads only NAME=VALUE lines (RUNPOD_API_KEY=...) and its default store folder is /workspace. I wrote a JSON file as the docs say and the client reported both settings missing. The client's own error message and the setup script say NAME=VALUE, so a person following the README cannot use a rented card.
findings.where: README.md lines 25-26; skills/surfaces-wear-and-construction/rendering-on-rented-cards.md lines 47-51; code in kit/place-kit/place_kit/render/client.py read_settings_file lines 15-35 and 70-130
findings.fix: Change the README and the guide to NAME=VALUE lines and the default /workspace, or teach the client to read the JSON form too. Then add a test that reads the example the docs show.

findings.problem: The workflow and renderer agent say previews are drawn on the rented card ('the three previews ... are drawn with Cycles on the rented card in one job'), but they run `render --where auto` without --finals. `choose_where` sends auto without finals to the local computer, which keeps pictures tiny (480x320 at 8 samples EEVEE, 320x240 at 16 samples Cycles). The look checker and the blind reader then get half-size copies of those, so the reading test (12 of 16 features) is unlikely to pass and the Cycles rule is not met. The skills table also says 'previews on a rented card'.
findings.where: workflows/build-a-place.js renderPrompt and line 76 (WHERE); agents/place-renderer.md section 3; kit/place-kit/place_kit/render/client.py choose_where (line 279); skills/build-and-paint-a-place/SKILL.md tool table
findings.fix: When the settings are complete and the renderer rule says Cycles, make auto send previews to the card as well, with a LOOK saying so. Or make the workflow pass --where rented when `rent status` shows workers can start. Align the docs with what is done.

findings.problem: A plain request never gets its road ruts. `finish` drafts settings with `roads: []` and prints 'PASS roads: no roads in the settings (nothing to shape)'. An object with role ground.dirt_road is not turned into a road entry. The audit's ground-relief and gauge checks only run for roads in the settings, so a village lane with no ruts and no hoof prints passed (one LOOK). That is the headline of the village request, and the REQUIRED block makes drafted settings the normal route. `finish` also takes no `--type`, so the place-type preset is only used when `new-settings --type` is run first.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/settings_file.py line 285 (draft); kit/place-kit/place_kit/cli.py (finish options); kit/calculators/place_audit_check.py ground_relief; skills/surfaces-wear-and-construction/SKILL.md REQUIRED step 2
findings.fix: Let `draft` make a roads entry for each object whose role is a road role (centre line from the long axis or skeleton, width from the short axis). Add `--type` and `--place` to `finish`. Make the audit fail (or LOOK loudly) when a road-role object has no road entry and no measured relief. Put a line in the REQUIRED block telling the model to write roads.

findings.problem: The audit and the whole pass see only MESH objects. A curve with bevel (rope, wire, thatch), text, surfaces, metaballs and empties that instance a collection are ignored. Test: a plain red bevelled curve floating 3 m up, a text sign and an instanced prop box gave 'PASS 17' with '22 objects'. A smaller model that builds fences or ropes from curves, or props by instancing, escapes every treatment.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/scene_read.py lines 16 and 29-33 (OBJECT_TYPES_WITH_SURFACE, mesh_objects); kit/place-kit/place_kit/checks/scene_audit.py
findings.fix: Count renderable non-mesh objects in the audit and make the judge FAIL them by name ('convert to mesh or give a never role'). Better, convert curve, text and metaball objects to meshes at the start of `finish`, and realize collection instances (or audit their source objects).

findings.problem: The construction check gives false FAILs for mirrored objects. Object matrix_world with a negative determinant is applied to the vertices but not to the triangle winding. Test: a wall with scale -1 on x was 'inside out', 'twin faces flicker', and a roof resting exactly on top 'floats (gap 2400 mm)'. A non-mirrored copy passes. The suggested fix ('flip the normals') is wrong for this case. Mirroring a window or one side of a cottage is common.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/checks/construction.py lines 100-104 (world vertices and triangles for a part) and 161-166 (signed_volume_and_closed); also the upward-face tests in rest_patch
findings.fix: When np.linalg.det(matrix[:3,:3]) < 0, swap two columns of every triangle (flip the winding) when building the part. Add a test with a mirrored wall under a roof.

findings.problem: The standalone `construction` verb (a REQUIRED step in every builder prompt) fails any sun, area or other lamp whose position is inside or below a solid, for example Blender's default sun at the origin below a graded ground. A sun has no position that matters. The audit ignores lights, so the two commands disagree. Test: 'FAIL sun: light inside a solid'.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/checks/construction.py line 403 (lamp loop) and commands.py verb_construction
findings.fix: Skip lamp.data.type == 'SUN' (and the kit's own PK sun). Judge point, spot and area lamps only. Make the audit and the verb use the same list.

findings.problem: A material that carries its own picture (a lettered sign, a downloaded prop) is 'kept' by `surfaces`, so it gets no normal map and no roughness variation. The module note says kept materials 'only get what they lack later', but nothing does that. The audit then FAILs it for roughness_variation, and every re-run gives the same FAIL. The fix text says to re-run, which cannot work. Only an off entry clears it.
findings.where: kit/place-kit/place_kit/surfaces/materials.py lines 6 and 218-222 (the `if not should_replace(...)` branch); kit/place-kit/place_kit/checks/material_inspect.py line 160
findings.fix: Add roughness variation (and a normal map where a UV exists) to kept materials without changing their picture, or exempt them with an automatic off entry whose reason says 'kept: carries its own maps'. List the kept materials by name in a LOOK line. Add a test with a lettered sign.

findings.problem: The `plates` stage asks for the place audit only when a scene is named (`--blend`, or a `scene_file` stamped in the check file).
